Position: Junior Technical Assistant (Livestock/ veterinary)
Department: Program
Project/Program: Sabal Balika Sabal Samudaya (SaBaSS) Project
Reports to: Enterprises Development Coordinator
Duty station: KIDS Central Office, Taulihawa, Kapilvastu, Lumbini Province
Employment Type: Full-time

About the Organization

Kapilvastu Integrated Development Services (KIDS) is a non-governmental, non- profit, and non-political organization established on 31 August 2005 in Kapilvastu District, Nepal. The organization is duly registered with the District Administration Office and affiliated with the Social Welfare Council (SWC) since 20 March 2007.

KIDS was founded by committed community members with the vision of fostering a Healthy, inclusive and prosperous society with full of peace and equal justice. Since its establishment, the organization has worked to improve the quality of life of vulnerable and marginalized communities through inclusive, community-driven, and sustainable development interventions.

KIDS implements development and humanitarian programs across Lumbini Province in partnership with government agencies, national and international NGOs, UN agencies, donor organizations, and local communities. Its core thematic areas include Health, Nutrition, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Food Security and Livelihoods, Climate Change Adaptation, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Child Protection, Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Education, and Community Empowerment.

The organization is committed to maintaining the highest standards of good governance, transparency, accountability, safeguarding, financial stewardship, and compliance with the Government of Nepal’s legal and regulatory framework, donor requirements, and internationally recognized humanitarian and development principles. KIDS promotes integrity, ethical conduct, gender equality, inclusion, environmental responsibility, and a culture of continuous learning and organizational excellence in all aspects of its work.

The Junior Technical Assistant (Livestock/ veterinary) will provide field-level technical

Job Summary

support to livestock farmers and entrepreneurs under the SaBaS Project. The position will promote livestock farming practices and support enterprise development through regular technical guidance, training, monitoring, and coordination with local stakeholders. This
reflects the typical role of JTAs in Nepal’s livestock and livelihood projects.

Primary Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

  •  Conduct regular field visits to monitor the health and condition of livestock and poultry.
  •  Provide basic veterinary first aid and technical support within the scope of VJTA responsibilities.
  •  Identify common signs and symptoms of livestock and poultry diseases and provide appropriate technical advice.
  •  Support disease prevention, control, and management activities.
  •  Assist in vaccination, deworming, parasite control, and other animal health campaigns as authorized.
  •  Maintain proper records of animal health services provided.
  •  Identify complicated or emergency cases and refer them to a qualified veterinarian or appropriate veterinary service provider.
  •  Provide technical advice to farmers on scientific livestock management practices.
  •  Promote improved cattle, buffalo and goat management practices.
  •  Support farmers in improving animal housing, sanitation, hygiene and biosecurity.
  •  Provide technical guidance on breeding, reproduction and general livestock management.
  •  Coordinate with livestock section on palika level or ward level.
  •  Coordinate with supervisor for taken proper guidelines and support.

Qualifications, Experience, Knowledge, and Skills

Qualifications and Experience

  •  Diploma/JTA/ TSLC in Livestock/ veterinary science from a recognized institution.
  •  2 years of relevant work experience in livestock, animal health, veterinary services, farmer mobilization, or community-based livestock programs.
  •  Good knowledge of livestock health, disease prevention, vaccination, deworming, animal nutrition, breeding, husbandry and basic veterinary practices.
  •  Field experience: Experience working directly with farmers, livestock groups and rural communities will be an advantage.
  • Strong communication and facilitation skills in Nepali; knowledge of local languages is an advantage.
  •  Valid two-wheeler driving license with willingness to travel extensively within Kapilvastu is preferred.

Application Instructions:

Interested candidates are requested to apply via email with a recently updated CV and cover letter by 12th August 2026 to: procurement.kids@gmail.com

More information: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/17ATa3uulyEtqbujjdzn6AQswmkZC2Vo5?usp=sharing

UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence.

At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling.

UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package.

Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF.

For every child, the right to Results

How can you make a difference?

Join our dynamic Janakpur field office team to provide technical, operational and administrative assistance throughout the WASH programming process across Madhesh province (or the provinces covered by Janakpur Field Office). You will prepare, manage and implement a variety of technical and administrative tasks, related to the development, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of the WASH output results from the field office coverage that largely contributes to the Nepal country programme.

You will also provide technical assistance to provincial and local governments and implementing partners to strengthen WASH systems, institutional capacity, and safely managed and climate-resilient service delivery. The role also contributes to humanitarian preparedness and response, particularly in drought/ flood-prone areas, while promoting evidence-based programming, cross-sectoral collaboration, and equitable access to sustainable WASH services.

Within the Janakpur Field Office, these functions are undertaken with a strong focus on strengthening WASH systems and decentralized service delivery by supporting provincial and local governments in planning, implementation, monitoring, and capacity development. The role contributes to improving governance, institutional capacity, evidence-based planning, and climate-resilient WASH services, while promoting equitable access to water, sanitation and hygiene in communities, schools, and healthcare facilities. It also supports preparedness and response to recurrent floods, droughts and other emergencies in Madhesh Province.

1. Programme development and planning
2. Programme management, monitoring and delivery of results
3. Technical and operational support for programme implementation
4. Humanitarian WASH preparedness and response
5. Networking and partnership building
6. Innovation, knowledge management and capacity building

To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have…

Desirables

For every Child, you demonstrate…

UNICEF’s Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values

UNICEF competencies required for this post are…

(1) Builds and maintains partnerships

Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and its different levels.

UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status.

UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage Accessibility | UNICEF. Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance.

UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities. UNICEF is committed to promote the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially.

UNICEF appointments are subject to medical clearance. Issuance of a visa by the host country of the duty station is required for IP positions and will be facilitated by UNICEF. Appointments are conditional on the selected candidates’ willingness to comply with current or future vaccination requirements, should UNICEF mandate it for personnel. Failure to comply with such requirements, where applicable and without a duly approved medical exemption from the relevant UN authority, will result in the cancellation of the selection or may lead to other administrative measures, including separation from service.

Remarks:

As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity.

UNICEF is committed to fostering an inclusive, representative, and welcoming workforce. For this position, eligible and suitable female are encouraged to apply.

Government employees who are considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF reserves the right to withdraw an offer of appointment, without compensation, if a visa or medical clearance is not obtained, or necessary inoculation requirements are not met, within a reasonable period for any reason.

UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants’ bank account information.

Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF’s Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to stay and deliver in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities.

Visa residence requirements: i.e. UNICEF shall not facilitate the issuance of a visa and working authorization for candidates under consideration for positions at the national officer and general service category.

All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates.

Posiiton: Children’s Home Associate
Location: Surkhet, Karnali

“A world where every child is safe, educated, loved”- Kopila Valley Sewa Samaj is a non-profitable NGO registered in Surkhet, Nepal to provide support for children and families in our community. Our mission is to change the world by empowering Nepal’s children. KVSS programs include a residential children’s home, Kopila Valley School (KVS) for inclusive quality education, women’s empowerment, sustainability, health and wellness, and family development programs. We provide our students with free education, educational materials, health treatment and medicine, counseling, and a place to live. With our innovative future program, we strive to provide our children with career guidance, and scholarships for further studies. Our children’s home provides a safe, loving, and stable home for children in extreme cases of need, when all other options have been exhausted. We do this with our funding partner BlinkNow Foundation and in close ties with the local government and communities.

Position Summary-

The Staff working at KVSS should have patient and passionate about working with children will thrive as childcare. Should be enthusiastic about the growth and well-being of Children, sensitive to their needs, able to mix, relax and interact socially with children and be linked and respected by Children. The Children Home Associate at Children’s Home is responsible for the care, wellbeing, and upbringing of the children living within the KV Children’s Home. Your role is to provide basic parental, pastoral, and holistic care to provide the children with the brightest future possible. It is also your responsibility to manage and coordinate with all the other staff members working within the KV Children’s Home, and make sure that all caregiving roles are running as smoothly as possible.

The Employee will be required to perform the following duties and undertake the following responsibilities in a professional manner.

Job Description

The Main Responsibilities

  • Make sure that the children at KV Children’s Home are cared for and supported in the best way possible.
  • Support to manage caregivers and other support team members.
  • Assist in enrichment activities of the children.

Detailed Responsibilities

1.Make sure that the children at Kopila Valley Children’s Home are cared for and supported in the best possible way.

  • Create and update routines for the activities of children in Kopila Valley Children Home, and make sure that they are followed properly.
  • Lead daily gathering (sutsang) for children after dinner.
  • Manage activities that are designed to promote physical, mental, and social development of children.
  • Support children in their education- ensure that they study for an appropriate period regularly, and manage interactive activities and support children to learn, grow and feel proud.
  • Support children to make sure that they are done with all the chores that they are supposed to do before school
  • Performing regular check-in with the children in a one-to-one format in order to provide support and engage their needs.

2.Support to manage caregivers and other support team members.

  • Supervise the work of caregivers at the children’s home daily and provide continued feedback for any improvements required to improve services.
  • Coordinate with the admin team in regards to any necessary items for children.
  • Demonstrate discipline from personal behavior, initiate it for the team to demonstrate, and encourage it to flow from the team to the children.
  • Support caregivers to address any obstacles or challenges they may face.
  • Evaluate the performance of the home caregivers and support them in their professional development.
  • Coordinate with relevant team members to run all other children’s home functions smoothly.

3.Assist in Academic and non academic activities of the Children

  • Support children during their home works and study time.
  • Assist in non academic activities as planned by the Enrichment coordinator.
  • Prepare engagement activities independently during their free time with the support of caregivers.
  • Ensure that children’s study time tables are duly followed as per the time table.

Additional expectations

  • Take ownership of change and engage and encourage innovation.
  • Build positive working relationships and environment in the organization by bringing solutions to the discussion table.
  • Report to the manager on a weekly basis, and as needed in case of urgent activities.
  • Build and maintain a strong relationship with the children, staff and relevant stakeholders.
  • Attend weekly staff meetings and share operational updates.
  • Always maintain integrity and confidentiality.
  • The above list of responsibilities is not comprehensive, and candidates may be required to take on additional responsibilities, as determined by your supervisor.

Must Have

  • Education: +2 in Social science or any discipline.
  • Experience: At least 3 years of proven experience in a residential care or child protection field
  • Language: A good communicator, fluent in Nepali and basic in English
  • Skills and Abilities: Ability to manage, mentor and lead children, youth, their activities
  • Passionate about and cares for children and vulnerable population; initiator, and competent in managing caregivers, children and basic operations.
  • Works collaboratively and independently with the least supervision required.

Note: This is a residential and immersive role where the Children Home Associate needs to be hands on caregiving as well. Preferred Female.

Key Characteristics

  • You believe that we can change the world, in the blink of an eye
  • You believe in making decisions that put children first
  • You are self-motivated, organized, and approachable
  • You enjoy creating systems, keeping records, and increasing efficiency
  • You are always looking for new ways for our team to work smarter instead of harder
  • You are detail-oriented and conscientious. You make sure nothing slips through the cracks
  • You have a strong work ethic and a willingness to pick up new skills. You are comfortable multi-tasking
  • You are positive, patient, and a clear communicator who is comfortable working with both Kopila Valley staff in Nepal and the BlinkNow staff in the United States
  • You are an empathetic person, with a knack for putting out fires before they start and soothing conflicts brewing beneath the surface
  • You require little supervision and are flexible. You understand that you will be wearing many hats in this role, many of which are not explicitly included in this job description

Application Procedure

If you think this career opportunity will amplify your career growth, we encourage you to apply by clicking “Apply for this Job” and submit all required document. Only shortlisted candidates will be called for further screening process. No telephone inquiries will be entertained. We accept and screen applications on a rolling basis.

Kapilvastu Integrated Development Services (KIDS) is a non-governmental, non- profit, and non-political organization established on 31 August 2005 in Kapilvastu District, Nepal. The organization is duly registered with the District Administration
Office and affiliated with the Social Welfare Council (SWC) since 20 March 2007.

KIDS was founded by committed community members with the vision of fostering an equitable, healthy, resilient, and self-reliant society. Since its establishment, the organization has worked to improve the quality of life of vulnerable and marginalized
communities through inclusive, community-driven, and sustainable development interventions.

KIDS implement development and humanitarian programs across Lumbini Province in partnership with government agencies, national and international NGOs, UN agencies, donor organizations, and local communities. Its core thematic areas include Health,
Nutrition, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Food Security and Livelihoods, Climate Change Adaptation, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Child Protection, Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Education, and Community Empowerment.

The organization is committed to maintaining the highest standards of good governance, transparency, accountability, safeguarding, financial stewardship, and compliance with the Government of Nepal’s legal and regulatory framework, donor requirements, and internationally recognized humanitarian and development principles. KIDS promote integrity, ethical conduct, gender equality, inclusion, environmental responsibility, and a culture of continuous learning and organizational excellence in all aspects of its work.

Job Summary

The Procurement & Logistics Officer is responsible for supporting the efficient planning, implementation, and monitoring of procurement, logistics, inventory, asset management, and fleet operations for organizational and project activities. The position
ensures that all procurement and logistics processes are conducted in compliance with the policies and procedures of Kapilvastu Integrated Development Services (KIDS), donor requirements, and the applicable laws and regulations of the Government of Nepal.

The Procurement & Logistics Officer coordinates the procurement of goods, works, and services through transparent, competitive, and value-for-money processes. The position is responsible for maintaining procurement documentation, managing supplier relationships, coordinating logistics arrangements, monitoring inventory and fixed assets, and ensuringthe timely delivery of supplies to support effective project implementation.

Working under the direct supervision of the Administration & Finance Manager/Senior Administration & Finance Officer (or designated supervisor), the Procurement & Logistics Officer collaborates closely with programme, finance,
administration, and field teams to ensure that procurement and logistics services are responsive to operational needs and donor compliance requirements. The position is expected to maintain high standards of integrity, accountability, confidentiality, and professionalism while contributing to efficient resource management, operational excellence, and the achievement of organizational objectives.

Primary Responsibilities

A. Procurement Management

  • Implement procurement activities in accordance with the organization’s Procurement Policy, donor regulations, and the applicable laws and regulations of the Government of Nepal.
  • Prepare and update procurement plans in coordination with project and support teams.
  • Receive, review, and process approved procurement requests ensuring completeness and budget availability.
  • Obtain quotations, conduct market surveys, and prepare comparative bid analysis to ensure competitive and value-for-money procurement.
  • Prepare Requests for Quotation (RFQs), purchase orders, purchase agreements, and other procurement documentation.
  • Coordinate bid opening, quotation evaluation, supplier selection, and procurement committee meetings as required.
  • Ensure procurement processes are transparent, fair, and properly documented.
  • Follow up with suppliers to ensure timely delivery of goods and services according to agreed specifications and delivery schedules.
  • Maintain procurement records and filing systems in both hard-copy and electronic formats.
  • Assist in preparing procurement reports and procurement status updates.

Logistics Management

  •  Coordinate the transportation, delivery, receipt, and distribution of project materials, equipment, and
    supplies.
  • Arrange logistics for meetings, workshops, training programs, field visits, and project events.
  • Ensure timely delivery of procurement items to project sites and end users.
  • Coordinate transportation arrangements for staff, consultants, visitors, and project activities as required.
  • Monitor delivery schedules and resolve logistics issues to minimize delays.

C. Inventory and Asset Management

  •  Maintain updated inventory records for office supplies, equipment, and project assets.
  •  Receive, inspect, record, and issue materials in accordance with organizational procedures.
  •  Conduct periodic physical stock counts and reconcile inventory records.
  •  Maintain an updated fixed asset register and ensure all assets are properly tagged.
  •  Report damaged, obsolete, or missing assets to the supervisor and support disposal processes in accordance with organizational policies.
  •  Ensure safe storage and proper handling of inventory and organizational assets.

D. Fleet and Office Support

  •  Maintain vehicle logbooks and monitor vehicle utilization, fuel consumption, servicing, insurance, and registration.
  •  Coordinate routine maintenance and repairs of vehicles and office equipment.
  •  Monitor office supplies and initiate procurement requests to maintain adequate stock levels.
  •  Support office administration by coordinating courier services, mail, office maintenance, and utility services when required.

E. Vendor and Contract Management

  •  Maintain an updated database of approved suppliers, contractors, and service providers.
  •  Assist in evaluating supplier performance and maintaining supplier records.
  • Monitor supplier deliveries and contract performance to ensure compliance with agreed terms and conditions.
  •  Coordinate with vendors to resolve delivery, quality, or service-related issues.

F. Compliance, Documentation, and Reporting

  •  Ensure procurement and logistics activities comply with organizational policies, donor requirements, and Government of Nepal regulations.
  •  Maintain complete procurement, logistics, inventory, and asset documentation for audit and donor review.
  •  Support internal audits, external audits, and donor monitoring visits by providing required documentation.
  •  Prepare monthly procurement, logistics, and inventory reports for management.
  •  Ensure proper filing and record retention in accordance with organizational and donor requirements.

G. Coordination and Communication

  •  Coordinate closely with Finance, Administration, and Program teams to ensure timely procurement and logistical support for project implementation.
  •  Liaise with suppliers, transport providers, government offices, and service providers regarding procurement and logistics matters.
  •  Participate in procurement committee meetings and provide administrative support as assigned.
  •  Communicate procurement progress and delivery status to relevant staff on a regular basis.

H. Safeguarding, Ethics, and Organizational Compliance

  • Comply with the organization’s Code of Conduct, Procurement Policy, Safeguarding Policy, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) Policy, Anti-Fraud and Anti-Corruption Policy, and other
    organizational policies.
  • Promote transparency, accountability, fairness, confidentiality, and value for money in all procurement and logistics activities.
  • Ensure all work is carried out with integrity and in accordance with donor requirements and organizational standards.
  •  Maintain confidentiality of procurement information and supplier documentation.
  •  Contribute to a safe, respectful, inclusive, and collaborative working environment.
  •  Perform any other procurement, logistics, or administrative duties assigned by the Supervisor, Project Coordinator, or Executive Director that are consistent with the nature of the position.

Qualifications, Experience, Knowledge, and Skills

Education

  •  Bachelor’s degree in business administration/ management from a recognized university.

Professional Experience

  • Minimum 2 years of relevant professional experience in procurement, logistics, administration, or supply chain management, preferably in NGOs, INGOs, or donor-funded projects.
  •  Experience in implementing procurement processes, logistics coordination, inventory management, and vendor management.
  •  Experience in preparing procurement documentation, maintaining procurement records, and supporting procurement committee processes.
  •  Experience in coordinating transportation, delivery of goods, and warehouse or inventory management.
  •  Familiarity with donor-funded project procurement procedures is desirable.

Knowledge

  •  Good knowledge of procurement principles, logistics operations, inventory control, and asset management.
  •  Understanding of procurement policies, competitive bidding procedures, and value-for-money principles.
  •  Familiarity with the procurement requirements of donor-funded projects and the applicable laws and regulations of the Government of Nepal.

Technical Skills

Core Competencies

The position helps in making timely informed decisions which allows the program to act according to program information/dataway,The position also work according to the donor requirements- and learn more as an organization.

The MERL Officer is in charge of creating and using monitoring plans, tracking numbers, making sure that the collected data is efficient, effective and correct. With the use of digital tools the position is responsible in checking the data quality through regular checks, data triangulation and source data verification. The role maintains the data base in order which supports in writing relevant reports and internal and external sharing documents with special emphasis on knowledge sharing so that the program can be more effective and impactful.

This position works under the guidance of the Project Coordinator. Works closely with the teams that handle the program, safety, sponsorships and technical issues. The MERL Officer makes sure that everything follows the rules of KIDS, the MERL standards of
Plan International Nepal what the donors want and the rules from the Government of Nepal. The role also helps with being responsible by making community feedback systems making sure data is honest keeping private data safe and helping the people working on the project and the partners learn more about the tools, ways and standards for MERL. By checking all the time making sure the information is correct and learning from the work the MERL Officer helps reach the goals of the project make the program better.
Help children, young people, families and communities, in the project areas.

A. Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning

  •  Develop periodic MERL work plans that match project objectives and donor requirements.
  • Maintain and regularly update project monitoring tools, indicator tracking systems and reporting mechanisms.
  • Regular monitoring of project outputs, outcomes and impact indicators and informing the program on timely basis.
  • Against the set targets check the performance of the project and suggest changes to make the program better and more effective.
  • Help include evidence-based planning and flexible program management.

B. Field Monitoring

  • Visit the field on a regular basis to check program implementation, stakeholders’ participation and assess that program activities are being conducted as per approved workplan, Monitor the quality of activities being conducted by the partner staffs, the schools, the health facilities and the community groups.
  •  Verify reported achievements through field observation, community/stakeholder’s consultations, document review and community feedback and ensure the validity and reliability of the data reported. Identify, gaps, challenges and potential risk areas that could cause and provide recommendations for overall program improvement
  • Write reports about what’s seen during the field visits and make sure that the things that were agreed to be done are actually done.

C. Data Collection and Database Management

  • Support the establishment and maintenance of systems for collecting, managing, and storing data on project beneficiaries, indicators, activities, and results to ensure accurate and reliable project information. Collect, compile, verify, and maintain project data on a regular basis to ensure it is accurate, complete, and securely stored.Update the digital data collection tools, like KoboToolbox. Coordinate with field staff to ensure project data is collected accurately, completely, and submitted on time for entry into the project database.Ensure that project data is kept secure and confidential and is managed in accordance with the organization’s data protection and confidentiality policies.D. Data Quality Assurance (DQA)
  • Prepare and put Data Quality Assessment (DQA) plans into action.
  • Carry out data checks, data triangulations,spot inspections and quality reviews.
  • Make sure that the data is accurate, complete, consistent, up to date, and valid.
  • Assess the data quality on timely manner and provide MERL support in making the reporting systems better.
  • Keep records and documentation of the data and reportings th for verification by donors and audits.

  • Support in supervising enumerators and field researchers during surveys and assessments.
  • Coordinate and support external consultants during evaluations and research assignments.

F. Data Analysis, Reporting and Visualization

  • Compile and analyze programme data to track progress against the set target.Prepare monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, annual, and donor reports in accordance with reporting schedules.

  • Document best practices, success stories, case studies, innovations, and lessons learned.

  •  Support the analysis of community feedback and contribute to recommendations for improving project implementation. Promote community participation, transparency, and accountability during monitoring and field activities. Promote transparency, inclusion, and accountability throughout project implementation.
  • Build the capacity of project staff, volunteers, partners, and community structures on MERL concepts, tools, and methodologies.

J. Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement

  •  Coordinate closely with programme, finance, safeguarding, sponsorship, and technical teams to ensure effective programme monitoring and reporting.

Job Summary

The Technical Coordinator – Enterprise Development will provide technical leadership and coordination for enterprise development initiatives aimed at improving livelihoods, promoting sustainable income generation, and fostering inclusive economic growth. The position will support the design, implementation, monitoring, and quality assurance of enterprise development interventions, with a focus on micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), entrepreneurship promotion, market systems development, value chain strengthening, financial inclusion, and employment generation.
The coordinator will work closely with local governments, private sector actors, financial institutions, cooperatives, producer groups, youth and women entrepreneurs, and other stakeholders to ensure effective implementation of enterprise development activities aligned with national policies and local economic development priorities.

A. Key Responsibilities

  •  Support the development/ manage of technical guidelines, training manuals, business toolkits, and operational procedures.
  •  Ensure quality implementation of enterprise development interventions in Kapilvastu.

  • Ensure timely, efficient, and quality delivery of planned activities in line with approved plans and budgets.

  •  Facilitate in running climate farmer field school
  •  Promote green, inclusive, and sustainable enterprises.

  • Collaborate with local governments for capacity building of young people
  • Capacity building of project team for effective implementation of the project activities.

  •  Organize exposure visits and learning events.

6. Partnership and Stakeholder Coordination

Contract Duration: Up to July 15, 2027, with potential for extension based on performance, funding availability, and project needs.

Position Overview

The District Focal Person (DFP) will lead the implementation of the Community-Led Monitoring (CLM) for Tuberculosis (TB) initiative at the district level. This role is pivotal in strengthening TB service delivery, enhancing health system accountability, and ensuring high-quality patient care. Under the guidance of the Team Lead and the M&E Manager, the DFP will coordinate community engagement, mobilize and supervise CLM Leaders, oversee data collection and validation, and foster strategic collaborations with local authorities, community leaders, and partner organizations.

Key Roles & Responsibilities

1. Program Coordination & Field Implementation

  • Execute district-level project activities in strict adherence to CLM guidelines, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), the CLM Toolkit, and the project’s logical framework.

Posiiton: Project Finance Officer
Location: Kathmandu, Nepal
Deadline: Thursday 13th August 2026

ActionAid is a global justice federation committed to advancing social justice, gender equality, and the eradication of poverty. Established in 1972, the organization has continuously evolved to address the systemic drivers of inequality and injustice. ActionAid’s core belief is that people living in poverty and exclusion hold the power to create meaningful change within their families, communities, and societies. Since the 1990s, ActionAid has embraced a Human Rights-Based Approach (HRBA) to development, and in 2003, the ActionAid International federation was formed, now headquartered in South Africa.

ActionAid International Nepal (AAIN), a member of this global federation, was established in 1982 as a social justice organization working across multiple provinces of Nepal. AAIN actively engages in national and international social justice movements and collaborates with networks, alliances, and civil society coalitions. Through an HRBA framework, AAIN empowers marginalized communities to claim their rights and challenge the root causes of poverty, exclusion, and injustice. As part of the global federation, AAIN works with partners worldwide to promote social justice, gender equality, poverty eradication, and climate justice.

The Project Finance Officer is responsible for supporting effective financial and grant management of externally funded programmes that contribute to climate resilience, Ecosystem-based Adaptation, and sustainable development, in alignment with ActionAid International Nepal’s (AAIN) Strategy 2029.

The position ensures sound financial management, planning and budgeting, grant management, financial and donor reporting, with AAIN policies and procedures, donor requirements, and applicable laws and regulations while providing technical and operational support to implementing partners to strengthen financial management, internal controls, and compliance, and contributes to strengthening AAIN’s financial systems, internal controls, and institutional financial sustainability as a member of the Finance Sustainability Unit.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Support finance team, programme team and partner organization on the planning and budgeting for both AAIN and Partners level following the organizational standards, donor’s requirements and applicable financial guidelines
  • Conduct and contribute to the review and consolidation of AAIN’s annual plans and budgets while providing technical support to Partner Organisations in the development of work-plan and budget from externally funded programmes
  • Support the line manager in analyzing and mitigating foreign exchange gain/loss implications during budget preparation and budget revisions.
  • Provide updated funding information, in consultation with the Line Manager to Head of Finance Sustainability and Administration (HoFSA) to support informed planning and budgeting decisions.
  • Monitor the financial performance of externally funded projects and provide regular financial status updates and analysis to the Line Manager, Finance Sustainability Unit and programme team.
  • Conduct periodic financial monitoring and compliance reviews of implementing Partner Organizations through monitoring visits, desk reviews and other appropriate mechanisms to ensure compliance with donor requirements, organisational policies and procedures, and applicable laws and regulations.
  • Track and follow up on the implementation of agreed corrective actions at both Partner Organisation and AAIN levels to ensure timely resolution of audit, monitoring, and compliance findings.
  • Support on Due diligence Process of partners as required
  • Timely and accurate recording of all income and expenditure transactions in the accounting system.
  • Perform periodic bank and account reconciliations and provide alternative for resolution of discrepancies.
  • Monitor and report exchange gains/losses related to project funds.
  • Support the timely updating of financial information in the CMS system.
  • Maintain adequate cash flow to facilitate the smooth implementation of programs and projects.
  • Provide accurate and timely financial information and reports to the Line Manager, finance team, program team and other stakeholders as required.
  • Support on SWC or regulatory body compliances like as periodic reports/CPAC/MPAC/evaluations etc.
  • Allocate and distribute common/shared costs across projects periodically in accordance with organizational policies, guidelines, and standard practices.

Requirements

  • Has knowledge about different donors’ requirements and compliance
  • Has good knowledge about effective communication among teams, partners and relevant groups
  • Has knowledge of operating accounting software it’s workflow to maintain financial records and transactions

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in finance/management/Commerce or equivalent from a recognized university
  • Master’s degree in finance, Accounting or Financial Management, Qualification such as ACCA, CA, CPA qualification are preferable
  • At least 3-5 years of relevant experience
  • Experience of working in a multi-cultural environment in similar role
  • Experience of working in Non-Profit Organization I/NGOs in donor funded projects is preferable.

AAIN is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to their ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, HIV status, and disability status.

AAIN is committed to its values and principles on feminist leadership, safeguarding (including Child Safeguarding and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse [PSEA]), and safety & security. All applicants are expected to adhere to AAIN’s policies and procedures.

UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence.

At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling.

UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package.

Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF.

For every child, the right to a Champion

How can you make a difference?

In this critical role, under the guidance and supervision of Deputy Representative, you will establish and implement Nepal Country Office emergency preparedness and response. You will be responsible for the development, planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of the emergency interventions to ensure the survival and well-being of children and mothers, and the affected communities in an emergency situation.

You will provide technical oversight to emergency preparedness and response actions led by the field offices, in close coordination with the Chief Field Offices and section heads in Kathmandu through the following key areas of responsibility:

  • Emergency Preparedness
  • Emergency Response
  • Emergency Project

If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: Download File JD Emergency Specialist NOC , Kathmandu.pdf

To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have…

Minimum requirements

  • Education: Master or equivalent (Advanced University Degree) in international relations, international law, Nutrition
  • Work Experience: 5 years of relevant work experience in programme/project development, planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and administration. Field work experience is required.
  • Skills: Knowledge of UN humanitarian reform principles, international humanitarian laws, global humanitarian issues
  • Language Requirements: Both English and Nepali – Proficient/Fluent

Desirables

  • Language: Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish).
  • Developing-country experience, UN system experience, maternal health, neonatal health, humanitarian preparedness.
  • Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts.
  • Proven track record of leading DRR, emergency preparedness and response actions in close coordination with the government, partners and different levels within the organization.
  • Experience in fundraising to support emergency preparedness and response actions.
  • Experience in establishing and providing strategic leadership for partnerships and resource mobilization opportunities to support emergency preparedness and response.
  • Demonstrated skills in drafting and compiling high quality reports in English and Nepali.
  • Strong thought leadership capacity in emergency preparedness and response.
  • Demonstrated experience in planning and monitoring programme funds and resources and verify compliance with organizational guidelines, rules and regulations .

For every Child, you demonstrate…

UNICEF’s Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values

UNICEF competencies required for this post are…

(1) Builds and maintains partnerships
(2) Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness
(3) Drive to achieve results for impact
(4) Innovates and embraces change
(5) Manages ambiguity and complexity

Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and its different levels.

UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status.

UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage Accessibility | UNICEF. Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance.

UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities. UNICEF is committed to promote the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially.

UNICEF appointments are subject to medical clearance. Issuance of a visa by the host country of the duty station is required for IP positions and will be facilitated by UNICEF. Appointments are conditional on the selected candidates willingness to comply with current or future vaccination requirements, should UNICEF mandate it for personnel. Failure to comply with such requirements, where applicable and without a duly approved medical exemption from the relevant UN authority, will result in the cancellation of the selection or may lead to other administrative measures, including separation from service.

Remarks:

As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity.

UNICEF is committed to fostering an inclusive, representative, and welcoming workforce. For this position, eligible and suitable female candidates and candidates from under-represented ethnic groups are encouraged to apply.

Government employees who are considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF reserves the right to withdraw an offer of appointment, without compensation, if a visa or medical clearance is not obtained, or necessary inoculation requirements are not met, within a reasonable period for any reason.

UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants’ bank account information.

Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF’s Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to stay and deliver in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities.

Visa residence requirements: i.e. UNICEF shall not facilitate the issuance of a visa and working authorization for candidates under consideration for positions at the national officer and general service category.

All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates.

Position Title: MEAL Officer (Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning) Officer
Project: SAMBHAV JEEVAN: Enabling Better Lives through Sight and Sound
Reports to: Project Manager, SAMBHAV JEEVAN
Duty Station: NNJS Project Office, Birendranagar, Surkhet with regular travel to all project catchment areas in Karnali Province
Supervises: No direct reports; works closely with project team, the Disability Inclusion Officer and the Admin & Finance Officer for data inputs
Contract Type / Duration: Full-time, fixed-term project position aligned with the project cycle; subject to performance and continued project funding

Background

Karnali Province continues to face a high burden of preventable and treatable eye and ear health problems, particularly among populations living in remote and hard-to-reach areas. Limited availability of specialized services, weak referral systems, and geographic barriers have resulted in inadequate access to quality care for the majority of communities. In this context, there is a critical need to design, plan, and implement comprehensive community-based eye and ear care interventions. The proposed project aims to strengthen early detection, expand outreach services, and improve access to affordable and inclusive care, ensuring that underserved populations in Karnali can receive timely and effective eye and ear health services.

Position Purpose

The MEAL Officer is responsible for designing, operating and continuously improving the project’s monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning system; for the timely and accurate collection, management and analysis of disaggregated project data; for producing the project’s MEAL-related reports on schedule; and for ensuring that communities, including persons with disabilities and other marginalized groups, have a genuine and accessible voice in shaping and reviewing project delivery through a functioning feedback and complaints mechanism.

Key Responsibilities:

i) MEAL System Design and Management

  • Develop and implement the project’s full Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Plan, and keep it updated throughout the project cycle.
  • Design and maintain data-collection tools (registers, screening/camp forms, referral forms, complaint forms) that capture results disaggregated in line with the Log Frame.
  • Set up and administer the project’s Database Management, ensuring camp, screening, surgical, referral and training data are entered, cleaned and backed up in a timely manner.
  • Track progress against all Log Frame indicators and flag off-track indicators early.
  • Maintain and regularly update the project risk register, in coordination with the Project Manager.
  • Support Program Manager to prepare standard operation plan (SOP) of the activities.

ii) Reporting and Compliance

  • Prepare, or coordinate inputs for, all MEAL-related deliverables in the Reporting Plan, including: the Indicator Tracking Report and Activity Plan Report, the Quarterly and Annual
  • Project Reports, the updated M&E Plan and updated Project Risk Register, the Annual Reflection Report, and the monthly project update and plan.
  • Work closely with the Program Manager and Admin & Finance Officer to ensure narrative and financial reporting are consistent and submitted to CBM Global on schedule.
  • Maintain project records, data and documentation in line with the contract’s requirement, and ensure data is available for audit or monitoring visits on request.
  • Support preparation for internal and external audits, donor monitoring visits, including organizing evidence and facilitating access to community-level data.
  • Prepare and submit the datae as requested for funding organization.

iii) Accountability, Community Engagement and Feedback

  • Establish and manage an accessible community feedback and complaints mechanism (complaint boxes, providing contact details, telephone log, suggestion box) at base hospitals, eye/ear camps and community events.
  • Ensure feedback and complaints are logged, reviewed, responded to, and reported at least quarterly.
  • Facilitate regular consultations with beneficiaries, local Organizations of Persons with Disabilities and community leaders to assess service effectiveness, and ensure their input feeds into project adaptation.
  • Coordinate for community-level learning and sharing sessions, and document lessons learned for internal reflection.

iv) Safeguarding-Related MEAL Duties

  • Support the Disability Inclusion Officer in implementing and monitoring the project’s safeguarding reporting, investigation and response procedures, including tracking the required face-to-face safeguarding training for staff.
  • Ensure any safeguarding, fraud or other substantial risk incident identified through MEAL processes.
  • Ensure Data Protection standards to all personal data collected through MEAL processes (informed consent, secure storage, anonymization/pseudonymization before sharing), and report any personal data breach within 48 hours.

v) Evaluations and Learning

  • Coordinate logistics, data provision and stakeholder engagement for the project’s Baseline, Mid-Term and Final/End-Term Evaluations, working with the appointed independent evaluators/consultants.
  • Uphold the principles of quality, accuracy, utility, participation, ownership, ethics, reliability, transparency, cost-effectiveness, and impartiality.
  • Document and help produce project case studies, blogs, newsletter and accessible success stories (audio/video/print), in coordination with the Program Manager and Disability Inclusion Officer.

vi) Disability and Gender Inclusion in MEAL

  • Ensure all data collection, analysis and reporting is disaggregated as demand by the project and findings are used to identify and close equity gaps in service access.
  • Work with partners and stakeholders to ensure MEAL processes (data collection tools, feedback mechanisms, evaluation participation) are accessible and participatory for persons with disabilities.

vii) Coordination and Capacity Building

  • Provide MEAL-related orientation and on-the-job coaching to Community Eye Health Workers, base-hospital data collectors and volunteers on data quality, recording and reporting standards.
  • Represent the project’s MEAL function in Project Coordination Committee meetings, project review and reflection meetings.
  • Perform other MEAL and programme-quality-related duties requested by the Project Manager or NNJS management in support of project objectives.

Qualifications and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree (Master’s preferred) in Public Health, Statistics, Social Sciences, Development Studies, or a related field.
  • At least 3 years of professional experience in Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) or M&E roles within an I/NGO, preferably in health, disability inclusion or community development programming.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and managing data-collection systems and databases, and contribute donor-standard quarterly/annual narrative and indicator reports.
  • Experience supporting or coordinating external evaluations, audits or reviews.
  • Prior experience working in Karnali Province or similar remote/hard-to-reach contexts is an advantage.
  • Experience working with Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) or on disability-inclusive programming is strongly preferred.

Skills and Competencies

  • Sound understanding and skills in qualitative and data collection, management and analysis.
  • Strong data management and analysis skills, including proficiency with mobile/digital data-collection tools, data management and analysis software.
  • Sound understanding of log frames, theory of change, and indicator design, including disaggregation by sex, age and disability.
  • Working knowledge of safeguarding, data protection and accountability.
  • Facilitation, coaching and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work respectfully and effectively with community members, persons with disabilities, government officials, and partners.
  • Willingness and ability to travel frequently within Karnali Province, including to remote hill and mountain districts.

Job Description

Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

  • Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
  • Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
  • Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers
  • Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience, and resources to help people build a better life. We are on the ground in 170 countries and territories, working with governments and people on their own solutions to global and national development challenges to help empower lives and build resilient nations.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Communications and Reporting Analyst will be responsible for designing and implementing a comprehensive communications and visibility strategy that effectively showcases the results, innovations, and lessons of the Nepal project. The Communications and Reporting Analyst will develop and manage communication materials, coordinate outreach with national and international stakeholders, and ensure alignment with UNDP and donor branding requirements. Key duties include documenting project achievements, producing multimedia content, strengthening media and partner networks, and supporting advocacy and knowledge exchange at national, regional, and global levels.

Design, Develop, implement and manage the project communication strategy:

  • Finalize, implement, and update a communications and visibility strategy aligned with UNDP standards.
  • Ensure coverage of all project components and integration of GESI and safeguards dimensions.
  • Produce high-quality materials, including press releases, newsletters, infographics, reports, case studies, photo essays, and short videos.
  • Oversee the design, layout, and production of communication outputs, ensuring adherence to UN editorial and branding guidelines.
  • Maintain a digital library of media, photographs, and knowledge products.
  • Track communication outputs, media coverage, and audience engagement.
  • Provide quarterly updates and inputs to project progress reports, highlighting communication milestones and results.
  • Recommend adjustments to enhance visibility, outreach, and impact.
  • Integrate GESI principles in all planning, implementation, and monitoring processes to ensure equitable participation and benefits for women, men, persons with disabilities, and marginalized groups.

Strengthen media engagement and partnerships:

  • Establish and maintain relationships with national and international media outlets, journalists, and influencers to raise awareness of project outcomes.
  • Facilitate media coverage of key milestones, site visits, and events related to UNDP projects.
  • Provide technical guidance and capacity building to staff, partners, and stakeholders on applying gender and social inclusion approaches in project interventions.

Job Description

Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

  • Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
  • Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

  • Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience, and resources to help people build a better life. We are on the ground in 170 countries and territories, working with governments and people on their own solutions to global and national development challenges to help empower lives and build resilient nations.

Under the overall guidance of the Project Manager, the Administration and Finance Analyst will be responsible for the day-to-day financial management, administration, and operational support of the project. The Analyst ensures the effective and transparent utilization of financial resources, compliance with UNDP rules and regulations, and integrates principles of Gender Equality, Social Inclusion (GESI), and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) into all operational activities.

Duties and Responsibilities

Ensure implementation of Financial Management and Accounting

  • Manage the day-to-day financial operations, ensuring full compliance with UNDP rules, regulations, policies, and NIM/DIM procedures.
  • Process payment requests, disbursements, and travel claim accurately within the UNDP ERP system (e.g., Quantum).
  • Maintain a robust internal expenditure control system. Regularly monitor financial exception reports, investigate unusual transactions or anomalies, and propose corrective actions to management.
  • Continuously monitor project budgets and expenditures in cooperation with the Project Manager.
  • Conduct quality financial analysis of budget performance by cost inputs and partners and support the preparation of financial forecasts and disbursement requests.
  • Prepare timely and accurate financial statements, bank reconciliations, and consolidated reports for the Project Board, donors, and the Country Office.
  • Support the development of funding requests, grant negotiations, and amendments.
  • Facilitate programme audits and investigations in coordination with relevant oversight bodies.
  • Ensure the effective implementation of audit recommendations, management actions, and recovery actions.
  • Conduct regular field visits in close coordination with the programme team to ensure financial compliance and provide monitoring support for implementing partners and sub-recipients.

Ensure management of programme budgets and the operation of the optimal cost recovery system

  • Prepare, continuously monitor, and revise programme budgets in UNDP ERP systems (Quantum and Hyperion), ensuring strict alignment with approved detailed budgets and Annual Work Plans (AWPs).
  • Implement optimal cost recovery mechanisms, ensuring Direct Project Costs (DPC) and General Management Support (GMS) fees are accurately calculated and billed.
  • Maintain robust internal controls to ensure transactions are correctly coded against budget lines and donor agreements prior to approval.
  • Conduct regular analysis of budget delivery and expenditure variances.
  • Prepare budget reviews, financial forecasts, and provide justifications for necessary budget reallocations or reprogramming requests for submission to donors.
  • Prepare accurate monthly, quarterly, and annual cash flow forecasts.
  • Monitor incoming donor contributions, ensuring the timely transfer, identification, and registration of receipts in the system.
  • Finalize the financial sections of progress reports, disbursement requests, and statements of sources and use of funds, strictly adhering to specific donor reporting timelines and requirements.
  • Transaction Processing & Records Management: Manage the initiation, approval, and settlement of bank transfers.
  • Ensure the proper management of cash receipts and petty cash, and maintain a rigorous, audit-ready filing system for all finance records and documents.

Ensure facilitation of knowledge building and knowledge sharing in monitoring and evaluation

  • In coordination with the Project Manager supports the development of partnerships and maintains strong working relationships with the national, provincial partners and entities, donors, technical partners, and UN agencies to ensure transparent and effective management, quality services and oversight of the programmes.
  • Supports the Project Manager in the development of capacity development through different trainings/coaching/mentoring and transition strategies to support national entities to implement and assume the PR role, ensuring access to appropriate tools and resources.
  • Actively participates in UNDP and other relevant external networks/forums to promote the programme.
  • Conduct training for the project and other relevant stakeholders on financial management and oversight.

Ensure Effective Administration and Operations Management

  • Ensure the effective administration and operational management of the project in compliance with UNDP rules, regulations, policies, and procedures.
  • Coordinate project procurement activities, including preparation of procurement plans, specifications, requests for quotations, purchase orders, and contract management in accordance with UNDP procurement policies.
  • Monitor the implementation of procurement activities and maintain an updated procurement tracking system to ensure timely delivery of goods and services.
  • Support recruitment processes for project personnel and consultants, including preparation of Terms of Reference (TORs), evaluation processes, contract administration, and onboarding arrangements.
  • Coordinate travel arrangements for project personnel, consultants, and stakeholders, including travel authorizations, ticketing, logistics, security clearances, and travel claim settlements.
  • Organize project meetings, workshops, trainings, and field missions, ensuring appropriate logistical, administrative, and financial arrangements.
  • Maintain project asset and inventory records and ensure proper utilization, maintenance, verification, transfer, and disposal of project assets in accordance with UNDP policies.
  • Ensure effective records management and maintain an organized filing system for project administrative, procurement, human resources, and operational documentation.
  • Monitor the validity and timely renewal of project contracts, agreements, leases, and service arrangements.
  • Support the preparation and monitoring of project work plans, procurement plans, HR plans, and operational plans.
  • Coordinate with UNDP operations units and service providers to ensure timely provision of administrative and operational support services.
  • Identify operational risks and recommend appropriate mitigation measures to ensure efficient project implementation.
  • Support project closure activities, including asset disposal, records archiving, contract closure, and administrative reporting.
  • Ensure environmental sustainability, accessibility, safeguarding, and GESI considerations are integrated into project operations and administrative processes.

Contribution towards Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI)

  • Ensure GESI is mainstreamed in the budget, Annual Work Plan (AWP), procurement and HR plans, and all other administrative work to be undertaken by the project in coordination with Community, Rights and Gender Analyst and GESI Analyst of UNDP CO.
  • Promote gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) throughout programme implementation.
  • Collaborates with team members, programme partners, and sub-grantees to ensure safe implementation of programmes at the community level applying Do No Harm approach.
  • Promote a respectful, inclusive, and safe workplace culture, supporting “Do No Harm” principles in all administrative and field-level operations.
  • Assist in collecting and reporting gender-disaggregated data related to project administration, procurements, and event participation.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

  • A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in Finance and/or Accounting in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.
