Nabil Bank, established in 1984, is a market leader in Nepal’s banking sector. We are dedicated to be Nepal’s most trusted and future-ready Bank. Upholding our brand promise, “Together Ahead”, we invite highly talented, motivated, and qualified Nepali citizens to apply for the following position:

Position : Chief Risk Officer (CRO)
Level : Senior Manager (M4) and Above

Job Summary

The Chief Risk Officer (CRO) is a Board-facing strategic executive responsible for providing independent oversight and leadership of the Bank’s enterprise-wide risk management and risk strategy. The CRO leads the Integrated Risk Management Framework (IRMF), ensuring effective identification, assessment, monitoring, and mitigation of material risks in line with the Bank’s risk appetite, strategic objectives, and regulatory requirements.

As the Head of Risk Management and Member-Secretary of the Board-level Risk Management Committee (RMC), CRO provides independent risk advice to the Board and Senior Management and oversees key areas including capital and stress testing, digital and cyber risk, climate and emerging risks, model governance, and operational resilience, while promoting a strong risk culture and supporting sustainable business growth.

Key Responsibilities

1. Risk Governance, Strategy & Board Advisory

  • Develop, lead and continuously enhance the Bank’s long- term Enterprise Risk Strategy, IRMF, and Risk Appetite Framework, aligned with the Board approved Risk Appetite, Risk Tolerance, and three lines of defense model.
  • Advise the Board and Senior Management on strategic and emerging risks, including risk implications of business plans and major business initiatives, and provide independent challenge where appropriate.
  • Establish and monitor risk limits, KRIs, dashboards, escalation and breach management frameworks, ensuring alignment with the Bank’s risk profile and regulatory requirements.
  • Review and enhance risk policies and control frameworks and provide periodic enterprise risk and emerging risk reports to the Board.

2. Credit Risk Leadership

  • Provide strategic oversight of credit risk, portfolio quality, sector and concentration risk, counterparty risk, sovereign exposure, and climate-related credit risk.
  • Oversee credit risk models, credit scorecards, early warning systems, watch list governance, NPA forecasting, recovery trend analysis and portfolio risk optimization.
  • Monitor the overall risk profile, asset quality, and portfolio concentration and strengthen risk analytics and emerging risk identification.

3. Market, Liquidity & Treasury Risk

  • Oversee Interest Rate Risk in Banking Book (IRRBB), foreign exchange, investment, Asset-Liability Management (ALM) and liquidity risks, transfer pricing risk including contingency funding and behavioral modelling.
  • Ensure effective macroeconomic scenario analysis and stress testing of market and liquidity exposures.
  • Provide oversight of compliance, AML/CFT, and information security risks as part of the Bank’s enterprise-wide risk framework.

4. Operational Resilience & Non-Financial Risk

  • Establish oversight frameworks for operational resilience, business continuity, disaster recovery, third-party/outsourcing, fraud, conduct, reputation, physical security, and crisis management risks.

5. Digital, Technology & Cyber Risk

  • Provide independent oversight of cyber, information security, cloud, digital banking, data governance / privacy, Artificial Intelligence, model, FinTech partnership, and technology investment risks.
  • Establish appropriate governance for technology and AI-enabled risk models.

6. Climate, ESG & Emerging Risks

  • Lead the development of the Bank’s climate and Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) risk management framework, covering physical and transition risks, green financing, sustainability considerations, and climate stress testing.
  • Identify and assess emerging risks that may affect the Bank’s resilience and long-term sustainability.

7. Capital & Balance Sheet Management

  • Provide oversight of ICAAP, capital forecasting, capital and reverse stress testing, recovery planning, economic capital, Risk Adjusted Return on Capital (RAROC), and risk-based pricing to ensure adequate capital and risk-adjusted returns.
  • Ensure alignment of capital with the Bank’s overall risk profile.

8. Model Risk Management

  • Establish and oversee the Bank’s Model Risk Management Framework covering model governance, validation, performance monitoring, and periodic review.
  • Oversee IFRS 9/ECL, credit, scorecard, stress-testing, and AI models, ensuring robust methodologies, assumptions, and outputs.
  • Ensure independent validation, backtesting, sensitivity analysis, and timely remediation of model-related findings, with appropriate integration into risk reporting, provisioning, capital planning, and ICAAP.

9. Enterprise – wide Risk Reporting

  • Ensure timely and comprehensive risk reporting to the Board and Senior Management through risk dashboards, heat maps, emerging risk reports, scenario analysis, top 20 Enterprise Risks and forward-looking enterprise risk outlooks to support strategic and business decisions.

10. Regulatory & Supervisory Engagement

  • Lead regulatory and supervisory engagement, ensuring compliance with applicable NRB directives and laws, effective coordination with regulators and auditors, and timely and accurate regulatory risk reporting, including Basel and resolution planning requirements.
  • Represent the Bank in relevant regulatory and industry forums and ensure effective management of supervisory reviews and inspections.

11. Risk Culture & Awareness

  • Promote a strong enterprise-wide risk culture through risk culture assessments, training, certification, conduct risk programmes, appropriate incentive alignment, speak-up mechanisms, and risk awareness initiatives.
  • Drive risk awareness, accountability, and appropriate risk-taking behaviour across the Bank and support organizational transformation and cross-functional collaboration.

12. Cross-functional Governance

  • Provide leadership and/or participate in relevant risk governance forums, including Executive Risk, Operational Risk, Market Risk, Model Risk, New Product Approval, Information Security, ALCO, Credit, Credit Control, Compliance, AML/CFT, and IT Steering Committees, as applicable.
  • Ensure strong coordination between business, support, and control functions and build appropriate capabilities, systems, and talent within the risk function.
  • Evaluate credit proposals, new products, strategic initiatives, and major business decisions from an independent risk perspective and ensure appropriate risk mitigation measures are in place.

13. Performance Management

  • Establish measurable risk management outcomes, including maintaining risk within Board-approved appetite, strengthening early warning and stress-testing capabilities, reducing material operational losses, ensuring timely closure of audit and regulatory observations, and maintaining compliance with regulatory requirements.

14. Risk Management Committee -Member-Secretary

  • Act as Member-Secretary of the Board-level Risk Management Committee (RMC).
  • Coordinate RMC meetings, including agenda preparation, circulation of relevant risk reports and materials, and effective communication with Committee members.
  • Ensure effective Board-level risk reporting and communication and monitor and track implementation of decisions and directives of the RMC.

Qualification & Experience

  • Master’s Degree in Finance, Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, Risk Management, Banking, Business Administration, or related discipline from a recognized University/Institution.
  • Minimum 15 years of banking experience, with at least 8 years in progressively senior risk management/leadership roles.
  • Currently serving in a senior risk leadership role in Risk Review, Monitoring and Management, such as Head of Credit Risk, Chief Risk Officer (CRO), or Deputy CRO.
  • Candidates with Professional certifications such as Financial / Professional Risk Manager (FRM/ PRM), CFA, CA & Cybersecurity Risk will be given preference.
  • Demonstrated experience interacting with Boards, regulators, auditors, and rating agencies.
  • Proven experience in enterprise risk management, Basel implementation, ICAAP, IFRS 9/ECL, stress testing, model governance, and digital risk.
  • Experience leading large cross-functional teams and driving enterprise-wide risk transformation.

Job Description

The Position:

Under the overall supervision of the International Operations Manager, guidance and direct supervision of the Finance Associate, the Finance Assistant is responsible for implementing the organizational financial rules and regulations in the UNFPA Country Office (CO). S/he delivers quality financial services to the CO staff, ensuring effective and transparent financial management. The Finance Assistant promotes a client-oriented approach and ensures adherence with relevant UNFPA policies, procedures, rules and regulations.

How you can make a difference:

UNFPA is the lead United Nations agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is intended, every childbirth is safe, and every young person’s potential is fulfilled. The UNFPA Strategic Plan for 2026-2029 articulates the organization’s response to a complex global environment, providing a roadmap for resilience and renewal. It is designed to accelerate the implementation of the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD) and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. This mandate is pursued through a focus on four interconnected outcomes: ending the unmet need for family planning; ending preventable maternal deaths; ending gender-based violence and harmful practices; and adapting to demographic change through evidence and rights-based policies.

In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff who embody these international norms and standards and will defend them courageously and with full conviction.

UNFPA is seeking candidates who transform, inspire, and deliver high-impact sustained results, ensuring effective external relations, communications, partnership-building and resource mobilization in a rapidly changing development and funding landscape. We need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them, and who commit to delivering excellence in programme results

Job Purpose:

The Finance Assistant will provide overall financial management support to the Finance Associate in the Operations Team. The Finance Assistant works in close collaboration with the operations, programme and project teams in the UNFPA CO; s/he facilitates smooth operations, helps resolve any complex financial issues, and ensures high quality and accuracy of work.

You would be responsible for:

1. Implementation of operational strategies:

  • Confirms full compliance of financial processes and financial records with UNFPA rules, regulations, policies, and strategies.
  • Provides input to the CO business processes mapping and elaboration of the content of internal Standard Operating Procedures in finance in consultation, with the direct supervisor and office management.
  • Provides input to the finance unit and operations annual plan.

2. Acting as the payment focal point, including preparing Payment Vouchers, Journal Vouchers and GLJEs:

  • Reviews payment request submitted through aodocs and ensure enough supporting documents are uploaded.
  • Create invoices in Quantum to disburse all payments to the vendors through ERP system ensuring availability of funds.
  • Reviews cash advance request documents, provides inputs and processes prepayment invoices in ERP for advance settlement the approved documents. Ensures settlement of the cash advance on time and creates necessary vouchers in the ERP.
  • On a monthly basis, checks and charges proper Chart of Accounts, in case they are wrongly charged.
  • Deposits any refund of funds/receipt of funds related to UNFPA to UNDP bank account.
  • Prepare adjustment vouchers.
  • Ensure proper processing of VAT; ensure VAT records are maintained, followed up with relevant authorities for timely refunds.
  • Maintains VAT records and reconciliations as required by policies and procedures.
  • Supports the Finance Associate in programme finance related issues.

3. Acting as FACE focal point for all the FACE forms of all IPs:

  • Follows-up and receives FACE forms from implementing partner focal persons for timely processing of disbursements and recording of expenditures.
  • Registers the FACE forms in the standard table developed for keeping record of FACE forms processed or pending processing for following up with concerned focal persons.
  • Processes the FACE form voucher(s) originated through QuantumPlus and proper filing.
  • Facilitates the finance-related training organized for the staff and IPs.

4. Receiving and reviewing the Travel Claim (TC) / F10 forms:

  • Review of the Travel Claims submitted through UNALL, as per the financial and travel policy of UNFPA.
  • Ensures proper settlement of Travel Claims including providing feedback to the sub-offices, as required.
  • Ensures for proper charging of accounts.

5. Liaises with UNDP Finance Section and Bank for timely transfer of funds:

  • Follows-up with UNDP for timely processing of payment vouchers processed to be picked up in the pay cycle.
  • Follows-up with UNDP finance and bank(s) for timely release of funds/payments to the vendors.
  • Liaises with UNDP on Receivables and ensures the correct Chart of Accounts is applied. Obtains Deposit ID numbers from UNDP finance to communicate with UNFPA HQ, as required.

6. Effective maintenance of Files/e-files of financial documents:

  • Files the vouchers in a proper manner regularly.
  • Files the finance related documents, i.e., AWPs, IP Agreements, FACE forms, projects &, etc. properly for easy reference and retrieval.
  • Make sure that all vouchers and supporting documents are properly scanned and e-filed on a regular basis.
  • Retrieves and supports FA prepare documents for audits, IP audits and spot checks, or other assurance related activities.

7. Production of various reports from ERP systems and ensuring compliance with Mandatory Tasks:

  • Produces different types of financial reports from ERP Systems and reporting portal.
  • Monitors financial dashboard regularly and clean it to maintain the quality of vouchers.
  • Assists with follow-up with relevant colleagues to ensure compliance with mandatory tasks.

8. Acting as a custodian of petty cash funds:

  • Responsible for safekeeping of petty cash funds.
  • Maintains petty cash register for recording transactions made through petty cash.
  • Reconciles petty cash funds with the expenses on a daily basis.
  • Make payments after Petty cash vouchers as approved.
  • Compiles the petty cash vouchers and forward for replenishment.
  • Assists in responding to HQ queries and maintaining records.

9. Others:

  • Perform any other duties assigned by the Country Office Leadership.
  • Collaborates with team members, programme partners, and sub-grantees to ensure safe implementation of programmes at the community level applying Do No Harm approach.

Qualifications and Experience:

Education:

  • Completed Secondary level education in Finance, Business Administration, Accountancy, Public Administration and related fields with five (5) years of relevant work experience OR Bachelor’s degree in above mentioned field with two (2) years of relevant work experience.

Knowledge and Experience:

  • Relevant experience in the field of finance – accounts receivable, accounts payable, general ledger maintenance, etc.
  • Experience in the application of Quantum/ERP systems would be advantageous.
  • Proficiency in use of Word, Excel and Google based systems.
  • Strong written and oral communications skills.
  • Ability to organize effectively, work under pressure with attention to detail, precision and accuracy.

Languages:

  • Fluency in Nepali & English (oral and written); Other UN languages is an asset.

Required Competencies:

Values:

  • Exemplifying integrity,
  • Demonstrating commitment to UNFPA and the UN system,
  • Embracing cultural diversity,
  • Embracing change.

Core Competencies:

  • Achieving results,
  • Being accountable,
  • Developing and applying professional expertise/business acumen,
  • Thinking analytically and strategically,
  • Working in teams/managing ourselves and our relationships,
  • Communicating for impact .

Functional Competencies:

  • Business acumen,
  • Implementing management systems,
  • Innovation and marketing of new approaches,
  • Client orientation,
  • Organizational awareness.

Compensation and Benefits:

This position offers an attractive remuneration package including a competitive net salary plus health insurance and other benefits as applicable.

UNFPA Work Environment:

UNFPA provides a work environment that reflects the values of gender equality, diversity, integrity and healthy work-life balance. We are committed to ensuring gender parity in the organization and therefore encourage women to apply. Individuals from the LGBTQIA+ community, minority ethnic groups, indigenous populations, persons with disabilities, and other underrepresented groups are highly encouraged to apply. Reasonable accommodation may be provided to applicants with disabilities upon request, to support their participation in the recruitment process. UNFPA promotes equal opportunities in terms of appointment, training, compensation and selection for all regardless of personal characteristics and dimensions of diversity. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion is at the heart of UNFPA’s workforce – click here to learn more.

Disclaimer:

Selection and appointment may be subject to background and reference checks, medical clearance, visa issuance and other administrative requirements.

UNFPA does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process and does not concern itself with information on applicants’ bank accounts.

Position Title: Program Officer – Active Citizenship Department

Department: Programme Department

Reports To: Executive Board

Supervises: Cohort Coordinator (project-based), Interns/Volunteers as assigned

Duty Station: Kathmandu with frequent field travel (Kavre, Rautahat, consortium locations)

Position Type: Full-time

Deadline: August 15, 2026

1. Position Overview

The Program Officer for the Active Citizenship Department plays a central role in driving YUWA’s mandate on youth political participation, with primary responsibility for the Political Participation of Persons with Disabilities (Y-PWD) project. The role requires strong program design, implementation, cohort management, research coordination, and cross-organizational collaboration. The Program Officer will also contribute to YUWA’s core political participation programs and provide support to other departmental initiatives when needed.

2. Purpose of the Position

The Program Officer is responsible for designing, implementing, and managing the Y-PWD Project and supporting the wider Active Citizenship portfolio. This includes fostering meaningful youth civic engagement, facilitating disability-inclusive political participation, coordinating with cohort members and consortium partners, and developing thematic resources and tools. The role ensures donor compliance, timely reporting, field-level monitoring, and collaborative execution of programmatic activities.

3. Key Responsibilities

A. Program Design, Planning, and Implementation (Primary – Y-PWD Project)

  • Lead day-to-day program design and implementation of the Y-PWD Project with minimal guidance, ensuring alignment with departmental and organizational strategies.
  • Co-design Detailed Implementation Plans (DIPs), activity plans, and engagement frameworks in collaboration with the Department Coordinator and Executive Board.
  • Coordinate cohort-based activities, including inception sessions, political participation trainings, exposure visits, and continuous engagement planning.
  • Support, when required, activities under Y-ERISID and department-led core programs.

B. Cohort and Team Supervision

  • Directly supervise the Cohort Coordinator assigned to the Y-PWD Project, ensuring clear task delegation, quality delivery, and accountability.
  • Act as the focal point for cohort management, including recruitment, onboarding, training, and engagement planning for persons with disabilities and the other cohort members.

C. Coordination, Representation, and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Represent YUWA in consortium meetings for the Y-PWD project and act as the primary technical focal person.
  • Engage with government representatives, youth networks, CSOs, disability groups, and other stakeholders to advance political participation objectives.

D. Reporting, Monitoring, Documentation, and Compliance

  • Take the lead in preparing donor-required reports, quarterly updates, and documentation for the Y-PWD Project.
  • Conduct regular field monitoring visits and produce high-quality field reports, documentation notes, and reflective summaries.

E. Finance, Logistics, and Administration

  • Take responsibility for budget tracking, expenditure monitoring, and adherence to financial guidelines for the Y-PWD Project.
  • Coordinate with the Finance Officer for procurement, payments, documentation, logistical arrangements, and compliance processes.

4. Reporting & Line Management

Direct Supervisor: Project Focal (Executive Board)

Secondary Oversight: Executive Board (for strategic guidance and project approvals)

Supervises: Cohort Coordinator, interns/volunteers as designated

Collaborates with: Program Assistant, Communications Team, Finance Team, and other departmental program team as required.

5. Qualifications and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in social sciences, Political Science, Development Studies, Gender Studies, or a related field with a strong understanding of Nepal’s political context, youth civic issues, disability rights,
  • 1–2 years of experience in civic engagement, youth mobilization, disability inclusion, or political participation programming (highly preferred).
  • Experience working with or engaging persons with disabilities is an advantage.
  • Experience in program design, field coordination, cohort engagement, or consortium-based work preferred.

6. Required Competencies

  • Strong understanding of disability-inclusive development and political participation.
  • Ability to design and implement programs with minimal supervision.
  • Strong coordination, facilitation, and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Understanding of budgeting, procurement coordination, and financial compliance.
  • Commitment to safeguarding, ethical conduct, respect, and inclusion

7. Safeguarding & Organizational Values

The Program Officer must adhere to YUWA’s safeguarding, gender equality, disability inclusion, and anti-harassment policies. Ensuring the safety and meaningful participation of young people, including persons with disabilities, is a non-negotiable aspect of the role.

Action for Nepal

AFN is a high performing, community-centric organization building healthy, educated communities in Nepal through effective projects, sound strategies, efficient processes and successful partnerships. AFN is committed to respecting, protecting and promoting internationally recognized human rights including civil and political, economic, social and cultural rights, with particular emphasis on gender equality, the protection of children, people with a disability and the rights of minorities and vulnerable and marginalized groups.

Position overview:

AF Nepal is seeking two qualified and experienced MEAL Associates to support and strengthen project-specific MEAL systems. The MEAL Associates will contribute to results-based monitoring, data collection and management, data quality assurance, analysis, reporting, accountability, learning, and evidence generation across AF Nepal’s projects. They will work closely with project teams to ensure quality data and evidence are systematically generated, documented, and used to inform decision-making, program improvement, accountability, and organizational learning.

Duties and Responsibilities:

A. Monitoring System Implementation

  • Support the Project Officer in implementing field-level activities in line with the project design and M&E framework, ensuring alignment with the theory of change and intended outcomes.
  • Assist in tracking indicators across all outputs and monitoring progress of activities against approved plans.
  • Maintain and regularly update indicator tracking sheets and project databases.
  • Coordinate with district authorities, rural municipalities, health facilities, and other stakeholders to ensure timely and accurate data collection for all project activities.
  • Contribute to the preparation of annual work plans, quarterly activity plans, and detailed activity schedules in coordination with the project team.
  • Plan, implement, and coordinate project activities to ensure quality standards across AFN programs.
  • Participate in joint supervision visits and in MSS assessments.
  • Support data collection and documentation for MSS assessments, facility improvement plans, and supportive supervision.
  • Document MSS findings and track follow-up actions.
  • Ensure activities are implemented effectively and on time in accordance with approved project documents.
  • Assist in the preparation and timely submission of activity reports, quarterly progress reports, and required data as per reporting timelines.
  • Ensure adherence to AFN policies and procedures across all field-level activities.
  • Maintain regular communication with the project team and provide field-level support to program implementation.
  • Coordinate with local stakeholders and contribute to planning for project sustainability.
  • Support to organize and schedule meetings/events, and maintain agendas and minutes.
  • Support program growth and development initiatives.

B. Data Collection, Management, and Documentation

  • Collect and verify data from Municipalities, Health facilities, FCHVs and Community activities
  • Ensure quality data in terms of Accuracy, Completeness, Timeliness
  • Support disability-disaggregated data recording and reporting.
  • Support training and follow-up on HMIS/PAMS reporting and data review and management practices.
  • Conduct regular field visits to monitor project activities, collect data, prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual reports and ensure adherence to project plans.
  • Compile field monitoring findings and Data summaries and visualization.
  • Provide regular and timely updates of the field activities and document the information;
  • Document stories of change, best practices and learning from the project.
  • Ensure quality assurance of the project activities in the district in terms of logistic management, content, delivery of the activities and documentation.
  • Proper documentation of all the relevant references and materials.

C. Safeguarding, Risk management and Inclusion

  • Ensure all project activities comply with the organization’s safeguarding and inclusion policies, including Child Safeguarding, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment (PSEAH), and Gender
  • Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) standards.
  • Contribute to assessing, mitigating and reporting on all risks, including risks of child abuse and exploitation and sexual abuse and exploitation, in the project area.
  • Support the implementation of effective incident reporting mechanisms both within the health centers and in the community.
  • Ensure immediate reporting to AFN of any incident of abuse and exploitation.
  • Follow directives of AFN for follow up required regarding incidents, including reporting to concerned authorities;
  • Ensure safety of survivor, confidentiality and survivor centered approach.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Public Health, Statistics, or related field
  • Minimum 1-2 years of post-qualification experience Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL/M&E).
  • Familiarity with government of Nepal’s HMIS/PAMS systems, Data collection tools and project reporting formats.
  • Experience working with Local governments and Health systems in Nepal.

Required Skills

  • Strong data analysis and skills on statistical tools (KOBO, SPSS, R etc)
  • Excellent computer skills, including Microsoft Office package
  • Ability to work in field settings
  • Good communication skills
  • Analytical and problem-solving ability
  • Report writing and documentation
  • Fluency in Nepali and English

The MEAL Associate may be assigned other reasonable duties and responsibilities by the supervisor or senior management in accordance with AF Nepal’s organizational priorities and program needs.

Shree Latinath Madhyamik Vidyalaya Raskot

NEEDS Nepal is a non-profit, non-governmental a social organization that has been actively working in the social sector for the past 27 years. The organization was established in 1999 as a youth group and has since then engaged in various social transformation, good governance, and development initiatives. NEEDS Nepal is registered with the Government of Nepal and has partnered with numerous government, I/NOGs, bilateral agencies to implement programs that focus on empowerment, socio-economic development, and social transformation for marginalized and vulnerable communities such as children, women, youths, persons with disabilities, Dalit, and Janajati and other marginalized.

Project Brief

NEEDS Nepal, in partnership with Oxfam in Nepal, has been implementing “Strengthening Community Preparedness, Rapid Response and Recovery in Nepal (SCOPR3)”. The project started in January 2024 and will be completed in December 2026. The project is being implemented in 40 different communities disaster management committee (CDMCs) of four municipalities of two districts Beldandi RM, Dodhara-Chandani municipality and Bhimdatta municipality of Kanchanpur and Parshuram municipality of Dadeldhura district. The purpose of this project is to ensure that communities affected by recurrent disasters in highly vulnerable areas have enhanced capacities for disaster preparedness, response, and recovery, and are better equipped to co-lead on relief and recovery efforts in collaboration with local authorities.

NEEDS Nepal is seeking a qualified and dynamic with experience on livelihood and enterprise development candidate for the project.

The summary of ToR is given below:

Job Title: Livelihood and Enterprise Development Officer (LED-Officer)

Location: NEEDS-Nepal Central Office, Kanchanpur

Post holder reports to: Project Coordinator, SCOPR3, NEEDS

People’s management responsibility: Yes; Social mobilizers

Project Name: Strengthening Community Preparedness, Rapid Response and Recovery (SCOPR3)

Project Locations: 40 communities from Parsuram municipality from Dadeldhura district, Bhiagmdatta municipality, Beldandi RM and Dodhara-Chandani municipality from Kanchanpur district.

Job purpose

To strengthen the economic resilience of vulnerable and disaster-prone communities- particularly women-by supporting local enterprise and livelihood development so they become more financially stable and better able to withstand disaster impacts.

Specific task and responsibilities

  • Business Development: Identify and assess potential business opportunities within the community. Facilitate the establishment and growth of enterprises through market research and analysis.
  • Strengthen the Value chain: develop the value chain and strengthen as per enterprise. To promoting the enterprise and create the enabling environment to strengthen the value chain.
  • Organizational Strategy and visioning: Develop the Livelihood and enterprise sector strategy of organization for sustainability. Capacity development livelihood and enterprise resource material preparation.
  • Capacity Building: Provide training and workshops to enhance the skills of entrepreneurs. Offer guidance on business planning, financial management, and marketing strategies.
  • Financial Assistance: Assist in securing funding and financial resources for startup businesses. Collaborate with financial institutions and government agencies to facilitate loans and grants.
  • Networking: Build and maintain relationships with local businesses, government agencies, and non-profit organizations. Connect entrepreneurs with relevant stakeholders and resources.
  • Livelihood Improvement: Implement programs that contribute to the improvement of livelihoods in the community. Focus on sustainable and inclusive economic development initiatives.
  • Monitoring and Evaluation: Develop and implement systems to monitor the progress and impact of enterprise development programs. Evaluate the effectiveness of interventions and make recommendations for improvements.
  • Community Engagement: Engage with the local community to understand their needs and aspirations. Foster a collaborative approach to enterprise development, involving community members in decision-making processes.
  • Market Access: Facilitate access to markets for local products and services. Explore opportunities for partnerships and collaborations to enhance market reach.
  • Sustainability Focus: Promote all dimensions of sustainable business practices (technical, social, environmental, political commitment). Encourage the adoption of ethical and socially responsible business approaches.
  • Data Management: Maintain accurate records and data related to enterprise development programs. Use data for reporting, analysis, and informed decision-making.
  • Educational Initiatives: Develop educational initiatives to enhance the entrepreneurial skills of community members. Encourage a culture of continuous learning and adaptation.
  • Additional: as per immediate requirements and requested by your line manager.

Requirements

  • At least bachelor’s degree in agriculture and relevant to micro-enterprise with having minimum 2 years experiences in micro enterprise and livelihood related projects as a officer/Project Coordinator.
  • Possess working experiences in Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) projects and hold knowledge on correlation between DRR and livelihood will be asset.
  • Good experiences in all aspects of rural sector micro-enterprises development.
  • Report writing skills in English and Nepali both language.
  • Coordination skills with pertinent stakeholders.
  • Basic knowledge on MS office package, and Canva.

Safeguarding & PSEA

NEEDS Nepal has a zero-tolerance policy and approach to any abuse, sexual harassment, or exploitation of, a vulnerable adult or child by any of our staff, volunteers, consultant, and suppliers. All individuals and institutions have committed to respecting the core principles regarding the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the organization safeguarding policy, Zero tolerance Policy, PSEA& code of conduct that is associated with the organization.

NEEDS Nepal has expected from all the staff to share this commitment through Safeguarding, PSEA Policy, and Code of Conduct. All staff must be committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants, or others, are treated with respect and dignity.

How to apply

Qualified & eligible national citizens are highly encouraged to apply with their updated CV along with a motivation letter & expected salary in gross per month to the following email address, hr@needsnepal.org.np by 9th August 2026.

Women, ethnic minorities, and local applicants are highly encouraged to apply. No telephone calls will be entertained and this automatically disqualifies in the recruitment process.

NEEDS Nepal will reserve all rights to make the final decision. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for the further recruitment process. The remuneration and other benefits package shall be as per NEEDS Nepal HRM policy & guidelines.

ROLE SUMMARY

The District Lead is responsible for improving education quality in UWS schools at the district level by working closely with government officials, teachers, and communities to ensure all programme activities
align with UWS Nepal standards. The position holder will coordinate with stakeholders for school construction, ensure smooth implementation of education programmes, coordinate teacher training, and support procurement processes. TheDistrict Lead reviews and approves expenses within their authority and ensures timely submission of documents to the Finance team. In addition, the position holder handles administrative tasks, leads and supervises the district team, and supports HR functions such as developing job descriptions, setting KPIs, and conducting staff performance appraisals with support from the HR Team.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Programme Implementation and Quality Assurance [40%]

  • Lead and oversee implementation of all UWS Nepal programmes in the district, ensuring alignment with organizational strategy, annual plans, and quality standards; monitor progress and troubleshoot implementation challenges.
  •  Provide regular, accurate updates on programme progress, achievements, and challenges to the Senior Education Manager and Executive Director, and promote evidence-based, continuous
    improvement.
  • Lead design and delivery of teacher professional development (pre-service and in-service training), ensuring content is practical, context-sensitive, and aligned with national education priorities; adapt/translate training materials as needed.
  • Mentor and coach Education Officers (EOs), School Mobilizers (SMs), and teachers to strengthen facilitation, classroom practice, and community engagement skills; facilitate peer-learning and
    lesson-sharing among teachers.
  • Track trainer schedules and quarterly training deadlines; monitor classroom practices and schoollevel interventions that contribute to improved student learning outcomes.
  • Maintain accurate records of programme activities, training, and monitoring visits, and use data/feedback to inform decision-making, document lessons learned and refine programme approaches.
  • Monitor school construction progress; coordinate with relevant departments to ensure the timely delivery and stockpiling of construction materials.

2. Government and Stakeholder Engagement [30%]

  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with local government Education Units and other stakeholders to ensure programme alignment with local, provincial, and federal education priorities.
  • Represent UWS Nepal in district-level meetings and coordination forums, in close coordination with the UWS Nepal Board.
  • Strengthen collaboration with School Management Committees (SMCs), Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs), school leaders, and communities to secure partnerships and support programme continuity and sustainability.
  •  Engage local government bodies on school construction, repair, and maintenance activities, and coordinate with other UWS Nepal departments to ensure joined-up engagement with local government.
  •  Coordinate and monitor school construction, renovation, repair, and maintenance projects to ensure quality, timely completion, and compliance with approved standards, budgets, and timelines.
  •  Ensure infrastructure projects meet safety, inclusivity, accessibility, disaster resilience, and environmental standards while maintaining proper documentation and project handover.

3. Financial and Human Resource Leadership (20%)

  • Support preparation of District budgets and work plans; monitor periodic expenditure against approved budgets, providing justification for variances and ensuring alignment with programmematic

Job Title : School Mobilizer
Department : Programmeme
Base Location : Jitpur Simara Municipality, Bara
Reports to : District Lead
Duration : Fixed term until December 2026 with the possibility of extension, subject to satisfactory performance and the availability of funding

ROLE SUMMARY

The School Mobilizer (SM) is responsible for providing field-level support to UWS Nepal supported schools within the assigned cluster. Working under the guidance of the District Lead, the SM serves as the key liaison between schools, communities, and UWS Nepal. The role focuses on supporting the effective implementation of education programmes, strengthening communication and coordination with concerned school stakeholders, collecting and maintaining school data, supporting the use of educational resources and digital tools, and promoting child protection, safeguarding, and inclusive education practices. The SM works collaboratively with schools to identify needs, facilitate support, and strengthen programme implementation.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. School Support and Programme Implementation

  •  Conduct regular visits to assigned schools and maintain positive working relationships with school leadership, teachers, and stakeholders.
  • Support schools in the implementation of UWS education programmes, activities, and initiatives.
  •  Assist schools in the utilization of educational resources, learning materials, and programme tools provided by UWS Nepal.
  •  Identify challenges affecting programme implementation and communicate them to the District Lead for need-based support and follow-up.
  •  Support schools during assessments, events, campaigns,training, and other educational activities as required.

2. Data Collection, Documentation and Reporting

  •  Collect, verify, and maintain school-level data as required by UWS Nepal, including student attendance, enrollment information, assessment, training records, meeting minutes, and other relevant documents.
  •  Maintain accurate records of school visits, activities, observations, and stakeholder engagements.
  •  Support schools in completing required reporting formats and documentation.
  • Submit timely reports and updates to the District Lead according to established reporting schedules.
  •  Ensure confidentiality and safe handling of student and school information.

3. Teacher and School Capacity Support

  •  Facilitate communication between teachers, schools, and theDistrict Lead regarding professional development activities.
  • Support classroom observation processes led by the District Lead and assist with follow-up actions when required.
  •  Encourage participation in teacher training, mentoring, and professional learning opportunities organized by UWS Nepal.
  • Share relevant educational resources, guidance, and information with teachers as directed by the District Lead.

4. Community Engagement and Stakeholder Coordination

  •  Maintain regular communication with School Management Committees (SMCs), Parent Teacher Associations (PTAs), Mothers’ Groups, Child Clubs, School Retention Team, and community
    stakeholders.
  •  Support schools in strengthening parent and community engagement in children’s education.
  •  Follow up with families of students identified by schools as having attendance or participation concerns.

5. Child Protection, Safeguarding and Inclusion

  • Promote awareness and implementation of UWS Nepal’s Child Protection, Safeguarding, and Inclusion Policies at the school level.
  •  Immediately report child protection or safeguarding concerns through established organizational reporting mechanisms.
  •  Support the identification and referral of children who may require additional support or protection services.
  •  Assist in maintaining records related to safeguarding cases in accordance with confidentiality requirements.
  • Promote inclusive practices that support the participation of all learners regardless of gender, disability, ethnicity, language, or socio-economic background.

6. Coordination and Other Responsibilities

  • Participate in team meetings, training sessions, planning workshops, and review meetings.
  •  Foster positive relationships with local government representatives and education stakeholders.
  • Carry out other education-related duties assigned by the District Lead that are consistent with the purpose of the role.

EXPERIENCE, KNOWLEDGE AND COMPETENCIES

  • At least intermediate level (10+2) in Education, Social Sciences, Development Studies, or relate field(s).
  •  Minimum of 1 year’s working experience with schools, communities, educational projects, or development programmes.
  •  Understanding of Nepal’s education system and local education governance structures, including SMCs and PTAs.
  •  Good understanding of child protection and safeguarding.
  •  Strong communication, facilitation, and interpersonal skills.
  •  Ability to build and maintain positive relationships with school and community stakeholders.
  •  Experience in data collection, documentation, and report preparation.
  • Basic digital literacy and ability to use mobile applications, databases, spreadsheets, and online reporting systems.
  •  Ability to travel regularly to assigned cluster schools.
  •  Good problem-solving and organizational skills.
  •  Fluency in Nepali, working knowledge of English is an asset

Project: Educated, Empowered, and Thriving Girls for a Safe and Inclusive Society and Sponsorship communication program
Duty Station: JSDP. Sindhuli field office, Kamalamai-6, Sindhuli

Expertise: Bachelor’s Degree in Business Management, Finance, Accountancy and other relevant field with 3 years of working experience in the development sector i.e. NGO/INGO of relevant field.
Reports to: Project Coordinator
Accountable to: Board of JSDP Sindhuli

Janajati Society Development Program, Sindhuli (JSDP) is a district based non-profit making development organization. JSDP is registered under Organization Registration Act 2034, in 2064 at District Administration Office, Sindhuli. Janajati Society Development Program (JSDP) Sindhuli has been working in the different developmental initiatives for sustainable development at Sindhuli district, since its establishment. It is established for the socio- economic improvement of the deprived, socially excluded, and marginalized people of the district. Janajati Society Development Program, Sindhuli (JSDP) foresees a rightful, gender equitable and socially inclusive society where peace, progress and prosperity are established.

Project Introduction:

The “Educated, Empowered and Thriving Girls for a Safe and Inclusive Society in Sindhuli” is a consortium project with Plan International Nepal, HANDS Nepal and JSDP, Sindhuli for two years focusing Education and ECD, and Protection as themes, and youth empowerment, climate crisis, WASH and humanitarian as cross cutting themes. It targets public schools and marginalized communities of 33 wards from six local governments (LGs) of Sindhuli districts, which starts on July 2026 and will end on June 2028. The project adapts the learnings from previous projects and focuses to enable children, adolescents, and youth especially girls from marginalized communities in Sindhuli District to access quality, safe, inclusive, and gender-responsive education, to get support for transition to home to schools, to thrive in a safe, non-violence and non-discriminative environments and to nurture through parenting education, thereby reducing child, early, and forced marriage (CEFM) and supporting a dignified transition to adulthood. To enable children, adolescents, and youth, especially girls from marginalized and vulnerable communities in Sindhuli District, the project will focus;

  • To improve equitable access to quality, inclusive and child-friendly ECED and school education through strengthened learning environments, teacher capacity, child participation and family engagement.
  • To strengthen nurturing care, positive parenting and nutrition practices that promote holistic early childhood development and school readiness.
  • To strengthen community-based child protection systems and promote gender equality through increased awareness, participation and prevention of violence, GBV and child, early and forced marriage.
  • To strengthen the capacity of local governments and stakeholders to develop, implement and institutionalize evidence-based education, ECED and child protection policies, plans and budgets.

Major Responsibilities:

A. Finance related (30%)

  • Support to prepare the bank reconciliation statement.
  • Advance Settlement documents review and settle, Payment requests reviews, requests for additional information, and ensure that payments with the Finance team continue to move through proscribed process.

  • Support to conduct annual physical inventory check.
  • Maintain the stock register and supervise office assistant to make sure it is regularly updated in coordination with the Office Assistants, as required.
  • Responsible for making hotel reservations for all events according to the requirement.
  • Assist the board and finance for the Procurement and Operations, in coordinating with the concerned team.
  • Supervise facilities management, and ensure overall office maintenance, including electronics, furniture and fixtures.
  • Ensure that all utility bills, vehicle tax & renewal are done within due date and submit a quarterly utility and communications report to finance, Admin and Procurement, updating progress.
  • Monitoring performance of the staff as per policy and agreement.

Position Title: Junior Technical Assistant (JTA) – Agriculture
No. of Vacancy: 1
Grade: A1
Vacancy No.: 02/2083/084
Project: Youth Empowerment for Transformation and Innovation (YETI) Project
Duty Station: HANDS Nepal, Field office Sindhulimadi (with 70% field visit to project area)
Contact type: One year with the possibility of extension
Working Area: Sindhuli district
Responsible to: District Project Coordinator (DPC), HANDS Nepal YETI Project.

Background

Human & National Development Society (HANDS) Nepal, established in 2001, is a non- governmental, non-political, non-profit organization focused on integrated community development and natural resource management. With a vision of a prosperous, equitable, and ethical society, HANDS Nepal’s mission is to implement initiatives fostering inclusive and equitable development. For over 25 years, the organization has promoted sustainable development, addressing areas such as governance, education, child rights, WASH, climate change, disaster risk reduction, health, and livelihoods. HANDS Nepal aims to empower marginalized groups, particularly women, children, and Dalits, to access basic needs and lead dignified lives. Through partnerships with multiple agencies and over 42 projects impacting more than 200,000 people across thirteen districts, HANDS Nepal strengthens local governments, promotes participatory governance, and ensures marginalized communities can shape their futures.

Project: Youth Empowerment for Transformation and Innovation (YETI) Project

HANDS Nepal, Sindhuli has been working in a long-term partnership with Plan International Nepal since 2012. Currently, the organization is collaborating with Plan International Nepal to implement the Youth Empowerment for Transformation and Innovationn (YETI) Project. The project goal is Economic empowerment of young girl, adolescent women and marginalized youths driving inclusive, climate-resilient, and market-driven economies. The planned intervention will be reaching to young people from targeted communities. The project will work equipping young people with the knowledge, skills, and confidence needed to initiate and manage sustainable business enterprises. It emphasizes fostering an entrepreneurial mindset that enables youth to identify, develop, and scale innovative business ideas aligned with emerging local market opportunities. Likewise, the project will work on strengthening and institutionalizing enterprise development support systems that enable youths to access business development and support services for entrepreneurship, and business growth. The aim is to strengthen a coherent, accessible, and sustainable support ecosystem that systematically connects youth with enterprise development services and markets. Similarly, the project focuses on enabling young people particularly young women and marginalized youth to access and effectively use appropriate financial services that support their transition from training to sustainable entrepreneurship.

Furthermore, focuses on building a policy and institutional ecosystem that enables youth especially young women and marginalized groups to thrive as entrepreneurs and innovators.

General Responsibilities

The Technical Assistant – Agriculture is responsible for providing field-level technical assistance to farmers/youth entrepreneurs to improve agricultural productivity, climate-resilient farming practices, agribusiness development and market linkages. The position supports the implementation of project activities related to crop production, extension services, demonstrations, capacity building, monitoring, and coordination with local governments and private sectors to promote sustainable and market-oriented agriculture.

Key Responsibilities

1. Agriculture Production and Technical Support

  • Support farmers/youth entrepreneurs in selecting suitable crops and agricultural enterprises.
  • Provide field-level technical support on the production of vegetables, spices, fruits, and other high-value crops by promoting Good Agricultural Practices, improved crop management techniques, quality seed use, and efficient input utilization.
  • Conduct regular field visits to monitor crop performance and provide timely technical advice.
  • Support in adopting improved irrigation methods, crop diversification, post-harvest management, and value addition practices to enhance productivity and profitability.
  • Provide regular technical coaching and mentoring to strengthen their technical knowledge and practical skills.

2. Agribusiness and Enterprise Development

  • Support youth entrepreneurs in preparing agribusiness plans, enterprise development plans, and investment proposals for agricultural enterprises.
  • Assist farmers in conducting basic cost-benefit analyses, gross margin calculations, enterprise budgeting, and farm record keeping to improve farm profitability and business decision-making.
  • Promote market-oriented production systems, value addition, grading, packaging, storage, and collective marketing to enhance farmers’ income.
  • Facilitate linkages between farmers, cooperatives, input suppliers, financial institutions, buyers, and other market actors to strengthen agricultural value chains.

3. Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Coordinate with Municipal Agriculture Sections, Ward Offices, agricultural service providers, cooperatives, community organizations, private input suppliers, and other relevant stakeholders for effective implementation of agricultural activities.
  • Support farmers/youth entrepreneurs in implementing project activities according to approved work plans.
  • Participate in municipal coordination meetings, agricultural campaigns, exhibitions, and stakeholder consultations as required by the project.

4. Documentation and Reporting

  • Prepare monthly progress reports, field visit reports, training reports, success stories, case studies, lessons learned, and other documentation required by the project.
  • Develop and update seasonal agricultural calendars and IEC materials to support project implementation.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Diploma in Agriculture or 10+2 in Agriculture (JTA) from a recognized institution.
  • Minimum one (1) year of relevant professional experience for Diploma holders or three (3) years for JTA in agricultural extension, crop production, farmer training, or agriculture and rural development projects.
  • Prior experience working with NGOs and/or INGOs will be considered an added advantage.

Core Competencies and Skills

  • Strong technical knowledge of crop production and soil management.
  • Community facilitation and coordination skills.
  • Proficiency in MS Word, Excel, documentation and reporting

Safeguarding and GESI Commitment

  • Demonstrated commitment to safeguarding, child protection, gender equality, disability inclusion, social inclusion, environmental sustainability, and compliance with Plan International and HANDS Nepal safeguarding and GESI policies.

Other Conditions

  • The organization reserves the right to assign additional responsibilities relevant to the position and project needs.

General Responsibilities

The incumbent will improve livestock productivity, youth employment, entrepreneurship, value chain, climate-resilient livestock farming, and market linkage through technical guidance, capacity building, and close coordination with government stakeholders and private sector actors.

Key Responsibilities

1. Technical Planning

  • Support the PC in developing periodic project implementation plans, including annual, quarterly, and monthly work plans, to ensure the timely and effective delivery of livestock development interventions.
  • Develop and implement an annual fodder development and management plan to ensure the sustainable production and distribution of forage grasses for feed availability and improving livestock productivity.
  • Promote improved livestock management practices by encouraging farming households through technical awareness, demonstration, and extension support.
  • Plan, provide technical supervision, and support the construction and improvement of animal-friendly goat sheds using locally available materials and appropriate technologies to improve animal welfare, disease prevention, and farm productivity.
  • Develop transparent and technically sound beneficiary and livestock selection criteria in coordination with the Project Coordinator, local governments and other stakeholders, and facilitate the fair and accountable distribution of goats and other livestock support.

  • Develop technical specifications and selection criteria for improved breed livestock, provide technical support during procurement processes to ensure the acquisition of healthy and quality breeding stock, and facilitate for the transparent and accountable distribution of livestock.

3. Coordination, partnership and Linkages

  • Serve as a technical liaison between livestock entrepreneurs, private sectors and local government authorities to improve access to quality livestock inputs and services.
  • Coordinate with insurance companies to facilitate livestock insurance services, including raising awareness, policy enrollment, claim verification, documentation, and settlement of compensation in cases of livestock mortality.
  • Conduct regular monitoring, field supervision, and follow-up visits to assess the quality and progress of project implementation.
  • Facilitate and strengthen livestock entrepreneurship development to ensure farmers/youth entrepreneurs receive timely technical assistance and quality veterinary services.

4. Documentation and Reporting

  • Prepare and submit monthly technical and progress reports in a timely manner.
  • Actively participate in monthly, quarterly, and other review, planning, coordination, and learning meetings.

  • Experienced in livestock commercialization
  • Proven experience working with youth and women entrepreneurs.

Core Competencies and Skills

Self-motivated and proactive

Position: Programme Coordinator (PC)
Project: Educated, Empowered, and Thriving Girls for a Safe and Inclusive Society and Sponsorship Communication Program
Duty Station: Project Office of JSDP, Sindhuli at Kamalamai-6, Sindhuli
Working area: Target LGs of Sindhuli district
Contract type: 11 month and possible to extension
Expertise: Master’s Degree in Art or Education or other relevant field and three years of experience in relevant field in I/NGO such as protection, education, ECD and campaign. or Bachelor Degree in Art or Education or other relevant field and seven years of experience in relevant field in I/NGO.
Responsible: to JSDP, Sindhuli Focal Person or Chair Person and Project Lead of Partner organization Janajati Society Development Program (JSDP), Sindhuli

Janajati Society Development Program, Sindhuli (JSDP) is a district based non-profit making development organization. JSDP is registered under Organization Registration Act 2034, in 2064 at District Administration Office, Sindhuli. Janajati Society Development Program (JSDP) Sindhuli has been working in the different developmental initiatives for sustainable development at Sindhuli district, since its establishment. It is established for the socio- economic improvement of the deprived, socially excluded, and marginalized people of the district. Janajati Society Development Program, Sindhuli (JSDP) foresees a rightful, gender equitable and socially inclusive society where peace, progress and prosperity are established.

Project Introduction:

The “Educated, Empowered and Thriving Girls for a Safe and Inclusive Society in Sindhuli” is a consortium project with Plan International Nepal, HANDS Nepal and JSDP, Sindhuli for two years focusing Education and ECD, and Protection as themes, and youth empowerment, climate crisis, WASH and humanitarian as cross cutting themes. It targets public schools and marginalized communities of 33 wards from six local governments (LGs) of Sindhuli districts, which starts on July 2026 and will end on June 2028. The project adapts the learnings from previous projects and focuses to enable children, adolescents, and youth especially girls from marginalized communities in Sindhuli District to access quality, safe, inclusive, and gender-responsive education, to get support for transition to home to schools, to thrive in a safe, non-violence and non-discriminative environments and to nurture through parenting education, thereby reducing child, early, and forced marriage (CEFM) and supporting a dignified transition to adulthood. To enable children, adolescents, and youth, especially girls from marginalized and vulnerable communities in Sindhuli District, the project will focus;

  • To improve equitable access to quality, inclusive and child-friendly ECED and school education through strengthened learning environments, teacher capacity, child participation and family engagement.
  • To strengthen nurturing care, positive parenting and nutrition practices that promote holistic early childhood development and school readiness.
  • To strengthen community-based child protection systems and promote gender equality through increased awareness, participation and prevention of violence, GBV and child, early and forced marriage.
  • To strengthen the capacity of local governments and stakeholders to develop, implement and institutionalize evidence-based education, ECED and child protection policies, plans and budgets.

Purpose of the Position

The Program Coordinator (PC) is responsible for leading the project, which includes technical expertise on protection, education, pre-school campaign and sponsorship communication. S/he has to mobilize JSDP’s team and effective collaborate with HANDS Nepal and Plan International Nepal. Program Coordinator provides technical, conceptual and strategic support to JSDP Sindhuli for program cycle management in planning, implementing and monitoring “Educated, Empowered, and Thriving Girls for a Safe and Inclusive Society in Sindhuli” and “Sponsorship Communication Program”, following child centered community development, right based approach and gender transformative approach. S/he will ensure successful completion of all program activities implemented and ensure achievement through empowering the community groups, children, youth, women, girls and boys, children/people with disability in their self-led development approach.

The position holder ensures the quality of program delivery and the achievement of agreed outcomes in accordance with program design and partnership. The position holder will also lead on influence work approach in program implementation, ensuring support to children, youth and young women groups. S/he is accountable for leading the innovation and ensuring lessons learnt are constantly integrated in program interventions, thus continuously improving efficiency and effectiveness. S/he also leads the local level networking and advocacy in support of the board members and staff team.

DETAILED OBJECTIVES AND TASKS

Implementation, Coordination and Leadership (30%)

  • Coordinate with district line agencies, local government authorities (Rural/Municipality), communities and all local stakeholders to run the program smoothly.
  • Ensuring continuous communication and sharing project information with right holders and communities’ representatives regarding the implementation of works and in order to ensure a flawless progress of activities.
  • Liaise with all project staffs to ensure that project interventions in timely with concrete project plan and budget as per finalized project documents.
  • Develop strategies and plans that contribute to raising profile of working organization.
  • Develop capacity of project team, right holders and stakeholders by conducting or using resource person on technical training based on project theme.
  • Liaise with the different organization implementing the similar project for effective implementation of the project and also to avoid the duplication of the events.
  • Support and monitoring of construction work and mobilize PO for technical aspect of construction works both new and repair & maintenance works in schools and communities.
  • To support in preparing the tender documents and open it concerning the materials are of the construction materials.
  • Influence local government for ownership of intervention and reflect good practices and learning in policy and plan.

Program Management (25%)

  • Responsible for the risk management, guidance, staff management during project implementation in the target locations.
  • Responsible for developing Detail Implementation Plan (DIP), tools and approaches of project management based on the organizational operational policies and guidelines as well as donor agencies.
  • Ensure for managing the minimum standards of technical quality and services in all interventions of project activities.
  • Promote women entrepreneurship, skill development of women ensuring most vulnerable and marginalized groups are included.
  • Ensure that cross cutting issues like GESI, Child Protection and equity are mainstreamed.
  • Ensure gender transformative approach of the project as per gender transformative marker of Plan International Nepal.

Financial Management (15%)

  • Lead the financial management of project including budget planning, monitoring and revision.
  • Manage the project budget and ensure project expenditures are in-line with agreed project plan and budget.
  • Ensure that project expenditures are undertaken in-line with financial policies and procedures and that available resource are optimally utilized.
  • Identify program supplies needs and coordinate with the logistics team to put in place a sensible phased procurement plan.

Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting (15%)

  • Conduct effective monitoring of each activity regularly which ensure to meet the goal and outcome of the project.
  • Update, operationalize and lead in the systematic evaluation strategy in order to ensure the effective implementation of projects activities as per DIP.
  • Plan proper data management to keep track of the Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) plan of project and ensuring this links to reporting requirements.
  • Work with the team to identify and document project learning and success stories and disseminate learning across the sector.
  • Ensure to catch the project reporting deadline and timely reporting to donor agencies through line manager.
  • Ensure effective communication between the organization, project teams and report immediately on any new developments, changes, financial aspects and important decisions and directives.
  • To conduct frequent field visits, focus group discussions and key informant interviews based on the project objectives to track the project.

Team leadership and supervisory Role (10%)

  • Supervise project officers, associates, and supervisor provide guidance on project management
  • Identify capacity gap and support for capacity building of project team as requirement of projects
  • Ensure projects are implemented within scope, budget and time through mobilization of project team and consortium member as per requirement.
  • Support JSDP for hiring/recruitment process of staffs and experts including JD preparation, hiring process and recruitment
  • Ensure supervisees’ performance appraisal as per HR policy of JSDP, Sindhuli
  • Provide inducation to newly recruit staffs on organization and project
  • Carry out others administrative works as supervisor.

Safeguarding Children and Program Participants (5%)

  • Act as a focal person of safeguarding of children and program participant for JSDP Sindhuli.
  • Assess safeguarding risk of the project/program and prepare their mitigation plan
  • Ensure proper safeguarding mechanism in project/program delivery with proper reporting mechanism.
  • Support JSDP and partner for safeguarding response and reporting mechanism as per requirement.

Competence (Expertise, Skills and Desirables)

  • Qualification and Experience: Master’s Degree in Art or Education or other relevant field and three years of experience in relevant field in I/NGO such as protection, education, ECD and campaign. or Bachelor Degree in Art or Education or other relevant field and seven years of experience in relevant field in I/NGO.
  • Project cycle management: Planning, Budgeting, Implementation, M&E and reporting.
  • Strategic: Analytical, Critical thinking, negotiating skills, Innovative. creativity, problem solving and ability to build effective relations for influencing and team work.
  • Attitude and behavior: Respect and promote marginalized people; men/women, boy /girls, youth and young women and recognize their capabilities and ideas. Takes responsibility for social change, gender sensitive and transparent. Strives for quality in all they do, respecting deadlines and working continuously to improve performance. Takes responsibility for their actions, and learn from behavior, successes and failures. Supports gender equality, diversity and multi-sociocultural and challenges forms of inequality or harassment.
  • Language: Ability to write clearly and concisely in English and Nepali.
  • Communication: Sound communication skills, managing work relationships (internal/external), coordination and networking.
  • Proven IT skills: Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, open access M&E tools and skill of computer applications.
  • Female, Dalit, Adibashi/Janajati and Madeshi candidates are strongly recommended to apply.

Level of Contact with Children and Program Participants: High

Application Procedure

If eligible, drop your CV with cover letter to HR Department of JSDP Sindhuli within 7 days office hour of notice publication (no later than 7 August, 2026) to jsdp_vacancy@jsdpsindhuli.org.np or Documents can be submitted in office of JSDP Sindhuli kamalamai-6, Ratmata Sindhuli in office hour within the mentioned time frame. If the last day of application falls on public holiday, the application can be submitted on the next day as well.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for the next stage of the selection process. Requested to submit updated CV including cover letter clearly mentioning the position applying in the subject line. No telephone inquiries will be entertained and any inappropriate recommendation might automatically disqualify the candidate from further processing. JSDP Sindhuli respects child rights and strictly follows the child protection policy of the organization.

JSDP Sindhuli is an equal opportunities employer and strictly follows the merit-based selection. Qualified female candidates or those from disadvantaged communities are strongly encouraged to apply.

JSDP Sindhuli reserves right to qualify/disqualify applications in any case.

Female, Dalit, Adibashi, Janajati, Person with Disability candidates are strongly recommended to apply.
