Captivating Nepal is a non-profit organization dedicated to breaking the cycle of poverty and fostering long-term community development by empowering marginalized groups, with a primary focus on women and children. Through core interventions in education, healthcare, anti-trafficking, and sustainable livelihoods, the organization works to build resilient and self-reliant communities. A key initiative, the Captivating Village Program (CVP), helps out-of-school children, particularly vulnerable girls, re-enroll and complete their education by providing essential support. To ensure sustainable impact, CVP enhances classroom quality through teacher training, mitigates human trafficking risks by expanding economic and educational opportunities, and offers family livelihood and skill-building programs to achieve financial independence for women and youth. Additionally, Captivating Nepal addresses holistic well-being by conducting child health camps and psychosocial screenings to respond to critical child and adolescent mental health needs across its project areas.

Position: Program Officer

Required number of position: 1

Duty Station: Gaththaghar, Bhaktapur (50% field visits to project sites)

Expected Start Date: As soon as possible

Contract Type: 12 months (3 months’ probation period)

Report to: Program Manager

Job purpose

The Program Officer who will be responsible for the effective planning, implementation, and monitoring of Captivating Nepal’s programs activities in the project site. The Program Officer will ensure the successful delivery of education, healthcare, women’s empowerment, and livelihood support initiatives, aimed at addressing key challenges such as school dropouts, human trafficking, and gender inequality. The role requires coordinating program activities, managing partnerships, overseeing project staffs, and ensuring alignment with organizational goals. The Program Officer will also contribute to improving the quality of education, promoting skill development, supporting sustainable livelihoods, and addressing child and adolescent mental health concerns, ultimately contributing to the empowerment and well-being of marginalized communities.

Roles and Responsibilities

1. Program Planning and Coordination:

  • Develop, implement, and manage the overall strategy and action plans for the Captivating Village Program across all project sites
  • Ensure alignment of program activities with Captivating Nepal’s mission and goals, ensuring a holistic approach to education, healthcare, women’s empowerment, and sustainable livelihoods.
  • Conduct needs assessment, prepare report and design the program activities based on the assessment.
  • Prepare Detailed Implementation Plan (DIP) for the project and regularly follow up with the progress made based on the DIP prepared.
  • Coordinate with local government authorities, community leaders, and stakeholders to ensure smooth program execution and adherence to local needs.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with local communities, schools, women’s groups, and other stakeholders to ensure active participation and support.

2. Program Implementation:

  • Oversee the day-to-day implementation of program activities at all project sites, ensuring high-quality delivery and timely completion.
  • Facilitate the return of school dropouts to education and ensure continued educational support for vulnerable children, especially girls.
  • Lead the design and delivery of skill development and income-generating activities for out-of-school youth and marginalized communities.
  • Ensure the integration of child and adolescent mental health initiatives, including health camps and psychosocial screenings.

3. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting:

  • Establish and maintain a robust monitoring and evaluation framework to track program progress, outcomes, and impact.
  • Regularly assess the effectiveness of the program and suggest improvements to meet objectives and address any emerging challenges.
  • Collect, analyze, and report data on program activities, achievements, and challenges to management, stakeholders, and donors.
  • Prepare and submit timely progress reports, ensuring accurate documentation of all activities, lessons learned, and key outcomes.

4. Capacity Building and Staff Management:

  • Supervise and provide guidance to program staff, volunteers, and field teams to ensure effective execution of program activities.
  • Organize and conduct regular training and capacity-building sessions for staff and local partners to enhance their skills and knowledge.

5. Community Engagement and Stakeholder Management:

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with local communities, schools, women’s groups, and other stakeholders to ensure active participation and support.
  • Foster partnerships with local authorities, NGOs, and other organizations to amplify the impact of the program.
  • Conduct outreach activities and awareness campaigns to educate communities about the importance of education, health, and women’s empowerment.

6. Financial Management and Resource Mobilization:

  • Manage program budgets and resources effectively, ensuring funds are allocated and used according to project plans and donor requirements.
  • Ensure the timely disbursement of funds for program activities, ensuring transparency and accountability.
  • Identify funding opportunities and assist in the development of proposals to secure resources for program sustainability.

7. Program Sustainability and Impact:

  • Ensure the sustainability of program activities through the development of long-term strategies, partnerships, and local ownership.
  • Facilitate exit strategies for phased-out activities, ensuring communities continue to benefit from the program after its conclusion.
  • Ensure a gender-sensitive approach and promote the inclusion of marginalized and vulnerable groups in all program activities.

8. Child Protection and Safeguarding:

  • Ensure that all program activities adhere to child protection and safeguarding policies.

Qualification, experience, and skills requirements:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Social Science, Education or relevant field. Master’s will be an advantage
  • Minimum of three years of experience in the Education, Anti-human trafficking, Livelihood, Agriculture and or related field.
  • Experience on Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) approach will be an added advantage.
  • Fully proficient in MS-Office Package, Outlook and Skype and various data collection application and software.
  • Prior experience in performing Needs Assessment, Base Line and End line survey and report preparation and dissemination.
  • Excellent reporting and financial management knowledge
  • Excellent donor communication and reporting capabilities
  • Willingness to travel mostly at the rural sites and engage with the communities to identify needs and resources

Position: Field Mobilizer

Required number of position: 1 (Local female residents are highly encouraged to apply)

Duty Station: Ganeshman Charnath Municipality, Dhanusha, Madhesh Province

Expected Start Date: As soon as possible

Contract Type: 12 months (3 months’ probation period)

Job Purpose

The Field Mobilizer will lead day-to-day community-level activities, focusing on Education, women’s empowerment, and sustainable livelihood programs (including poultry farming). He/She will build strong relationships with local beneficiaries, community leaders, and local government stakeholders to ensure smooth project implementation, effective monitoring, and impactful storytelling

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Lead and facilitate field level community activities, ensuring project objectives are met smoothly and effectively.
  • Drive livelihood programs tailored for women and families, providing regular coaching, follow-up, and practical guidance.
  • Oversee community poultry farming initiatives, offering advice on livestock health, proper maintenance, and business growth.
  • Assist beneficiaries in developing local marketing strategies and establishing trade links to sell their poultry and local goods successfully.

  • Follow up of the implemented activities and provide feedback and suggestion to the beneficiaries.

Motivation, Team Work, Strategic Vision, Effective Communication, Pressure Handling, Organizing and Planning, Adaptability and Flexibility, Innovation and Creativity, Analytical Capacity, Care and Respect.

Job Description

Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers
Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

While climate change is observed across Nepal, the rate of temperature increase is more pronounced at higher altitudes. This temperature rise accelerates the rate of glacial retreat, increasing the size of glacial lakes located in these high-altitude areas and, in turn, their likelihood of breaching in the form of Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOF) which cause severe flooding, landslides and mudflows that damage infrastructure and private assets, and disrupt transportation networks, agricultural production, power supplies from hydropower plants and tourism activities. Damages from GLOFs are often irreparable for decades, with considerable economic costs, particularly to downstream populations. The risk of GLOFs is further exacerbated by increasing temperatures which increase the rate of snow and ice melt and the proportion of precipitation falling as rain, which increases the volume of the lakes, thereby reducing the amount of ‘freeboard’, which increases the likelihood of overflow and the intensity of resulting floods.

The Thulagi, Lower Barun, Lumding Tsho and Hongu 2 Lakes are at exceptionally high risk of breaching having already exhibited considerable increases in volume, accelerated degradation of their ice-cored moraines, and a reduced amount of ‘freeboard’ as a result of climate change. Combined, these factors have destabilized the lakes, exposing the Gandaki Basin and the Dudhkoshi and Arun Sub-basins to the threat of a GLOF event. Without intervention, these glacial lakes could breach at any given moment, adversely impacting vulnerable Nepalese communities.

In response to this risk, USD36 millions of GCF funds, alongside USD14 million in cofinance, will be directed to reduce the risk and impacts of GLOFs at the four priority glacial lakes by shifting towards a proactive approach to GLOF risk reduction in Nepal. The proposed project presents an integrated approach to GLOF risk management in Nepal by addressing institutional and technical capacities, physical protection (both grey and green infrastructure approaches), hazard monitoring and early warning. This integrated approach will utilise GCF funds to: i) lower the water levels of four glacial lakes to reduce their risk of breaching; ii) implement Eco-Disaster Risk Reduction interventions in mountain ecosystems to mitigate the residual flood impacts from a GLOF; iii) establish and implement early warning systems to alleviate damages and prevent the loss of lives from GLOFs; and iv) strengthen the technical and institutional capacity of Nepal’s Department of Hydrology and Meteorology to plan for and respond to GLOFs and floods. These interventions will catalyse a shift from a need- and project-based approach towards proactive and pre-emptive approaches, engendered through strengthened capacity among institutions and communities.

The project will be implemented following UNDP’s support to National Implementation Modality (NIM), with Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM) under Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation (MoEWRI) of Nepal serving as the Implementing Partner. Under this modality, UNDP is supporting DHM in recruiting key positions for the establishment of a Project Management Unit, which will be based in Kathmandu, Nepal. Members of the PMU will collectively be responsible for overall planning and budgeting, collaborating with other ministries, sectors and government entities to implement the project performance management system; bidding for the provision of project consultancy services; coordination with the responsible parties in terms of bidding of goods and services; disbursement and implementation of project audits, operation of accounts, monitoring and preparation of overall project reports (annual), and safeguards policy monitoring reports.

Duties and Responsibilities

The DRR/M-EWS Analyst will ensure that the project’s multi-hazard EWS interventions are technically sound, socially inclusive, and institutionally sustainable. Service providers will design and install systems, while the Analyst ensures quality assurance, coordination, and integration into national DRR frameworks.

Provide technical oversight of EWS design:

  • Oversee interventions related to the generation and dissemination of early warnings, verifying quality of materials, techniques, and final finishes.
  • Review and validate EWS designs, SOPs, and protocols.
  • Ensure early warnings are inclusive and reach vulnerable communities.
  • In collaboration with the Hydrological and Meteorological experts, support the technical and institutional capacity development of DHM to produce early warnings and disseminate them to government agencies and productive sectors.
  • Oversee the development of community-based response plans, multi-hazard-based risk assessments (integrating community knowledge and science-based assessments), and training of communities on disaster risk management.
  • Oversee the development of climate-responsive Municipal Disaster Preparedness and Response Plans.

Oversee system installation and operation:

  • In collaboration with the Hydrological and Meteorological experts, monitor and guide contractors during installation and commissioning of EWS components.
  • Certify deliverables and ensure proper documentation for payments.

Contribute to knowledge management and build institutional and community capacity:

  • Conduct training for government personnel and community groups.
  • Support drills, simulations, and awareness campaigns.
  • Develop knowledge and awareness material on access and response to early warnings, including for the establishment and mobilisation of youth groups and volunteer’s corps.
  • Document good practices and lessons for replication.

Oversight and reporting:

  • Certify completion and quality of works related to the installation and operation of hydrological equipment, ensuring documentation is in place for payments, handovers, and audit requirements.
  • Maintain equipment records, compile periodic technical reports, and provide updates to PMU/PIU in line with UNDP/GON/GEF standards.
  • Ensure that all project data and information on physical and financial progress related to DRM and EWS systems are duly maintained with transparently, expediently, and effectively in line with UNDP rules and regulations
  • Contribute to annual workplans and budgeting within the PMU as related to DRM and EWS systems, applying adaptive management principles.
  • Monitor the progress of DRM and EWS interventions according to annual work plan, ensuring that targets are fully met and the reporting requirements are fulfilled, and provide technical inputs to donor reports and evaluations.
  • Contribute to the inclusion of EWS in Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs).

Ensure Gender and Social inclusion considerations in the project and facilitate knowledge sharing

  • Mainstream GESI considerations in disaster risk reduction (DRR) and early warning systems (EWS) by ensuring risk assessments, preparedness, and response strategies address the specific needs of women, men, youth, elderly persons, persons with disabilities, and marginalized communities.
  • Strengthen inclusive participation by engaging diverse community groups—including women’s groups, disability organizations, and indigenous representatives—in the design, testing, and dissemination of community based EWS and DRR interventions.
  • Ensure accessibility of information and communication systems by developing and promoting gender- and disability-responsive early warning messages in local languages and formats that are understandable and usable by all.
  • Collect and utilize sex, age, and disability disaggregated data to identify differential vulnerabilities and capacities, ensuring evidence-based recommendations for inclusive DRR and climate resilience planning.
  • Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners.

Disaster Information Management System (DIMS) and Data Management for Early Warning Systems

  • Lead and support the planning, development, and operationalization of a Disaster Information Management System (DIMS) to systematically manage data generated from Early Warning Systems (EWS), hydrometeorological monitoring, risk assessments, and community-based DRM interventions.
  • Establish data management frameworks, standards, and protocols to ensure the consistent collection, validation, storage, analysis, visualization, and dissemination of disaster risk and early warning data in line with national systems and international best practices.
  • Ensure interoperability and integration of EWS-related data with existing national platforms and information systems of the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM) and other relevant government entities.
  • Support the development of dashboards, decision-support tools, and reporting mechanisms to enable timely, evidence-based decision-making for preparedness, response, and anticipatory action.
  • The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation

Institutional Arrangement

The PMU will be headed by the Project Coordination Specialist (PCS). The Disaster Risk Reduction/Management and Early Warning System Analyst will report directly to the Project Coordination Specialist. The PMU will operate under the overall guidance of the National Project Director (NPD) — as assigned by MoEWRI.

Posiiton: Private Sector Engagement Specialist
Location: Kathmandu, with frequent field travel

About Mercy Corps

Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible. In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions into action – helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within. Now, and for the future. Mercy Corps has been operating in Nepal since 2005, implementing programs in food security, agriculture, market development, financial services, youth engagement, climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction. We take a systems-based approach in our programming, with the aim of improving the lives and potential of vulnerable individuals and communities across Nepal.

Program/Department Summary

The Zurich Climate Resilience Alliance (ZCRA) is an alliance of nine organizations including international NGOs, private sector, and academic organizations, who have come together with the support of the Zurich Foundation to drive better policy and practice to reduce the negative impact of floods on peoples’ and communities’ ability to thrive.

The Alliance is implementing a 12-year vision through 2025. The current phase (phase 3, 2024-2027) represents the first cycle of this long-term vision. Previously, the Alliance completed its first phase in 2018, and its second phase in December 2023 and third phase will run till Dec 2027. During this time, The Alliance works together to achieve 12-year vision by implementing solutions, promoting good practice, influencing policy and facilitating systemic change. In Nepal, the Alliance is comprised of Mercy Corps and Practical Action, working together on joint outcomes aiming at:

Building ex-ante resilience of communities at risk of flood and heat impacts across Nepal
Improving early warning and early action in advance of probable hazards
Enabling people who experience livelihoods losses due to floods and heat to recover quickly through compensation and/or insurance

General Position Summary

The Private Sector Engagement Specialist will provide strategic and technical leadership to map, design, pilot, institutionalize, and scale private sector engagement, climate-resilient enterprise development, and climate risk financing interventions under the Climate Resilient Communities (CRC) Programme. The expert will work closely with governments, business associations, financial institutions, insurance providers, private sector actors, and development partners to strengthen climate-resilient local economies and increase private sector investment in climate adaptation and disaster resilience.

As gender and social inclusion (GESI), governance and environmental compliance are cross-cutting and core components of all MC programs and is required to own these components to ensure GESI sensitivity and integration, governance practices and environmental compliance are integrated into the program activities.

Essential Job Responsibilities

The specific duties and responsibilities of the Private Sector Engagement Specialist include, but are not limited to, the following:

Strategy and Technical Leadership (20%)

  • Lead the design and implementation of the programme’s private sector engagement strategy, aligned with CRC program.
  • Provide technical guidance on climate-resilient enterprise development, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), Public–Private Partnerships (PPP), blended finance, and climate risk financing to the program and partner’s team.
  • Strengthen coordination mechanisms between governments, private sector actors, financial institutions, and development partners for climate resilience.
  • Contribute to policy recommendations that strengthen enabling environments for climate investment, climate risk financing and resilient enterprise development.
  • Identify strategic opportunities to integrate private sector engagement into local economic development, climate adaptation, disaster risk reduction, and resilience programming.
  • Develop technical frameworks, operational guidelines, and implementation tools for enterprise resilience and private sector collaboration.
  • Provide technical oversight to ensure interventions are evidence-based, gender-responsive, inclusive, and market-driven.

Climate-Resilient Enterprise Development (15%)

  • Lead implementation of climate-resilient SME and value chain strengthening initiatives.
  • Map and prioritize climate-resilient enterprises and value chains with high adaptation and livelihood potential.
  • Develop and promote climate risk assessment tools, Business Continuity Planning (BCP) guidelines, and enterprise resilience training packages.
  • Support SMEs to improve climate resilience, business continuity, productivity, market access, and competitiveness.
  • Facilitate integration of enterprise resilience into municipal Local Economic Development (LED) plans and business support services.
  • Strengthen collaboration and linkage with business development service providers, cooperatives, financial institutions, and market actors, enterprise network etc.
  • Explore opportunities and create linkage between resilient enterprise and climate vulnerable communities for enhanced economic growth.

Private Sector Partnerships and Investment (15%)

  • Map and engage private sector actors, investors, chambers of commerce, business associations, and industry networks.
  • Engage with National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority and federal entities to lobby CRS for climate and disaster resilience.
  • Identify CSR priorities and facilitate CSR partnerships supporting climate-resilient infrastructure, enterprise, livelihoods, and community resilience.
  • Facilitate co-investment work between businesses, municipalities, and communities to pilot climate resilience initiatives
  • Develop and facilitate strategic partnerships with FNCCI, CCI, FWEAN, financial institutions, and other private sector organizations.

Climate Risk Financing and Insurance (15%)

  • Map and engage insurance companies to raise awareness among municipalities, SMEs, on insurance and climate risk transfer mechanisms.
  • Lead technical work on climate risk transfer mechanisms, including insurance and innovative financial protection approaches.
  • Coordinate with Nepal Insurance Authority, insurance companies, financial institutions, and Practical Action to pilot climate risk financing initiatives.
  • Support development and testing of insurance products for climate-vulnerable SMEs, farmers, outdoor workers, and communities.
  • Facilitate integration of climate risk financing into municipal disaster risk management and local economic development systems.
  • Generate evidence and lessons to support policy dialogue and scale-up of climate risk financing mechanisms.

Advocacy, Influencing and Capacity Strengthening (10%)

  • Design and deliver training programmes for SMEs, municipalities, communities, and CRC partner organizations on climate-resilient business practices, risk management, and sustainable enterprise development.
  • Support the establishment of climate-resilient enterprise networks to facilitate peer learning, knowledge exchange, market linkages, and resilient business expansion.
  • Lead advocacy and influencing initiatives to promote an enabling policy and regulatory environment for climate-resilient enterprises, private sector investment in resilience and disaster risk financing.
  • Engage with federal, provincial, and local governments, private sector associations, chambers of commerce, financial institutions, and development partners to influence policies, strategies, and investment that support climate-resilient development.
  • Advocate for increased private sector investment through Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), blended finance, and innovative financing mechanisms to strengthen community resilience.

Knowledge Management, Learning, and Innovation (10%)

  • Document lessons learned, good practices, case studies, and innovative financing models.
  • Support evidence generation to inform programme adaptation, policy dialogue, and scaling strategies.
  • Facilitate cross-learning among municipalities, business associations, financial institutions, and programme partners.
  • Contribute technical inputs to programme reports, knowledge products, donor reporting, and communication materials.

Coordination and Programme Management (10%)

  • Coordinate implementation with CRC technical teams, ZCRA partners, Practical Action, government agencies, business associations, and financial institutions.
  • Ensure quality implementation of activities, monitoring of progress, and timely delivery of outputs.
  • Contribute to annual work planning, budgeting, monitoring, adaptive management, and reporting.
  • Represent the programme in technical forums, private sector platforms, and coordination meetings related to climate-resilient enterprise, investment, and disaster risk financing.

OTHERS

Posiiton: Senior Shock Responsive Social Protection (SRSP) Coordinator

The Opportunity

Save the Children believes every child deserves a future. In Bhutan and around the world, we give children a healthy start in life, the opportunity to learn and protection from harm. We do whatever it takes for children – every day and in times of crisis – transforming their lives and future we share. Save the Children expects that anyone associated with it abides by its Safeguarding and other Zero Tolerance Policies.

Under the guidance of the Humanitarian Manager (POD) and the Head of Field Programme Operations at the Surkhet Field Office, the role will be responsible for leading and implementing Save the Children’s component of the People in Need (PIN)-led consortium project, Pratibaddha IV: Whole-of-Society Approach to Strengthening and Scaling Shock Responsive and Anticipatory Multi Hazard Preparedness and Response in Western Nepal, across Sudurpaschim, Karnali, and Lumbini Provinces. The role will be responsible for coordinating with the SCI team, PIN, other consortium partners, and government stakeholders at the provincial and local levels to plan, implement, and monitor project activities in accordance with the agreed Detailed Implementation Plan (DIP), ensuring that the required technical support is provided. The role will also be responsible for ensuring the implementation of the MEAL plan, documenting and promoting project learning for scale-up, and enhancing the visibility of Save the Children’s work on Shock Responsive Social Protection (SRSP).

In the event of a major humanitarian emergency, the role holder will be expected to work outside the normal role profile and be able to vary working hours accordingly.

KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:

Technical Assistance and Quality Assurance:

  • Serve as the provincial technical lead for Shock-Responsive Social Protection (SRSP) within the context of Disaster Risk Management (DRM) governance.
  • Lead the planning and coordination of technical project activities, including capacity-building initiatives for consortium partners and relevant government personnel at the provincial and local levels, as required.
  • Facilitate and coordinate capacity-building activities in collaboration with PIN and the Humanitarian Manager, based on the capacity-building plan and in alignment with project outputs and indicators.
  • Lead the development and/or revision of SRSP-related tools, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and guidelines at the provincial level.
  • Support to ensure quality of programmes in the field including benefiting to the vulnerable population.
  • Support for the development and implementation of Minimum Standard for SRSP and other delivery
  • Make regular field visits and ensure the quality, identify best practices, identify issues to be addressed, and share with Humanitarian Manager to seek technical advice
  • Ensure the use of consolidated multi hazard and multi-sector risk assessment tools/guidelines that fits in line with the SCI CSP, MEAL plan and learning from stakeholders.
  • Coordinate to ensure that all project implementation materials /guidelines are reviewed by relevant technical team
  • Faciliate the SRSP part at the provincial level workshops and trainings
  • Lead the thematic discussion on SRSP at provincial level including mandates, roles and responsibilities, coordinating arranngements, challenges and proposed solutions
  • Lead in co-creation of operational blue print for SRSP embeded with AA and Response at provincial and local levels
  • Carrry out multihazard risk analysis embeding social protection database

Project management /implementation:

  • Takes lead role at province level in delivery of SCI component in a consortium led by PIN and ensure SRSP result is delivered and is integrated in other results of the project
  • Ensure timely and quality technical support is available to the partner’s team on SRSP activities through implementation of DIP.
  • Ensure the effective and efficient implementation of the project grants
  • Liaising closely with the CO team, ensure clear roles, responsibilities and timelines are set for all project requirements such as reports, budget realignments etc.
  • Ensure development and implementation of project /detail implementation plans and budgets, procurement plans and provide guidance and solutions to problems to ensure smooth, quality implementation of MEAL plan and achievement of log-frame objectives and results.
  • Development of manual with specification for emergency support stockpiling for local governments

Coordination:

  • Coordinate closely with PIN to ensure implementation of SCI deliverables
  • Build good working relationships with all the stakeholders working in Anticipatory Action and SRSP at province and local levels and across other teams within SCI
  • Work closely with the implementing partner deployed by PIN for the implementation of the SCI component of the project
  • Coordinate with local government and provincial government in coordination with the CO team
  • Work with logistic team to ensure that programme supply needs are clearly defined and coordinated for implementation
  • Provide assistance to SCI staff to the local coordination with partners, municipality and clusters,

Advocacy:

  • Coordinate with provinces, municipalities and relevant stakeholders
  • Work as a province level focal point to coordinate with PIN
  • Development and implementation of advocacy strategy

Documentation and reporting:

  • Organize field visits to ensure to prepare high quality learning documents and reports as per SC and the donor’s requirements and timely submit to related stakeholders
  • Encourage SCI team and partners to document the innovative approaches, best practices, lesson learned, and case studies
  • Ensure quality progress reports and learning documentation are prepared and share them at appropriate level
  • Keep Humanitarian Manager abreast regularly on the progress, consult for key decisions and way forward in the area responsible for.
  • Work with programme teams to ensure that reports are delivered according to SC and donor contractual requirements, within the agreed timescale and budget.
  • Ensure the compliance of programmes with internal SC requirements and any relevant external donor requirements

Qualifications and Experience:

  • A minimum of 4 -5 years’ experience in DRR/humanitarian/social protection sectors
  • Master’s degree in relevant areas such as disaster risk management, social policy, social sciences or equivalent with a minimum of 4 years of relevant experience, or a Bachelor’s degree with min 6 years of experience of relevant experience.
  • Solid project delivery, implementation, and monitoring skills with a proven history of delivering results
  • Experience of capacity building on shock responsive social protection, anticipatory action, DRR and emergency preparedness work
  • Good understanding of shock-responsive social protection, anticipatory action, DRR and Humanitarian programming or relevant thematic area
  • Specific knowledge and skills on disaster information management and communication
  • Proven experience in coordination with municipalities, district stakeholders, other government partners and the ability to lead, motivate and develop others
  • Ability to analyze information, evaluate options and to think and plan strategically
  • Effective interpersonal skills including leadership skills and ability to motivate those line managed by you and provide constructive feedback on performance
  • Fluency in written and spoken English and Nepali, as well as excellent report writing skills
  • Commitment to and understanding of Save the Children’s aims, values and principles including rights- based approaches
  • Prior experience of using GIS in humanitarian/DRR works

Desirable

  • Worked within the NGO community, donor agencies and government departments in relevant role
  • Ability and willingness to stay and travel to any parts of the country
  • Skills related to participatory methods, computer literacy and team management

Kapilvastu Integrated Development Services (KIDS), a non-governmental and non-profitable organization working in the field of Health, Nutrition, Climate change, Livelihood and WASH since 2005 in Lumbini Province of Nepal. KIDS is implementing SRHR program in Kapilvastu, Rupandehi, Arghakhanchi, Pyuthan, Rolpa and Rukum (East) districts supported by UNFPA under Lumbini Province. Connecting to this program, KIDS invites applications from interested, qualified, eligible, accountable and have the ability to deliver results with the highest level of integrity for the following position:

Position: Technical Coordinator (MPDSR and EmONC)
Duty Station: Ministry of Health/Directorate Lumbini Province

Qualifications and Experience

  • Advanced degree in Medicine or Nursing. An additional degree in Public Health will be an added advantage.
  • At least five years of progressively responsible experience in maternal and newborn health, reproductive health, health systems strengthening, or public health programs.
  •  Demonstrated experience in implementing MPDSR, EmONC, Post Pregnancy family planning, quality improvement initiatives, and health information systems. Candidates with ToTs and experience in these areas will have a distinct advantage.
  •  Sound understanding of Nepal’s health system, maternal and newborn health policies, and quality improvement approaches.
  •  Experience working with government institutions, development partners, and health facilities.
  •  Strong analytical, coordination, facilitation, report writing, and stakeholder engagement skills.
  •  Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and health management information systems.
  •  Excellent communication skills in English and Nepali.
  •  Willingness to undertake frequent field travel (approximately 40%) within Lumbini Province.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide technical leadership for the implementation and strengthening of Maternal and Perinatal Death Surveillance and Response (MPDSR), Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (EmONC), and other maternal and newborn health (MNH) interventions in Lumbini Province in line with national policies, guidelines, and standards.
  •  Mentor and provide technical support to priority hospitals to strengthen MPDSR implementation, quality improvement initiatives, strengthening of post-pregnancy family planning, and implementation of response plans following maternal and perinatal death reviews.
  •  Support the implementation, monitoring, and follow-up of recommendations from EmONC prioritization and facility improvement plans.
  •  Monitor the functionality of EmONC referral networks and the EmONC online dashboard, and support health facilities to improve service readiness, referral systems, reporting, and data quality.
  • Support the Family Welfare Division (FWD) and the Provincial Ministry of Health to strengthen the quality of MPDSR and EmONC data by ensuring the timeliness, completeness, accuracy, and utilization of information reported through the web-based MPDSR system and EmONC dashboard.
  • Analyze and share monthly updates on MPDSR implementation, response plan status, EmONC functionality, and key programme findings with the Family Welfare Division, Provincial Ministry of Health, and UNFPA to support evidence-based decision-making.
  •  Provide technical backstopping to Ministry of Health, Provincial Health Training Centre, Health Directorate in implementation of evidence-based maternal and newborn health interventions such as post pregnancy family planning, postpartum hemorrhage management, the Labour Care Guide, the WHO Safe Surgery Checklist, and other RH issues.
  •  Support to strengthen the clinical training sites, service providers clinical and programmatic updates including piloting and scale-up of innovative referral mechanisms, digital monitoring tools, and social and behavior change interventions to improve institutional delivery and access to quality maternal and newborn health services.
  •  Provide technical support during the technical meetings such as Reproductive Health Coordination Committee (RHCC) meetings, Technical Working Group (TWG) meetings, Programme reviews, workshops, and other coordination forums, and ensure timely follow-up of agreed action points.
  •  Liaise with the Ministry of Health, Family Welfare Division, Provincial Health Directorate, local governments, professional associations, and development partners to strengthen coordination and implementation of maternal and newborn health programmes.
  •  Prepare high-quality technical briefs, progress reports, and documentation of Programme achievements, lessons learned, and best practices, including improvements in maternal and newborn care resulting from MPDSR and EmONC interventions.
  •  Undertake regular field monitoring and supportive supervision visits to supported districts and health facilities, and perform other duties assigned by KIDS and UNFPA to ensure effective Programme implementation.

Position: Program Coordinator (Mental Health)
Location: Rolpa District

Qualifications and experiences:

  • At least Bachelor’s degree in Nursing / Public health or related field.
  • At least three years of professional experience in mental health, Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR), public health programming, or health system strengthening.
  • Proven experience in planning, implementing, and coordinating MHPSS or SRHR programs, including integrating mental health services into primary health care and community-based service delivery.
  •  Sound knowledge of Nepal’s health system, the National Mental Health Strategy and Action Plan, SRHR policies and guidelines and quality improvement approaches for integrated service delivery.
  •  Experience working with provincial and local governments and development partners.
  •  Strong skills in data analysis, report writing, facilitation, and stakeholder coordination.

Major Responsibilities and Duties

1. Technical Leadership and Program Implementation

  • Provide technical guidance for the implementation and strengthening of mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) interventions and SRHR interventions in line with national policies, strategies, guidelines, and protocols.
  • Play lead role to implement the provincial mental health strategy in the districts and local level.
  • Support the Health Offices, and local governments in developing annual and periodic work plans integrating mental health and SRHR interventions into routine health service delivery.
  •  Analyze the local health policies and plan from MHPSS perspectives and update where required in consultation with concerned authorities.
  •  Coordinate the planning, implementation, and monitoring of MHPSS and SRHR program activities to ensure the delivery of quality, accessible, and integrated services at community and health facility levels.
  • Facilitate the integration of MHPSS and SRHR priorities into provincial and local health plans, annual work plans, and budgets, advocating for sustainable resource allocation.
  • Provide technical assistance, mentoring, and supportive supervision to health facilities to strengthen the quality of integrated MHPSS and SRHR services.

2. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting

  • Coordinate and support the implementation of the Mental Health Support Program baseline assessment, including planning and supervising data collection, ensuring data quality, contributing to data analysis and interpretation, and supporting the preparation of technical reports and dissemination of findings.
  •  Monitor the implementation and quality of work plan activities across the district per the requirements.
  •  Prepare periodic technical reports, case studies, presentations, and success stories.
  •  Support documentation of best practices and lessons learned.
  •  Ensure timely submission of reports to KIDS, UNFPA, and relevant government authorities.

3. Coordination and Partnership

  • Maintain close coordination with the Health Offices, hospitals, local levels and development partners.
  • Update the mental health organizations and their profile in the province
  • Represent the organization in technical working groups, review meetings, and coordination forums related to SRHR, MHPSS and maternal health.
  • Facilitate collaboration among stakeholders to improve mental heath referral systems and quality of maternal and newborn care services.
  • Support advocacy initiatives to prioritize mental health including SRHR interventions and resource allocation.

Posiiton: Senior Project Manager-DRR, Emergency & Humanitarian Response
Location: Kathmandu

The Organization:

Lutheran World Relief, which is part of Corus International, has been present in Nepal since 2011. Corus International is the parent of a family of world-class organizations working to deliver the holistic, lasting solutions needed to end extreme poverty once and for all. We are a global leader in international development, with 150 years of combined experience across our brands. Our nonprofit and for-profit subsidiaries include IMA World Health and its fundraising brand Corus World Health, Lutheran World Relief, CGA Technologies, Ground Up Investing, and Farmers Market Brands. In Nepal, Corus operates under Lutheran World Relief. Our more than 400 employees around the globe are experts in their fields and dedicated to helping the world’s most vulnerable people break the cycle of poverty and lead healthy lives.

At Corus we believe that good only grows stronger and we reflect that belief in our workplace culture. We value every employee’s specialized area of expertise and nurture professional growth. We promote an engaging and supportive work environment, where employees feel enabled and driven to innovate, learn and collaborate. And because our subsidiaries often function as partners, our employees have the opportunity to work across our enterprise family.

Job Brief:

Position Summary: This position will be an employee of Lutheran World Relief. The RISE Fund project strengthens disaster preparedness, governance, and resilience in Nepal’s most vulnerable provinces, Karnali and Sudurpaschim. The program runs across multiple sectors to reduce humanitarian risks and build inclusive disaster risk management systems.

The program has four interlinked components:

  • Emergency Preparedness & Coordination – establishing rapid response teams, provincial search and rescue units, and activating emergency operations centers.
  • Shelter & Relief Support – pre-positioning emergency supplies, constructing temporary shelters, and ensuring rapid deployment within 24-72 hours after disasters.
  • Health & WASH Services – training health workers, deploying mobile medical camps, distributing dignity kits, and restoring safe water and sanitation systems.
  • Protection & Logistics – providing mental health and psychosocial support, safeguarding vulnerable groups, and creating an emergency transportation fund for rapid deployment.

The project aims to work with the provincial government to enable them to target 13 priority districts and 116 municipalities, directly benefiting over 30,000 individuals and indirectly reaching more than 500,000 people.

The Senior Project Manager- DRR, Emergency and Humanitarian Response Manager (DEHRM)’s core functions are to manage anticipated DRR, Emergency and Humanitarian Response including identifying and supporting local partners, implementing projects, representing LWR in the government and non-government sector in federal and provincial level. The DEHRM will oversee and monitor the implementation of anticipated DRR, Humanitarian and Emergency Response project activities in close coordination with federal and provincial governments stakeholder along with peer agencies, manage local implementing partners, and ensure the program quality; and meet the highest international as well as Donor’s standards of implementation.

Responsibilities:

Program Management: 20%

  • Support in design and implement DRR, emergency and humanitarian response related projects and programs in coordination with federal and provincial Government, local partners and other stakeholder as necessary.
  • Leads design and implementation of DRR, emergency and humanitarian response program in Nepal.
  • Ensure current and potential LWR’s DRR partners have capacity and skill to implement assigned projects.
  • Ensure all reports meet LWR internal deadlines, Cooperation Agreement deadlines, and/or AAA award agreement deadlines.
  • Ensure partner narrative and financial reports are completed and submitted to the LWR-Nepal office and HQ on a timely basis.
  • Works as a team member of partner selection committee and provides inputs on technical capability of potential partner organization for future opportunities.
  • Manage partner organizations for successfully implementing the project and ensure high-quality outcomes in or field.
  • Monitors the assigned DRR, emergency and humanitarian response project periodically including financial, collects learning and provide feedback and mentoring to partner organizations and LWR for improvement in program. Support in project evaluation, assessment and surveys including developing terms of reference (ToR) and agreement with consultant and firms.

DRR, Emergency and Humanitarian Response: 30%

  • Support in design and implementation of DRR, early preparedness and emergency response and resilience program in Nepal.
  • Ensure that the reporting requirements of donors and LWR are timely submitted with high-quality standards.
  • Coordinate in establishment and strengthening of Rapid Response Teams, Provincial Search and Rescue Teams, Emergency Medical Teams, and other emergency response mechanisms.
  • Work closely with partners and ensure stock pilings are maintained at strategic locations and ensure minimum standard of the emergency materials and develop Standard Operating Procedure (SoP) for handling stockpiling.
  • Support in activation or strengthening of Provincial Emergency Operations Centers (PEOCs) and coordination mechanisms.
  • With Country Office and HQ, provide input on decisions regarding responding to sudden onset and complex emergency situations.
  • Lead LWR needs assessments or participate in joint assessments and draft high-quality needs assessment report within 72 hours from sudden onset emergency.
  • Participate in initial coordination meetings of response agencies and document outcomes.
  • Represent LWR at selected UN and peer agencies (AIN) cluster meetings related to DRR, emergency, and humanitarian response.
  • With PD, coordinate with CHO and HQ on response decisions.
  • Lead the Country Office emergency team following protocols as outlines in the Emergency Preparedness Plan.

Coordination and Collaboration: 20%

  • Maintain and liaise cordial coordination, communication and collaboration with government stakeholders, donors, peer agencies and local partners.
  • Maintain strong relationships with federal, provincial, and local governments, humanitarian coordination mechanisms, donors, UN agencies, and NGO partners.
  • Represent LWR in relevant coordination forums, including NDRRMA, Ministry of Home Affairs, Provincial Ministries, AIN working groups, UN Clusters, DDRCs, LEOCs, and other humanitarian platforms.
  • Obtain necessary permission, authentication from the ministry or province and municipality as required.
  • Lead for approval of related project Agreement (PA) and project evaluation by the SWC and other government stakeholders.
  • Represents LWR in AINTGDM working group of AIN and others.

Technical Support: 10%

  • Provide technical DRR, Emergency and Humanitarian response supports to local partners, and their staffs along with provincial LWR’s co-workers.
  • Provides technical support in DRR, emergency health preparedness, humanitarian response, resilience, shelter, WASH, health in emergency, and protection programming to provincial and provincial and local government officials as well as partner NGOs on program implementation.
  • Support in establishing and strengthening of rapid response team, search and rescue team, emergency medical team, and community-based disaster preparedness mechanisms.
  • Ensure high-quality implementation of emergency shelter, dignity kits, WASH, health, and psychosocial support interventions.
  • Strengthen emergency health preparedness and response by training health workers, DDRC members, and Emergency Medical Teams (EMTs); supporting disease early warning and risk communication through mass media; and coordinating the deployment of mobile medical camps to provide first aid, essential medicines, maternal and child health services, disease surveillance, and referral services during emergencies.
  • Facilitate Technical training to Government officials (Provincial, district and local government stakeholders), NGO and LWR staff on CHS, SPHERE and other relevant HA tools.
  • Organize technical meeting and workshop in consultation with government stakeholders at provincial, district and local along with peer agencies related to DRR, HA and emergency response.
  • Act as a key resource person in conducting above training, project design and business development in the DRR, HA and emergency response programming area, gap-filling and taking on growth responsibilities, as needed.
  • Coordinate the identification of staff capacity and technical assistance needs of partner organizations and capacity strengthening and required interventions to support program quality.
  • Work closely with MEAL team to monitor project performance, generate evidence, document lesson learned, success stories and improve program quality.
  • Lead in developing the ToR for the consultant as needed for the project and hire them ensuring the LWR’s standard procedure and requirement.

New Business Development 10%

  • Supports and facilitates exploring new DRR, preparedness, HA and emergency response program opportunities in the country.
  • Serves as a member of country focal person for institutional donor as well as other donor opportunities on DRR, emergency and humanitarian response and be the member of capture and proposal team.
  • Lead in drafting concept note related to DRR, emergency and humanitarian response opportunities in the country.

content.rendered:
Established in 1990, Banke UNESCO Club is a non-governmental organization registered with the District Administration Office, Banke, and affiliated with the Social Welfare Council. The establishment of the organization was inspired by the ideals of non-violence, social justice, self-reliance, sustainable development, and volunteerism.

The organization is committed to promoting holistic and integrated development, guided by a harmonious balance of socio-cultural, material, scientific, and environmental dimensions. Its mission is to enhance the literacy rate among disadvantaged, marginalized, deprived, and the poorest of the poor (POP) groups, with particular emphasis on women and children, by providing access to quality education.

Banke UNESCO Club has been engaged in a long-term partnership with Plan International Nepal. At present, the organization is collaborating with Plan International Nepal to implement the Youth Empowerment for Transformation and Innovation (YETI) Project in Bardiya District.

The overarching goal of the project is to foster the economic empowerment of adolescent girls, young women, and marginalized youth, enabling them to drive inclusive, climate-resilient, and market-oriented economies. The initiative seeks to equip young people with the knowledge, skills, and confidence required to establish and manage sustainable enterprises. It emphasizes cultivating an entrepreneurial mindset that empowers youth to identify, develop, and scale innovative business ideas aligned with emerging local market opportunities.

Furthermore, the project aims to strengthen and institutionalize enterprise development support systems, ensuring that young people can access business development services and resources essential for entrepreneurship and enterprise growth. It envisions building a coherent, accessible, and sustainable support ecosystem that systematically connects youth with enterprise development services and markets.

In addition, the project focuses on enhancing access to appropriate financial services, enabling young women and marginalized youth to transition effectively from training to sustainable entrepreneurship. It also prioritizes the development of a supportive policy and institutional environment that allows youth particularly young women and marginalized groups to thrive as entrepreneurs and innovators.

Banke UNESCO Club now invites applications from qualified, experienced, and motivated candidates to join the team in implementing the YETI Project in Bardiya District.

Job Description
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

  • Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
  • Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
  • Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers
  • Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

As part of these efforts, UNDP, with anchor investment from partners such as the International Climate Initiative (IKI) of Germany and in consultation with several members of Tiger Conservation Coalition (TCC), is leading the development and operationalization of the Tiger Landscapes Investment Facility (TLIF). The Tiger Landscapes Investment Facility or TLIF is a blended finance mechanism developed in response to the urgent need to catalyze private sector investments into nature-positive businesses that contribute to the protection, restoration, and sustainable management of Tiger Landscapes.

The TLIF is uniquely structured to mobilize private sector capital predominantly from domestic financial institutions. The TLIF is structured to have two arms. The Technical Assistance Facility (TA facility) aims to work with the local stakeholders, conservation organizations, and institutions – government and private – to develop pipelines of investable projects. An innovative and fit-for-purpose guarantee facility – administered by the United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) – provided to the local financial institutions to enable lending to those pipelines of projects created through the support of the TA facility. The TLIF is also designed to have a unique governance structure that represents the donors, the investors and members of the Tiger Conservation Coalition (TCC).

Duties and Responsibilities

The National Project Specialist (NPS) will lead the coordination and management of the TA facility in Nepal. The incumbent will identify and engage with partners on pipeline development and coordinate with the Financial Service Providers (FSPs) to support the financing of the nature-positive projects. By the end of the project, a substantial number of enterprises are expected to have been established, contributing to the conservation and restoration of the tiger landscapes. In addition to that the NPS will contribute to the impact monitoring and evaluation, randomized verification, preparation of case studies and engagement with the government to further enhance the scale and impact of the Facility.

The NPS will lead the project and oversee day-to-day implementation of the TA Facility in Nepal under the direct supervision of the Portfolio Manager, Resilience and Environment Portfolio and in close coordination with the Global Project Manager of the TLIF as well as the Assistant Resident Representative (ARR) for Nepal. The NPS will be responsible for ensuring that project results are delivered in line with the approved project document, meeting agreed standards of quality, timeframes, and budget. Key duties include preparing annual work plans and budgets for approval, as well as semi-annual and annual progress reports outlining achievements, challenges, and necessary adjustments. The NPS will manage procurement and recruitment of national and international service providers and specialist expertise in consultation with the Global team and Country Office. The NPS will also play a central role in coordinating the efforts of all partners to ensure coherent and effective delivery.

Lead Project Coordination and Management

  • Develop annual work plans, budgets, and targets in line with the TLIF Project Document.
  • Monitor progress against plans, identify bottlenecks, and propose corrective measures to ensure timely and quality delivery.
  • Support UNDP with regular updates, background materials, and reporting for decision-making.
  • Lead and supervise the Project, setting clear objectives and providing performance guidance.
  • Oversee procurement, contracting, and recruitment processes, including drafting TORs and technical specifications.
  • Ensure the effective and accountable use of project resources in line with UNDP standards.
  • Identify, contract, and supervise consultants, suppliers, and service providers to ensure quality and timely delivery of outputs.
  • Coordinate and oversee the timely execution of project activities, consultants, and suppliers.
  • Monitor the quality of technical outputs, ensuring compliance with approved standards.
  • Establish and maintain systems for monitoring progress, risks, and results.
  • Prepare semi-annual and annual progress reports for submission to Global Team and CO.
  • Lead the implementation of project activities, ensuring the timely delivery of approved project outputs and coordination with responsible parties.
  • Coordinate annual and third-party verification processes and consolidate impact and other relevant reports as required by the donor, UNDP and the government partners.
  • Monitor project risks, provide updates on evolving or materialized risks, and propose mitigation and management actions.
  • Ensure compliance with project frameworks and funding requirements, especially UNDP’s Programme and Operations Policies and Procedures (POPP).

Lead Implementation of Technical Assistance Facility

  • Lead the establishment of pipeline development programme by identifying business service providers, specialised agencies, and conservation NGOs through a competitive process.
  • Lead the technical assistance to the financial service providers (FSPs), particularly in ensuring that the TLIF eligibility criteria are fit for purpose and are accurately applied as per the agreement between TLIF and the FSPs.
  • Engage pipeline development partners to enhance outreach to local enterprises to be developed.
  • Strengthen the capacity of the pipeline development partners, focusing on improving the biodiversity impact of the enterprises.
  • Establish and manage relevant advisory groups to enhance the competitiveness of the nature-positive enterprises
  • Facilitate exchanges between business service providers, conservation NGOs, specialized government agencies and Financial Service Providers (FSPs) to enhance financial and impact competitiveness of enterprises and increase the outreach to target beneficiaries.
  • Conduct field visits to potential and financed enterprises to monitor impact and provide strategic support for strengthening biodiversity-positive impact.
  • Coordinate with the Impact Investment Specialist to ensure FSPs have the necessary capacity to apply the Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), including the TLIF eligibility criteria, and monitor biodiversity impact.
  • Coordinate with the Impact Investment Specialist to ensure that the necessary financial literacy and capacity on finance among the business service providers, and the enterprises financed.

Build Strategic Partnerships, Stakeholder Engagement and Facilitate Knowledge Sharing

  • Serve as the central point of coordination and maintain strong working relationships with project partners at national, state, and community levels, ensuring effective liaison with government counterparts, UN agencies, and other responsible parties involved in implementation.
  • Ensure regular engagement with the government and other stakeholders to share updates, challenges and opportunities.
  • Maintain good relationships with key stakeholders, including government agencies, private sector partners, financial institutions, conservation organizations including the members of the Tiger Conservation Coalition, and local communities within tiger landscapes.
  • Organize, facilitate, and/or participate in events, meetings, workshops and conferences to enhance the profile of the TLIF and to engage stakeholders.
  • Support the south-south exchange and participation of the government in relevant events.
  • Support knowledge-sharing and learning efforts to enhance the effectiveness of the Tiger Landscapes Investment Facility.
  • Support project visibility and communications activities in coordination with UNDP and national partners.
  • Promote knowledge exchange and capacity development with Government counterparts and local stakeholders.
  • Document and disseminate lessons learned and best practices within Nepal and across region.

Mainstreaming Gender Equality and Social Inclusion:

  • Ensure mainstreaming of Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) principles throughout project planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting in line with national policies and UNDP’s gender and social safeguards requirements.
  • Facilitate the integration of gender-responsive and inclusive climate actions in project interventions, ensuring that women, indigenous peoples, persons with disabilities, and marginalized groups actively participate and benefit equitably.
  • Promote capacity development on GESI and climate resilience for project staff, implementing partners, and local stakeholders, ensuring inclusive participation and gender-balanced representation.
  • Ensure that data collection and reporting are sex-, age-, and disability-disaggregated, and that progress reports adequately reflect gender equality and social inclusion outcomes.
  • Identify and address potential gender and social risks associated with project activities, proposing mitigation measures in coordination with relevant stakeholders.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The National Project Specialist will head the Project Unit and oversee day-to-day implementation of the TA Facility in Nepal. The NPS will function as the Project Manager for TLIF in accordance with UNDP’s Internal Control Framework under the direct supervision of the Portfolio Manager (Resilience and Environment). The NPS is required to work in close coordination with the Global Project Manager of the TLIF as well as under the guidance from the Assistant Resident Representative (Resilience and Environment Portfolio) for Nepal.

Competencies

Core competencies:

  • Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact
  • Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems
  • Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences
  • Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands
  • Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results
  • Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration
  • Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity
  • People Management: UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies Nature

  • Ecosystems and biodiversity: Biodiversity Finance
  • Ecosystems and Biodiversity: Policy and practice shift

Procurement

Strategic sourcing:

  • Knowledge of strategic sourcing concepts, principles and methods, and ability to apply this to strategic and/or practical situations

Business Management

  • Project Management

Ability to plan, organize, prioritize, and control resources, procedures, and protocols to achieve specific goals

Partnerships Management

  • Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society, and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies

Risk Management

Identify and organize action around reducing, mitigating and proactively managing risks

2030 Agenda: People

  • Gender

Innovation for Gender Equality

Business Direction & Strategy

System Thinking

Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

2030 Agenda: Prosperity

Inclusive Growth

Social Inclusion

Required Skills and Experience

Min. Education requirements

  • Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Finance, Environmental Science, Business Administration, or a related field is required. Or
  • A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the said fields with 2 additional years of relevant experience may be considered in lieu of a master’s degree.

Min. years of relevant work experience

A minimum of 5 years (with a master’s degree) or 7 years (with a bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience in project implementation and management, with a focus on planning, monitoring, reporting, and stakeholder and team coordination.

Required skills

Good computer literacy – MS office applications, web-based management information systems.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

  • Experience in business development, pipeline development or entrepreneurship
  • Experience in processing and interpreting data and information.
  • Experience in effectively networking within the national team and with external institutions.
  • Experience in biodiversity conservation.
  • Experience in impact investment or finance, including biodiversity or conservation finance;
  • Experience of the UN and/or UNDP’s rules, policies and procedures.
  • Exposure to environmental issues or biodiversity
  • Prior experience in managing high-value, donor-funded projects
  • Extensive managerial experience, including experience in leading multi-cultural teams.
  • Demonstrated leadership in multi-stakeholder coordination (government, civil society, IPLCs, private sector, and international organizations).
  • Demonstrated ability to draft high-quality reports, policy briefs, and official communications;
  • Experience in budget management and oversight experience
  • Proven experience in working with government counterparts, donors, and development partners at policy/strategic level including familiarity with government procedures, donor compliance requirements, and project governance frameworks.

Required Language(s)

Fluency in English and Nepali is required.

Established in 1997, SEBAC-Nepal is a national-level NGO. SEBAC-Nepal works in various thematic areas such as Livelihood/ Agriculture/ Economic Recovery; Rural Infrastructure; Nutrition, Health and Education; Governance, Gender Advocacy and Empowerment; Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH); and Disaster Risk Reduction and Management/Natural Resource and Biodiversity Management/ Climate Change. The organization invites applications from qualified, motivated, and dynamic individuals for the following position:

Position Title: Proposal Development and Reporting Manager

Required No.: One (1)

Duty Station: Thecho Lalitpur with 60% & Konjyosom Rural Municipality 40% based in SEBAC-Nepal Office.

Duration: Minimum two years

Minimum Qualifications, Experience and Requried Competencies & Skills:

  • Master’s degree in Development Studies, Project Management, International Relations, Social Sciences, or a related field with at least 5 years of experience in proposal development, donor reporting, and project documentation in the development sector.
  • Demonstrated experience in developing high-quality project proposals, concept notes, donor reports, and technical documentation for bilateral, multilateral, and institutional donors.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Nepali, with strong analytical, research, and editing abilities.
  • Strong knowledge of logical framework (Logframe), results-based management (RBM), project monitoring, donor compliance, and reporting requirements.
  • Proficiency in MS Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), with excellent organizational, coordination, interpersonal, and time management skills, and the ability to work under pressure to meet tight deadlines.

Key Responsibilities:

The Proposal Development and Reporting Manager will lead the development of high-quality project proposals, concept notes, donor reports, and organizational documentation. The position will coordinate with program, finance, and field teams to compile project information, ensure donor compliance, monitor reporting timelines, and maintain quality standards. The Manager will support resource mobilization, strengthen partnerships, document project achievements, and ensure timely submission of accurate technical and narrative reports aligned with organizational and donor requirements.

A. Proposal Development

  • Lead the development of high-quality project proposals, concept notes, expressions of interest (EOIs), and grant applications.
  • Coordinate with program, finance, and technical teams to develop competitive and donor-compliant proposals.
  • Conduct background research, needs assessments, and gather evidence to strengthen proposals.
  • Prepare logical frameworks, implementation plans, budgets, and supporting documents.

B. Donor Reporting and Documentation

  • Prepare and submit timely, accurate, and high-quality narrative reports in accordance with donor requirements.
