Posiiton: Project Associate- Agriculture & Livestock, MaWRiN Project
Location: Sindhuli

Company Description

WWF Nepal, the global conservation organization leading international efforts for a living planet, seeks applications from qualified Nepali candidates for the following full-time position. If you think you are an achiever and willing to work within a diverse team in a multicultural environment with commitment and passion for what you believe in, you are highly encouraged to apply.

Our Mission

At WWF Nepal, we firmly believe people and nature are inextricably linked. Our mission is to stop the degradation of our planet’s natural environment and build a future Nepal in which people live in harmony with nature.

Our Vision

From its origins as a small group of committed wildlife enthusiasts, WWF has grown into one of the world’s largest and most respected independent conservation organizations, active in over 100 countries.

Over this time, WWF’s focus has evolved from localized efforts in favor of a single species and individual habitats to an ambitious strategy to preserve biodiversity and achieve sustainable development across the globe.

WWF-Nepal envisions a prosperous Nepal, with an active and socially responsible citizenry that a greater sense of stewardship towards the environment.

Our Core Values

We celebrate and respect diversity in nature and among the people, partners, and communities with whom we work. Across the many cultures and individuals that represent WWF, we are unified by one mission, one brand, and one common set of values:

Courage: We demonstrate courage through our actions, we work for change where it’s needed, and we inspire people and institutions to tackle the greatest threats to nature and the future of the planet, which is our home.

Integrity: We live the principles we call on others to meet. We act with integrity, accountability, and transparency, and we rely on facts and science to guide us and to ensure we learn and evolve.

Respect: We honor the voices and knowledge of the people and communities that we serve, and we work to secure their rights to a sustainable future.

Collaboration: We deliver impact at the scale of the challenges we face through the power of collective action and innovation.

Job Description

The Managing Watersheds for Enhanced Resilience of Communities to Climate Change in Nepal (MaWRiN) Project is being implemented in the Marin watershed, which covers two major rivers, i.e., Marin and Kyan in Sindhuli district. The project is funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF) managed Least Developed Countries Fund (LDCF) to be implemented over a period of six years by WWF in close association with the federal Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment (MoAFE) as the National Executing Agency and Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Forests and Environment of Bagmati Province as the Project Executing Partner. The project will enable the government and local stakeholders to invest in protecting the Marin watershed while bolstering the longer-term resilience of local and indigenous communities against climate emergencies.

The objective of the project is “to enhance climate resilience of Indigenous people and local communities in the Marin watershed (partly/fully covering the area of Marin rural municipality, Kamalamai municipality, Ghyanglekh rural municipality, and Hariharpurgadhi rural municipality) through nature-based solutions and livelihood improvement.” The project’s objective will be achieved through the following three inter-connected components:

Component 1: Enabling environment for mainstreaming climate change through development of capacity of the municipalities and other key local agencies to assess and understand climate risks and vulnerabilities, and accordingly mainstream climate change adaptation strategies and actions in local policies and plans. Also, through the establishment of a multi-stakeholder platform for dialogue and coordinated actions on climate change adaptation at the watershed level.
Component 2: Enhanced Resilience of Local Communities to Climate Change through a) community-based natural resource management such as community identification of adaptation interventions, support and demonstration of sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture and livestock practices, improved water management, strengthened management of community and leasehold forests, and b) Nature-based Solutions that reduce climate impacts and risks.
Component 3: Monitoring, evaluation and knowledge management, through tracking of project progress on a regular basis; garnering and analysis of lessons and good practices; and development and dissemination of knowledge that reinforces project results from components 1 and 2, providing a sound basis for their replication, adaptation and sustainability.

A Project Management Unit (PMU) has been set up at Kamalamai Municipality, Shantinagar, Sindhuli Madi, Sindhuli. The main functions of the PMU are to (i) oversee fiduciary arrangements, (ii) ensure overall efficient management, coordination, timely implementation of the agreed project work plan/result framework including the Environment and Social Management Framework (ESMF) and related Safeguard plans, (iii) operational oversight of implementation activities, (iv) timely reporting, and for effective use of GEF/LDCF resources for the approved work plan and (v) monitoring of the project. The PMU will also serve as the secretariat to the project coordination committee and multi-stakeholder dialogue and action platform.

Under the direct supervision of the Project Officer, the Project Associate (Agriculture & Livestock) will support the implementation of project activities. This position is expected to have expertise in community engagement and mobilization so that s/he can work with local communities and stakeholders to identify and take up climate-adaptive technologies and practices for agriculture, livestock management, and water resource management. This position requires approximately 70% travel to the project site.

Major Duties and Responsibilities:

1. Technical backstopping

  • Support in providing technical expertise for effective community and stakeholders’ engagement in the project.
  • Support in providing technical support in agriculture, livestock management, and climate-induced disaster risk reduction and management to local communities and stakeholders

2. Capacity Building

  • Support in training local communities/farmers/user group members on improved water management, climate-adaptive agriculture technologies and practices
  • Support in strengthening local communities/farmers/user group members’ capacity to climate-induced disasters.
  • Support capacity building events targeting local and provincial government agencies for the effective delivery of extension services to local communities on climate-adaptive technologies and practices in agriculture, irrigation, livestock, and water management

3. Planning

  • Support the planning process by bringing the voices of the vulnerable community and their adaptation needs during annual workplan finalization.
  • Engage in local communities, government, and stakeholders’ planning processes to integrate improved water management, climate-adaptive agriculture technologies and practices, resource leverage, and sharing project best practices and learning.

4. Project Implementation & Coordination

  • Facilitate local communities and stakeholders to ensure that activities are planned and executed in line with the project’s established processes and guidelines.
  • Support overall implementation of project activities across all components.
  • Support in organizing workshops, training, and periodic planning meetings/sessions.
  • Coordinate and communicate with local stakeholders and project partners.
  • Support in logistic arrangements and coordination for PCC meetings and PSC meetings.

5. Reporting and Documentation

  • Support the preparation of semi-annual and annual project progress reports (PPR).
  • Support the Inclusive Conservation Assistant to ensure documentation of all safeguards-related activities, including Grievances Redress Mechanisms (GRM).
  • Support the Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning (MEL) and Communications Officer to ensure that communication and learning materials are developed, and success stories are documented and published.

Paid Relocation: None

Company Description

WWF Nepal, the global conservation organization leading international efforts for a living planet, seeks applications from qualified Nepali candidates for the following full-time position. If you think you are an achiever and willing to work within a diverse team in a multicultural environment with commitment and passion for what you believe in, you are highly encouraged to apply.

Our Mission

At WWF Nepal, we firmly believe people and nature are inextricably linked. Our mission is to stop the degradation of our planet’s natural environment and build a future Nepal in which people live in harmony with nature.

Our Vision

From its origins as a small group of committed wildlife enthusiasts, WWF has grown into one of the world’s largest and most respected independent conservation organizations, active in over 100 countries.

Over this time, WWF’s focus has evolved from localized efforts in favor of a single species and individual habitats to an ambitious strategy to preserve biodiversity and achieve sustainable development across the globe.

WWF-Nepal envisions a prosperous Nepal, with an active and socially responsible citizenry that a greater sense of stewardship towards the environment.

Our Core Values

We celebrate and respect diversity in nature and among the people, partners, and communities with whom we work. Across the many cultures and individuals that represent WWF, we are unified by one mission, one brand, and one common set of values:

Courage: We demonstrate courage through our actions, we work for change where it’s needed, and we inspire people and institutions to tackle the greatest threats to nature and the future of the planet, which is our home.

Integrity: We live the principles we call on others to meet. We act with integrity, accountability, and transparency, and we rely on facts and science to guide us and to ensure we learn and evolve.

Respect: We honor the voices and knowledge of the people and communities that we serve, and we work to secure their rights to a sustainable future.

Collaboration: We deliver impact at the scale of the challenges we face through the power of collective action and innovation.

Job Description

The Managing Watersheds for Enhanced Resilience of Communities to Climate Change in Nepal (MaWRiN) Project is being implemented in the Marin watershed, which covers two major rivers, i.e., Marin and Kyan in Sindhuli district. The project is funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF) managed Least Developed Countries Fund (LDCF) to be implemented over a period of six years by WWF in close association with the federal Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment (MoAFE) as the National Executing Agency and Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Forests and Environment of Bagmati Province as the Project Executing Partner. The project will enable the government and local stakeholders to invest in protecting the Marin watershed while bolstering the longer-term resilience of local and indigenous communities against climate emergencies.

The objective of the project is “to enhance climate resilience of Indigenous people and local communities in the Marin watershed (partly/fully covering the area of Marin rural municipality, Kamalamai municipality, Ghyanglekh rural municipality, and Hariharpurgadhi rural municipality) through nature-based solutions and livelihood improvement.” The project’s objective will be achieved through the following three inter-connected components:

Component 1: Enabling environment for mainstreaming climate change through development of capacity of the municipalities and other key local agencies to assess and understand climate risks and vulnerabilities, and accordingly mainstream climate change adaptation strategies and actions in local policies and plans. Also, through the establishment of a multi-stakeholder platform for dialogue and coordinated actions on climate change adaptation at the watershed level.
Component 2: Enhanced Resilience of Local Communities to Climate Change through a) community-based natural resource management such as community identification of adaptation interventions, support and demonstration of sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture and livestock practices, improved water management, strengthened management of community and leasehold forests, and b) Nature-based Solutions that reduce climate impacts and risks.
Component 3: Monitoring, evaluation and knowledge management, through tracking of project progress on a regular basis; garnering and analysis of lessons and good practices; and development and dissemination of knowledge that reinforces project results from components 1 and 2, providing a sound basis for their replication, adaptation and sustainability.
A Project Management Unit (PMU) has been set up at Kamalamai Municipality, Shantinagar, Sindhuli Madi, Sindhuli. The main functions of the PMU are to (i) oversee fiduciary arrangements, (ii) ensure overall efficient management, coordination, timely implementation of the agreed project work plan/result framework including the Environment and Social Management Framework (ESMF) and related Safeguard plans, (iii) operational oversight of implementation activities, (iv) timely reporting, and for effective use of GEF/LDCF resources for the approved work plan and (v) monitoring of the project. The PMU will also serve as the secretariat to the project coordination committee and multi-stakeholder dialogue and action platform.

Under the direct supervision of the Project Officer, the Project Associate (Forests & Watershed) will support the implementation of project activities. This position is expected to have expertise in community engagement and mobilization so that s/he can work with local communities and stakeholders to identify and take up climate-adaptive technologies and practices for agriculture, livestock management, and water resource management. This position requires approximately 70% travel to the project site.

Major Duties and Responsibilities:

1. Technical backstopping

  • Support in providing technical expertise for effective communities and stakeholders’ engagement in the project.
  • Support in providing technical support to communities and stakeholders in strengthening community forests, leasehold forests and the rehabilitation and protection of degraded lands and vulnerable areas.

2. Capacity Building

  • Support in training local communities/farmers/forest user group members on strengthening community and leasehold forest management, climate-adaptive agriculture technologies and practices
  • Support capacity building events targeting local and provincial government agencies for the effective delivery of extension services to local communities on climate-adaptive technologies and practices, forest management, rehabilitating and protecting degraded and vulnerable areas, and watershed management.

3. Planning

  • Support the planning process by bringing the voices of the vulnerable community and their adaptation needs during annual workplan finalization.
  • Engage in local communities, government, and stakeholders’ planning processes to integrate forest management, watershed management, rehabilitating and protecting degraded and vulnerable areas technologies and practices, resource leverage, and sharing project best practices and learning.

4. Project Implementation and Coordination

  • Facilitate local communities and stakeholders to ensure that activities are planned and executed in line with the project’s established processes and guidelines.
  • Support overall implementation of project activities across all components.
  • Support in organizing workshops, training, and periodic planning meetings/sessions.
  • Coordinate and communicate with local stakeholders and project partners.
  • Support in logistic arrangements and coordination for PCC meetings and PSC meetings.

5. Reporting and Documentation

  • Support the preparation of semi-annual and annual project progress reports (PPR).
  • Support the Inclusive Conservation Assistant to ensure documentation of all safeguards-related activities, including Grievances Redress Mechanisms (GRM).
  • Support the Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning (MEL) and Communications Officer to ensure that communication and learning materials are developed, and success stories are documented and published.

6. Inclusive Conservation

  • Support in identifying and integrating GESI and environmental and social safeguards provisions and activities in finalizing the annual workplan.
  • Support in identifying and integrating the voice, knowledge, skills, and values of indigenous peoples and local communities, and ensuring they benefit from project efforts and activities

7. Grant and Contract Management

  • Support for preparing grants and contracts.
  • Coordinate with contractors/consultants for timely completion of activities and submission of reports.

8. Other Duties

This job description covers the main tasks and conveys the spirit of the tasks that are anticipated proactively. Other tasks may be assigned as necessary according to the project needs.

Experience: At least 2 years of experience in project implementation. Knowledge of GESI, Safeguards, climate-adaptive technologies and practices is highly desirable. Experience of working in national GEF projects will be an added advantage.

Position: Outreach Officer (Social Worker/Senior Counsellor)
Reports to: Psychologist/Programme Coordinator
Location: KOSHISH Emergency Care Service Center, Pharping, Kathmandu

A. JOB SUMMARY

The Outreach Officer is responsible for coordinating community outreach activities, conducting awareness and advocacy programs, providing psychosocial support, facilitating reintegration and follow-up services, and collaborating with stakeholders to promote mental health and psychosocial well-being.

The position involves working closely with local governments, health facilities, One-Stop Crisis Management Centers (OCMCs), safe houses, community organizations, and other stakeholders to strengthen community support systems, facilitate referrals, and promote access to quality mental health services. The officer is also responsible for maintaining proper documentation, case records, and reporting while supporting the recovery, reintegration, and social inclusion of women and girls with mental health conditions.

B. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Community Outreach

  • Plan and coordinate rescue, reintegration, and follow-up activities in consultation with the multidisciplinary team, in accordance with KOSHISH policies and approved budgets.
  • Document rescue, reintegration, and follow-up activities for learning, reporting, and communication purposes.
  • Coordinate with local governments, health officials, OCMCs, safe houses, police, and relevant organizations to ensure long-term support for beneficiaries.
  • Collaborate with wards and municipalities to link reintegrated beneficiaries with available mental health services.
  • Identify women requiring specialized psychosocial support through screening and refer them to the Emergency Care Service Centre (ECSC) or other appropriate services.
  • Link beneficiaries with available mental health services, social protection programs, and social security schemes.
  • Conduct joint livelihood assessments with the psychologist for reintegrated beneficiaries requiring livelihood support and coordinate with local stakeholders for appropriate assistance.
  • Conduct community and family awareness sessions to strengthen support systems and promote successful reintegration.

2. Advocacy

  • Engage with local governments and relevant stakeholders to advocate for mental health and psychosocial well-being.
  • Advocate for the allocation of local government budgets for mental health services and community awareness initiatives.
  • Promote the rights of persons with mental health conditions and advocate for their access to services and resources.
  • Coordinate with OCMCs, health sections, women and children sections, planning sections, and provincial authorities to prioritize mental health within local development plans.
  • Empower self-advocates and rights holders to raise their voices for accessible mental health services and increased budget allocation.
  • Support the planning and facilitation of community orientation, awareness, and sensitization activities.

3. In-house Care

  • Facilitate group therapy sessions, relaxation exercises, and peer support groups in coordination with the multidisciplinary team.
  • Coordinate with the House In-charge to ensure the safety and security of beneficiaries, including emergency preparedness and incident management.
  • Promote products produced by beneficiaries within and outside KOSHISH.
  • Support agro-based activities that contribute to beneficiaries’ rehabilitation and the sustainability of the ECSC.
  • Arrange weekly family phone or video calls for beneficiaries in coordination with the outreach and nursing teams.
  • Conduct intensive follow-up of reintegrated beneficiaries every 15 days, document progress using the standard follow-up template, and share findings with the psychologist.
  • Support safe house staff and perform additional duties as assigned.

4. Case Management

  • Ensure proper coordination and obtain formal commitments from families, OCMCs, municipalities, community-based organizations (CBOs), or other relevant stakeholders before rescue and reintegration.
  • Explain treatment plans and recovery procedures to beneficiaries and their families in coordination with the psychologist.
  • Prepare monthly plans for rescue, reintegration, and follow-up activities.
  • Support the psychologist in identifying causes of relapse and planning appropriate interventions.
  • Conduct beneficiary screening and assessments and develop individualized care, treatment, and reintegration plans.
  • Provide need-based counselling through interviews, observation, and appropriate psychosocial assessment tools.
  • Counsel beneficiaries and their families during follow-up visits and maintain proper documentation.
  • Conduct regular follow-up visits and telephone calls in coordination with the outreach team and psychologist to promote recovery and reduce relapse.
  • Monitor reintegrated beneficiaries through KOSHISH community-based programs.
  • Coordinate with municipalities to strengthen referral mechanisms for mental health services.

5. Documentation and Reporting

  • Maintain accurate beneficiary records and databases while ensuring confidentiality and privacy.
  • Develop educational materials, presentations, and information resources on mental health.
  • Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual reports for submission to the line manager.
  • Review reports, success stories, and field data submitted by outreach and field staff before compilation.
  • Maintain and manage ECSC data systems accessible to authorized team members and supporting partners.
  • Develop communication materials, including photographs, videos, brochures, collages, and awareness materials, in coordination with the ECSC team.
  • Perform any other duties assigned by the supervisor that are relevant to organizational objectives.

C. ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS

  • Minimum Bachelor’s degree in Psychology, Social Work, or a related field (Counselling training is preferred).
  • At least two years of relevant experience in social work, counselling, or community mental health.
  • Knowledge of community resources, social service systems, and referral mechanisms.
  • Commitment to professional ethics, confidentiality, and continuous professional development.
  • Strong teamwork and interpersonal skills.
  • Excellent communication and counselling skills.
  • Sensitivity to mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) issues.
  • Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings and weekends when required.
  • Strong documentation, reporting, and data management skills.
  • Good coordination, advocacy, facilitation, and networking skills.

D. Safeguarding and Code of Conduct:

  • Ensure compliance with organizational safeguarding policies including Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment (PSEAH).
  • Maintain professional conduct and contribute to a safe and respectful working environment.

content.rendered:
NNSWA has been actively working with various community development projects in Sudurpaschim Province of Nepal for more than three and half decades. It has significant years of experience working in the sector of DRRM/CCA and humanitarian response, Education, Health, Livelihoods, HIV and AIDS, Nutrition, Physical Rehabilitation Services for the People with Disability along, Stop Leprosy with other development sectors and has been closely working with different funding partners and all levels of the government. NNSWA is going to implement DRM and HEA RISE Project, in Kanchanpur and Kailali Districts in partnership with World Vision International Nepal. Therefore, NNSWA announces the vacancy for applying for the following position.

Position: Project Coordinator

Required No: (1) One

Base Station: Kanchanpur/Kailali Project Office and frequent visit to Project Implementing Municipalities

GENERAL POSITION SUMMARY:

The Project Coordinator is responsible for the overall coordination, management, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of the RISE project, funded by the US Government and implemented by Nepal National Social Welfare Association (NNSWA) with the technical support from World Vision International Nepal. The position ensures effective delivery of project objectives, donor compliance and organizational requirements, safeguarding and quality assurance, stakeholder coordination, budget management, and effective humanitarian response maintaining the core principles of humanitarian standards.

Required Qualifications and experience:

Academic Qualification:

  • Master’s degree in environmental science, DRR&M, Social Science or a related field or Bachelor’s degree with substantial relevant experience in DRR and emergency response may be considered.

Experience:

  • Four years of experience in implementing DRR, humanitarian response-related programs and experience in managing projects including people and budget management
  • Experience working with local government authorities, humanitarian clusters, and local communities.
  • Strong knowledge of CBDRR approaches and humanitarian response including early warning system, strengthening local capacity.
  • Understanding of legal documents on DRR&M, humanitarian structure, emergency response mechanisms, and humanitarian principles and standards
  • Proficiency in oral and written communication in English and Nepali.
  • Strong project cycle management and budget management skills.
  • Excellent coordination, networking and stakeholder engagement abilities.
  • Strong analytical, report writing and documentation skills.
  • Experience in data analysis and MEAL system

Position: DRR and Humanitarian Field Officer (RISE)

Required No.: (2) Two

Base Station: Kanchanpur: Krishnapur Municipality and One Rural Municipality-1 Kailali: Gauriganga Municipality and Ghodaghodi Municiplaity-1

GENERAL POSITION SUMMARY:

The DRR and Humanitarian Officer is responsible for planning, implementing, monitoring, and reporting Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and emergency response activities of the RISE project, funded by the US Government and implemented by Nepal National Social Welfare Association (NNSWA) with the technical support from World Vision International Nepal. This position is required to work closely with district and local stakeholders to support vulnerable communities to strengthen resilience through the implementation of interventions related to disaster preparedness, risk reduction measures, and effective humanitarian response in line with organizational standards, humanitarian principles and donor compliance.

Required Qualifications and experience:

Academic Qualification:

  • Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, DRR&M, Social Science or a related field.

Experience:

  • Two years of experience in implementing DRR, humanitarian response-related programs
  • Experience working with local government authorities and local communities.
  • Understanding of legal documents on DRR&M, humanitarian structure, emergency response mechanisms, anticipatory action framework, and humanitarian principles and standards
  • Proficiency in oral and written communication in English and Nepali.
  • Excellent coordination, networking and stakeholder engagement abilities.
  • Strong report writing and documentation skills.

Position: MEAL Officer

Required No.: (1) One

Base Station:Kanchanpur/Kailali Project Office and frequent visit to Project Implementing Municipalities

GENERAL POSITION SUMMARY:

The MEAL Officer is responsible and executes day-to-day monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning processes at the district and community levels under Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and emergency response activities of the RISE project, funded by the US Government and implemented by Nepal National Social Welfare Association (NNSWA) with the technical support from World Vision International Nepal. This role ensures that all field data of the project is clean, timely, and compliant with WVI Nepal standards . The officer works directly on the ground, receiving technical templates, guidance, and oversight from the Grant MEAL Coordinator, WVI Nepal and report to the Project Coordinator.

Required Qualifications and experience:

Academic Qualification:

  • Bachelor’s degree in social science, Development Studies, or a field relevant to MEAL.

Experience:

  • At least 2 years of experience working with an I/NGO in the monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning sector and two-wheeler driving license and active driving skills are highly preferred.
  • Clear understanding of MEAL plans, project logic, and logical frameworks.
  • Sound knowledge of qualitative and quantitative data collection methodologies and basic analysis.
  • Practical literacy in digital data collection tools and standard software (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  • Strong written and oral communication skills for reporting and presentation.
  • Working knowledge of local language of the working community
  • Proven ability to work under pressure and confidence to represent the project to district government bodies.

Position: Finance Officer

Required No.: (1) One

Base Station: Kanchanpur/Kailali Project Office

GENERAL POSITION SUMMARY:

The Finance Officer (FO) will be responsible mainly for (i)Administrative Operations; (ii) Reporting and relationships; (iii) Accounting; (iv) Filing and stamping, under the close supervision of the Project Coordinator and technical guidance from the NNSWA head office, the FO will ensure the successful implementation of the Rapid Interventions through Shared Engagement DRM & HEA RISE Project in Nepal, funded by the US Bureau of Disaster and Humanitarian Response (DHR) in partnership with World Vision International Nepal. The FO will approach their duties with proactive, innovative, original, and enthusiastic methods, focusing on achieving results. The role requires high adaptability and a continuous search for the most efficient ways to meet objectives and provide support. Close cooperation and liaison with other project staff members and consortium partners are essential, maintaining constructive and dynamic relationships with all involved parties.

Required Qualifications and experience:

Academic Qualification:

  • Minimum Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration from a recognized University with three (3) years of work experience in a similar field or Master’s degree with two (2) years of working experience in a similar capacity and able to travel and spend time in the project districts and community areas.

Experience:

  • Financial Skills: Budget Management, Financial Reporting, Bookkeeping, Cost Analysis, Regulatory Compliance, donor compliance specially USG related project.
  • Administrative Skills: Organizational Skills, Communication Skills, Project Management, Problem-Solving, Time Management
  • Technical Skills: Accounting Software Proficiency, Data Analysis, IT Skills

Position: Supply Chain Management (SCM) Officer

Required No.: (1) One

Base Station: Kanchanpur/Kailali Project Office

GENERAL POSITION SUMMARY:

The Supply Chain Management (SCM) Officer –RISE Project is responsible for leading end-to-end supply chain management activities under RISE/ grant-funded projects within the Organization. The position ensures that procurement, logistics, inventory management, asset management, distribution, and supplier management activities are conducted efficiently, transparently, and in compliance with donor requirements, organizational policies, and government regulations. The role contributes to effective project implementation through sound stewardship of grant resources, strong internal controls, risk mitigation, and timely delivery of goods and services. This position directly contributes to successful grant implementation by ensuring that project goods, services, equipment, and resources are procured, managed, and delivered efficiently, transparently, and in full compliance with donor and organizational requirements, enabling project objectives and beneficiary outcomes to be achieved effectively.

Required Qualifications and experience:

Academic Qualification:

Experience:

Assignment country: Nepal

Expected end date: 31/05/2027
Sustainable Development Goal: 11. Sustainable cities and communities
Host entity: UNDP
Modality: Onsite

Volunteer category: Expert UCoS from Apr2026

Details

Mission and objectives

UNDP in Nepal

VISION STATEMENT

UNDP Nepal works with the people and Government of Nepal, and other development partners to pursue equitable and sustainable human development goals through eradication of poverty, increase in livelihood opportunities, improvement in community resilience against conflict, disasters and impact of climate change, while laying down strong foundations for a society based on rule of law with an inclusive and participatory democracy.

Context

Pokhara, Nepal’s tourism capital, faces complex, interconnected challenges including youth out-migration, a fragmented informal economy, environmental degradation, and siloed public services. To address these systemic issues, UNDP Nepal and Pokhara Metropolitan City (PMC) have initiated the Pokhara Green Digital Portfolio, an adaptive framework designed to catalyze long-term, sustainable urban transformation.

The portfolio is structured around three core transformation shifts ( Outputs):

  •  Resilient and Digital Governance as a steering mechanism for the green transition.
  •  Youth-led Entrepreneurship Ecosystem to diversify the local economy.
  • Green Tourism ( Regenerative and circular) to create a sustainable, value-adding economic model.To drive this agenda, UNDP is seeking a dedicated, dynamic expert to be based on the ground in Pokhara. This role is critical for managing day-to-day portfolio implementation, fostering a multi-stakeholder coalition, and translating the strategic vision into tangible, on-the-ground actions. The UN Volunteer will also support user research and coordination for the Service Blueprint and Youth Entrepreneur Persona Study for Business Registration in Pokhara”.

Task description

Under the direct supervision of the Portfolio Manager and the close guidance of the Head of the Field Office (Gandaki and Lumbini Provinces), the Portfolio Coordinator will carry out responsibilities across four key pillars:

3.1 Portfolio Coordination and Dynamic Management

  •  Support the day-to-day coordination and dynamic management of the Green Digital Portfolio and its three strategic shifts by coordinating activities, tracking progress, risks, decisions and follow up actions.
  •  Facilitate the development and regular updating of the Green Digital Portfolio workplan.
  •  Support portfolio monitoring, learning, and adaptation by documenting implementation updates, emerging insights, and evidence for Funding Window dynamic management and reporting.
  • Support regular portfolio review and reflection processes to inform workplan adjustments, partners coordination, and resource mobilization.

3.2 Stakeholder Coordination and Platform Building

  • Act as the primary focal point for building and maintaining strong working relationships with Pokhara Metropolitan City, private sector actors, academic institutions, youth organizations, civil society, and relevant partners.
  •  Support the finalization and implementation of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between UNDP and Pokhara Metropolitan City.
  •  Help co-design and operationalize a practical joint-management mechanism for the portfolio
  •  Facilitate the implementation of the activities assigned to PMC, as part of the joint work plan of the Portfolio.
  •  Arrange, facilitate, and document regular multi-stakeholder meetings, workshops, and coordination sessions to ensure collaborative progress.

3.3 Support to Research and Strategic Development

  •  Coordinate and support the user research for The Service Blueprint and Youth Entrepreneur Persona Study for Business Registration in Pokhara, including coordination with users, municipal counterparts, and technical experts.
  • Support research team for organizing interviews, consultations, user mapping, documentation, and validation activities with youth entrepreneurs and business service actors.
  • Support the research team in synthesizing user needs and pain points into practical inputs for the design of targeted interventions that support young entrepreneurs (e.g., incubation, access to finance, market linkages).

3.4 Gender and Social Inclusion (GESI)

  •  Ensure GESI principles are systematically mainstreamed across all portfolio’s co-design and decision-making processes.
  •  Support and actively work to ensure the inclusion of women, youth, marginalized groups, and less represented enterprise actors in consultation, user research and all portfolio activities.
  •  Support the creation of a safe and respectful working environment for all partners and participants.

Eligibility criteria

Age: 18 – 80

Required experience: 7 years

Nationality: Candidate must be a national, legal resident or hold refugee status in the country of assignment.

Assignment requirements

Relevant experience: 7 years

Languages

Nepalese, Level: Fluent, Required
English, Level: Fluent, Required

Required education level: Master’s degree in any discipline

Competencies and values

Accountability | Adaptability and Flexibility | Creativity | Judgement and Decision-Making | Planning and Organising | Professionalism | Self-Management

Skills and experience

  • At least 7 years of professional experience in project management, local development and partnership building, or multi-stakeholder programme implementation.
  •  At least 3 years of hands-on experience in enterprise development
  •  Demonstrated experience working with municipal governments, private sector entities, and civil society organizations in Nepal.
  •  Research & Design: Experience in user research, service design, business process mapping, and digitization is highly desirable.
  •  Familiarity with system thinking, portfolio approaches /integrated approaches, and learning-oriented implementation is an advantage.
  •  Interpersonal Skills: Culturally and socially sensitive, with the ability to work inclusively with a range of partners.

Area(s) of expertise

Project management, programme development, strategy, Partnerships, resource mobilisation, Governance, elections

Driving license
–

Other information

Volunteerism is understood as a wide range of activities undertaken of free will, for the general public good, for which monetary reward is not the principal motivating factor.

Living conditions and remarks

This assignment will be based in Pokhara, the capital of Gandaki Province. Pokhara is a major urban center with excellent living conditions, including access to modern housing, amenities, and reliable transportation. The UN Volunteer will be responsible for arranging their own housing and other living essentials. The role requires extensive engagement within Pokhara and may involve frequent local travel. The security situation is stable, but the volunteer is expected to strictly adhere to all UN security guidelines.

Inclusivity statement

United Nations Volunteers is an equal opportunity programme that welcomes applications from qualified professionals. We are committed to achieving diversity in terms of gender, care protected characteristics. As part of their adherence to the values of UNV, all UN Volunteers commit themselves to combat any form of discrimination, and to promoting respect for human rights and individual dignity, without distinction of a person’s race, sex, gender identity, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, age, language, social origin or other status.

Scam warning

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Position: Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning Officer (Nepal)

Location: Kathmandu

Lutheran World Relief, which is part of Corus International, has been present in Nepal since 2011. Corus International is the parent of a family of world-class organizations working to deliver the holistic, lasting solutions needed to end extreme poverty once and for all. We are a global leader in international development, with 150 years of combined experience across our brands. Our nonprofit and for-profit subsidiaries include IMA World Health and its fundraising brand Corus World Health, Lutheran World Relief, CGA Technologies, Ground Up Investing, and Farmers Market Brands. In Nepal, Corus operates under Lutheran World Relief. Our more than 400 employees around the globe are experts in their fields and dedicated to helping the world’s most vulnerable people break the cycle of poverty and lead healthy lives.

At Corus we believe that good only grows stronger and we reflect that belief in our workplace culture. We value every employee’s specialized area of expertise and nurture professional growth. We promote an engaging and supportive work environment, where employees feel enabled and driven to innovate, learn and collaborate. And because our subsidiaries often function as partners, our employees have the opportunity to work across our enterprise family.

Job Brief:

This position will be an employee of Lutheran World Relief. The RISE Fund project strengthens disaster preparedness, governance, and resilience in Nepal’s most vulnerable provinces, Karnali and Sudurpaschim. The program runs across multiple sectors to reduce humanitarian risks and build inclusive disaster risk management systems.

The program has four interlinked components:

  • Emergency Preparedness & Coordination – establishing rapid response teams, provincial search and rescue units, and activating emergency operations centers.
  • Shelter & Relief Support – pre-positioning emergency supplies, constructing temporary shelters, and ensuring rapid deployment within 24-72 hours after disasters.
  • Health & WASH Services – training health workers, deploying mobile medical camps, distributing dignity kits, and restoring safe water and sanitation systems.
  • Protection & Logistics – providing mental health and psychosocial support, safeguarding vulnerable groups, and creating an emergency transportation fund for rapid deployment.
  • The project aims to work with the provincial government to enable them to target 13 priority districts and 116 municipalities, directly benefiting over 30,000 individuals and indirectly reaching more than 500,000 people. The Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Officer is a project-based position to support the implementation of anticipated DRR, Health Preparedness, Emergency and Humanitarian Response programming in the Karnali and Sudurpaschim Provinces in Nepal. MEL Officer reports to the DRR, Emergency and Humanitarian Response Manger and will have functional relationship with Senior Program Director,
  • Senior Program Manager (Agriculture and Livelihoods) and Kathmandu based administration and finance team. The position holder is expected to spend 30%of time in field especially in above two provinces and 25% of time in LWR other projects (especially PunarUtthan) working closely with the Senior Manager.

Position Summary:

The Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Officer is responsible for strengthening the project’s MEL system by ensuring high-quality data collection, analysis, reporting, and evidence generation. The position supports project monitoring, assessments, learning, and adaptive management while building the capacity of implementing partners and promoting the use of digital and AI-enabled solutions to improve data quality and decision-making.

Responsibilities:

  • Maintain and regularly update project databases, monitoring tools, indicators, supporting evidence, case studies, and other MEL documentation.
  • Plan, coordinate, and support household surveys, focus group discussions (FGDs), key informant interviews (KIIs), rapid assessments, baseline/endline studies, readiness assessments, outcome harvesting, and other monitoring and evaluation activities.
  • Review the partner’s periodic narrative reports including Performance Monitoring Plan (PMP), Beneficiary Tracking Table, Indicator Tracking Table and Activity Tracking Table and provide inputs on timely basis to ensure the data and information are correct and validated.
  • Ensure the quality, accuracy, completeness, and timely validation of project data in accordance with organizational and donor requirements.
  • Analyze monitoring and assessment findings and support the preparation of high-quality monthly, quarterly, annual, and donor reports in collaboration with the line manager.
  • Facilitate participatory action research, document Most Significant Change (MSC) stories, lessons learned, innovations, and evidence-based best practices for knowledge sharing and adaptive management.
  • Provide training, mentoring, coaching, and technical support to project staff and implementing partners on MEL systems, data collection tools, data quality assurance, and reporting standards.
  • Support the development, strengthening, and regular maintenance of digital MEL databases, dashboards, and information management systems.
  • Promote organizational learning by documenting project achievements, challenges, cross-learning events, and disseminating evidence-based findings to internal and external stakeholders.
  • Provide technical MEL support to other Corus/LWR projects and programs, as assigned, to strengthen organizational monitoring, evaluation, and learning practices.
  • Promote and facilitate the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI), digital technologies, and innovative approaches to improve data collection, analysis, visualization, reporting, and knowledge management across projects.

Supervisory: None

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in social science, public health, public administration or related field.
  • A minimum of three (3) years of demonstrated experience in the field of monitoring, evaluation, learning or project management with I/NGOs preferably in DRR and emergency health projects.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Knowledge of humanitarian standards.
  • Knowledge of health management information system (HMIS) will be a plus.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
  • Ability to implement and manage technical project activities and collaborate across multiple teams.
  • Strong skills in programmatic data analysis, report writing and documentation.
  • Strong negotiation, coordination, communication, and interpersonal skills (diplomacy, patience), believing in teamwork with the ability to perform multiple tasks and work under pressure.
  • Fluent in English and Nepali (speaking and writing)
  • Willingness to contribute and trust in teamwork.
  • Proficiency in Office 365 applications including Word, Excel, SharePoint, and PowerPoint.

Physical and Mental Requirements:

  • The physical requirements that may be needed to execute responsibilities may include bending, standing, and walking, etc.
  • The mental requirements that are essential to satisfactorily executing the responsibilities outlined in this job description include, but not limited to: learning new tasks, comprehending, and retaining information, completing tasks independently, effectively communicating verbally and in writing, demonstrating proficiency in using computer software to perform assigned tasks.

Other Duties:

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive list of activities, duties or responsibilities for the position. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice. All positions are required to perform any additional tasks assigned by the supervisor. Global positions that are bound by contracts will not be changed without notice and approval.

Working Conditions, Travel and Environment:

  • LWR has an in-person work policy, with all employees reporting to the office Monday through Friday The employee must be available to work outside normal office hours or on the weekends as required.
  • This position must be able to travel as required for standard domestic and international business purposes. While performing the duties of this job in different locations, the employee may be exposed to precarious settings under high-security risks and/or very basic living conditions and outside weather conditions, as well as to infectious diseases.
  • If applicable, must have authorization to work in the country of assignment.

As a member of the Corus Family, each employee is expected to:

  • Foster a work environment where everyone feels valued and included.
  • Support employees’ evaluation and promotion processes based on skills and performance.
  • Promote a safe, secure, and respectful environment for all members of Corus family, stakeholders in general, and particularly for the communities we serve.

Job Brief:

Position Summary: This position will be an employee of Lutheran World Relief. The RISE Fund project strengthens disaster preparedness, governance, and resilience in Nepal’s most vulnerable provinces, Karnali and Sudurpaschim. The program runs across multiple sectors to reduce humanitarian risks and build inclusive disaster risk management systems.

The program has four interlinked components:

  • Emergency Preparedness & Coordination – establishing rapid response teams, provincial search and rescue units, and activating emergency operations centers.
  • Shelter & Relief Support – pre-positioning emergency supplies, constructing temporary shelters, and ensuring rapid deployment within 24-72 hours after disasters.
  • Health & WASH Services – training health workers, deploying mobile medical camps, distributing dignity kits, and restoring safe water and sanitation systems.
  • Protection & Logistics – providing mental health and psychosocial support, safeguarding vulnerable groups, and creating an emergency transportation fund for rapid deployment.
  • The project aims to work with the provincial government to enable them to target 13 priority districts and 116 municipalities, directly benefiting over 30,000 individuals and indirectly reaching more than 500,000 people.

The Project Manager – Provincial DRR Specialist will manage the implementing of LWR’s anticipated Humanitarian Response Project focused to DRR, Emergency and Humanitarian Response including identifying and supporting local partners, implementing projects, representing LWR in the government and non-government sector based at Provincial Ministry (Karnali or Sudurpaschim). The PDS will facilitate DRR, Emergency and Humanitarian Response Manager (DEHRM) and Senior Program Director to implement the anticipated DRR, emergency and humanitarian response project activities in close coordination with Provincial Governments, and local implementing partners, and ensure the projects meet the highest international as well as Donor’s standard of implementation. The PDS is a member of the program team of LWR’s DRR and Humanitarian Response Project. S/he will be responsible for assigned project through capacity building and strengthening the coordination, and networking with provincial government stakeholder specially at Provincial Emergency Operational Center (PEOC) under supervision of DEHRM Manager and Program Director.

Responsibilities:

Program Management:

1. Provincial Capacity Strengthening (30%)

Strengthen the technical and institutional capacities of provincial government agencies, particularly the Provincial Emergency Operations Center (PEOC), on disaster risk reduction (DRR), emergency preparedness, and humanitarian response. Provide technical support to improve provincial disaster management systems and coordination mechanisms.

2. Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement (20%)

Build and maintain effective coordination with provincial government agencies, humanitarian partners, and other relevant stakeholders. Represent LWR in provincial-level coordination forums and support joint planning and collaboration for disaster preparedness and response.

3. Training and Technical Support (20%)

  • Plan and facilitate training, workshops, simulation exercises, and other capacity-building activities on DRR, emergency preparedness, health emergencies, and humanitarian response. Provide ongoing technical guidance to government counterparts and partners to strengthen preparedness and response capacities.
  • Policy and Systems Strengthening
  • Support the review, implementation, and improvement of provincial DRR and emergency management policies, plans, and standard operating procedures. Strengthen PEOC systems and support the functionality and effective use of DRR equipment and Early Warning Systems (EWS).

4. Partner Management (20%)

  • Provide technical guidance and regular support to implementing partner organizations to ensure timely, high-quality, and compliant implementation of project activities. Monitor partner performance and facilitate problem-solving to achieve project objectives.

5. Reporting and Communication (10%)

  • Maintain effective communication with government counterparts, implementing partners, humanitarian actors, and the LWR Nepal office.
  • Prepare timely, accurate, and high-quality technical reports, progress updates, and documentation under the guidance of the DRR, Emergency and Humanitarian Response Manager and Senior Program Director.
  • Work closely with M&E officer and maintain all the project data, case studies, photos

Supervisory:

There are no direct reports.

Education & Experience:

  • Bachelor’s with at least 5 years’ progressive experience in designing, managing, implementing, and monitoring the DRR, health preparedness, emergency and humanitarian response related projects.
  • Experience working with local-based NGOs and community organizations
  • Experience living and/or working in developing countries preferred.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Good understanding of concept of DRR, early warning, anticipatory early action, climatic resilience and emergency health preparedness programming.
  • Should have understanding of humanitarian standards such as CHS, HAP, SPHERE.
  • Excellent communication and influencing skills to communicate effectively and credibly, both verbally and in writing in English. Nepali language fluency required
  • Familiarity with humanitarian systems internationally and in Nepal
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively with government systems mainly at province.
  • Ability to travel at least 80% of the time.
  • Proficiency in Office 365 applications including Word, Excel, SharePoint, and PowerPoint. Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.

Physical and Mental Requirements:

  • The physical requirements that may be needed to execute responsibilities may include bending, standing, and walking, etc.
  • The mental requirements that are essential to satisfactorily executing the responsibilities outlined in this job description include, but not limited to: learning new tasks, comprehending, and retaining information, completing tasks independently, effectively communicating verbally and in writing, demonstrating proficiency in using computer software to perform assigned tasks.

Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice. All positions are required to perform any additional tasks assigned by the supervisor. CAD Jumla is an autonomous, independent, nonprofit making independent, non-governmental organization (NGO) working in areas of promoting human rights and developmental activities. It was established in 2009 AD, by the enthusiastic youths of Jumla; lawyers, social workers, health worker, journalists, human rights activists and intellectuals to facilitate in promoting human rights and continuing developmental activities based on the principle of “for the Karnali people with the Karnali people and by the Karnali people” for establishing just and prosperous Karnali region by acknowledging the adversity and diversity of the region in terms of geographical remoteness, economic hardships, traditional practices and rich flora and fauna. The organization has been working on need based action orientated multi-disciplinary areas through social mobilization especially focusing on human rights, Women Empower, agriculture and School WASH.

CAD Jumla has been implementing the “Empowered Girls, Safe Community project” in partnership with Plan International Nepal. The project will be implemented in Hima, Sinja and Kanakasundari Rural Municipality of Jumla district. The key goal of the project is that all child, adolescent and young (CAY) particularly girls and young women enjoy their rights to live free from child, early and forced marriage (CEFM).

Position: Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Officer- One (Only for Female Candidate)

*Candidates who have previously applied, need not reapply.*

Contract Type: C-SC -7

Duty Station: Based at CAD Jumla field office Sinja Rural Municipality, Jumla (Frequent travel to Hima, Sinja and Kanakasundari Rural Municipalities to project areas)

Job period: Till June 2027 most probably can extend to June 2028

Reports to: Project Coordinator (CAD Nepal & PACE Nepal Jumla)

Technical Reporting: Executive Director (CAD Nepal), Executive Director (PACE Nepal) and MERL Focal Person, Plan International Nepal

Salary and Benefits: As per the organization’s norms commensurate with the project agreement

1. Job Summary: The Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) Officer is responsible for establishing and strengthening the project Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) system across both consortium partners (CAD Nepal and PACE Nepal). The position will ensure high-quality data management, monitoring, documentation, reporting, accountability mechanisms, learning processes and evidence generation for all project interventions related to Child Protection, Child Sponsorship, Livelihood, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Youth Empowerment and Gender Equality.

The M&E Officer will work closely with both consortium organizations to ensure standardized monitoring systems, quality reporting and effective utilization of project evidence for decision-making.

2. Key responsibilities and tasks

A. Compliance to policies, rules/regulations and guidelines

Adhere policies, rules & regulations and guidelines of CAD Nepal, PACE Nepal and Plan International Nepal including safeguarding children and program participants.

B. Monitoring Evaluation and Learning (MERL) System and Support

  • Ensure the proper implementation of the Result-Based M&E framework and Log Frame; orient field staff and project team on adherence to these frameworks.
  • Develop and maintain project monitoring systems for both CAD Nepal and PACE Nepal, ensuring consistency of monitoring tools across consortium partners.
  • Ensure all monitoring tools are GESI responsive (meaning they are designed to disaggregate data by sex, age, people/children with disability, ethnicity and geography)
  • Support district-based staff conducting baseline, Annual Data Collection, End-Line studies, in house assessment, Child Marriage Prevalence Survey and Knowledge, Attitude, and Practice (KAP) surveys.
  • Provide technical inputs to ensure survey and methodologies are inclusive (e.g. accessible formats for persons with disability, safe space for women etc.

C. Data Management, Quality Assurance & Reporting

  • Track progress against project outputs, outcomes, and indicators.
  • Collect routine project data, compile, and review to ensure quality deliverables.
  • Analyze monthly, semiannual, and annual coverage/people reached (focusing on Sponsored Children and marginalized groups).
  • Disaggregate all qualitative data and conduct qualitative analysis to measure how project interventions are affecting women, men, boys, girls, Dalit, and persons with dasibilties.
  • Prepare Monthly MEL reports and support the Project Coordinator in preparing periodic progress reports and database reports for Plan International Nepal. Support PCs to highlight GESI related achievement, barriers, and adaptive measure in all narrative reports.
  • Ensure the quality and confidentiality of all project data and information. Ensure that data handling practice protect vulnerable respondents from stigma or harm, particularly when collecting sensitive or protection related data.

D. Monitoring, Field Visits & Verification

  • Conduct routine monitoring visits, verify project achievements through field observation and data validation, and provide evidence-based synthesized report.
  • Actively triangulate data by conducting separate Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) with women-only, men-only, and mixed groups to capture diverse voices, including those often excluded from community dialogues.
  • Monitor whether project activities are physically and socially accessible to persons with disabilities and whether they actively challenge harmful gender norms and power imbalances in the community
  • Carry out routine field monitoring and share findings with project staff and the Plan MERL Unit. Ensure findings are analyzed through a GESI lens before sharing, highlighting any unintended negative consequences on marginalized groups
  • Promote use of Quality Monitoring Tools (QMT) and document evidence-based recommendations and action items.
  • Plan and Guide field staffs through regular monitoring and share findings with project staff and the Plan MEL section.
  • Analyze and discuss monitoring findings with the Executive Director, Project Coordinator, and field staff.

E. Capacity Building & Staff Support

  • Enhance the capacity of non-MEL staff on MEL requirements, systems, and proper documentation.
  • Conduct orientation sessions for field staff on GESI-responsive data collection techniques, including how to ask sensitive questions, avoid interviewer bias, and ensure the meaningful participation of women and persons with disabilities in monitoring activities.
  • Provide necessary feedback to project staff and support course correction during implementation.

F. Learning, Documentation & Knowledge Management

  • Prepare and document success stories, best practices, and lessons learned; share these with the team, community, and local/district line agencies.
  • Capture and uplift success stories of transformative change
  • Support field staff in maintaining/updating information at Watch Groups, Child Rights Committees, Inter-Religious Groups, Youth Networks, and Child Clubs.

G. Stakeholder Coordination & Advocacy

  • Establish sound relations and coordination with stakeholders, consortium partner, and the funding partner (Plan International Nepal).
  • Support the project in organizing regular review/reflection meetings and joint monitoring visits with Rural Municipalities and key stakeholders.
  • Ensure that review meetings include GESI focal persons from the Rural Municipality and that feedback from women and marginalized groups is systematically presented to decision-makers
  • Promote Community Engagement and Accountability (CEA) of CAD, PACE and Plan International Nepal. Ensure feedback received from stakeholders is communicated to the Project Lead and Board for better response.
  • Flag any GESI-related grievances or exclusion risks to the Project Lead immediately for remedial action.

H. Others

  • Any other duties towards achievement of project objectives assigned by the line Manager and Program Specialist/concerned staff of Plan International.

3. Academic Qualification, Experience and Competencies

a. Academic Qualification and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree (Preferred Master’s degree) in Public Health, social science and any discipline from recognized institutions with minimum of three years of working experience in similar Position and themes.
  • Experience in Child Protection, SOYEE & DRR and in mountain districts would be an added advantage.

b. Required Professional and Social Competencies

  • Strong inter-personal, communication, negotiation and facilitation skills;
  • Experience in establishing and maintaining collaborative relationships with rural municipalities, community groups and other agencies working in project area;
  • Fluency in both (written and oral) English and Nepali;
  • Proven experience with quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis
  • Strong capacity and creativity in leading and facilitating participatory methodologies to meaningfully engage beneficiaries, including children, and receiving their feedback through approaches such as social audit
  • Excellent knowledge and skills in Windows, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and data analysis tools and software.
  • Experience in program data management, use of data management electronic devices such as tablets is highly desirable
  • Willing to travel extensively to the project implemented sites and able to accommodate and adjust with local community/ stakeholders;
  • Sensitivity towards issues related to child protection, gender, social equality and poverty alleviation.
  • Sensitive and seriousness with safety and security system.

Link: CV format

Interested results-oriented candidates who meet the above-mentioned required qualifications and experiences can submit applications in the given format at cadrecruit2020@gmail.com by Thursday, July 30, 2026, before 5:00 PM.

Encourage people from disadvantaged and marginalized communities (Women, Dalit, Indigenous, Madhesi, Muslim and people with disabilities) to apply. Local candidates will be given high priority. Only short-listed candidates will be notified for selection process. Telephone inquiries shall not be entertained.

Posiiton: Multimedia Content & Video Production Assistant
Number of Positions: 1
Location: Kathmandu

Organization Description

The Why: NEPAL aspires to graduate from least developing country to a lower middle-income country by 2026. However, the development community’s excessive focus today on socio-political empowerment has not yielded the desired economic transformation. In reaching the 2026 national target, shall we wait for institutions of power to become accountability productive or shall we bolster innovations of people to bring inclusive prosperity? How do we strengthen grassroots-government collaboration in shaping an equal and enterprising future?

The How: DAAYITWA, with a focus on economic empowerment, envisions an enterprising Nepal where every youth has opportunities for a prosperous future. Daayitwa is a part of the Daayitwa Abhiyaan which consists of four organizations: Daayitwa, Governance Lab, Nepal Leadership Academy based in Nepal and Nepal Rising (Daayitwa-US) based in the U.S. Inspired by shared values of innovation, collaboration, and service, it promotes the socio- economic development of Nepal. The movement fosters inclusive and equitable economic growth by accelerating grassroots innovations, strengthening government institutions, and revitalizing a virtuous cycle of democracy and development through grassroots-government collaboration.

Our Focus Areas:

1. Promote enterprise-led employment creation

2. Design evidence-based policies for improved decision-making

3. Build state capability for effective policy implementation

4. Foster stakeholder collaboration for governance innovations

Daayitwa runs several programs and initiatives aimed at our focus area. These key programs include:

Growth Entrepreneurship and Employment Promotion (GEEP) Program: GEEP accelerates rural enterprises for boosting employment and income growth in rural Nepal. GEEP is executed through a partnership among Daayitwa, Gandaki and Koshi provincial governments, 10 local governments and the Nepali diaspora.

Daayitwa Nepal Public Service Policy Fellowship Program: Daayitwa supports bureaucrats and parliamentarians in making policy decisions by conducting policy research, building capability of government and strengthening research ecosystem.

Policy and Governance Research: Daayitwa has conducted research on several topics including youth employment, enterprise ecosystem, as well as women’s political and economic empowerment.

Leadership for Economic Governance Program: Daayitwa enables local governments to promote local economic development by enhancing their policy leadership capability and fostering trustful collaboration with other municipal ecosystem stakeholders.

Mission Asha: Mission Aasha is Daayitwa Abhiyaan’s flagship fundraising campaign, which supports and sustains these efforts by mobilizing resources and amplifying impact.

National Governance Symposium: The National Governance Symposium (NGS) is an annual event organized by Governance Lab at Daayitwa Abhiyaan, with Daayitwa as the organizing partner.

Policy and Governance Dialogues: Daayitwa has been organizing policy and governance dialogues to enhance the governance ecosystem of the country.

Job Description

The What: As the Multimedia Content Creator, you will develop engaging visual, written, and multimedia content that communicates Daayitwa’s programs, amplifies the voices of entrepreneurs and communities, supports fundraising efforts, and strengthens the organization’s digital presence.

Responsibilities:

  •  Produce high-quality video content, including entrepreneur stories, donor stewardship videos, event highlights, field documentaries, and short-form content for social media.
  •  Design engaging social media graphics, infographics, presentations, and digital communication materials.
  • Support the implementation of Mission Aasha’s digital communications and fundraising campaigns across multiple platforms.
  • Develop compelling impact stories by collaborating with entrepreneurs, community members, and program teams.
  •  Maintain a well-organized digital asset library for photos, videos, audio files, and other communication resources while ensuring proper consent and data protection.
  •  Provide creative design and layout support for reports, brochures, policy briefs, newsletters, and other organizational publications.
  • Work closely with program and field teams to identify storytelling opportunities and ensure communication products accurately reflect project outcomes.
  •  Support website content updates, basic SEO, social media scheduling, and digital campaign promotion.
  • Stay updated on digital media trends and recommend innovative approaches to enhance Daayitwa’s visibility and engagement.

Qualifications

  •  Academically compelling, with at least Bachelors (Completed or running) in Mass Communications, Public Relations, Journalism or relevant field
  •  Working knowledge of Canva, Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign and/or other design software
  • Relevant experience in multimedia and designing.
  •  Passionately driven by a strong inner calling for economic empowerment of Nepal
  • Understanding of social issues related to economic prosperity, gender equality, youth employment and community-driven development
  •  Independence in tackling complex problems consistently applying creativity, independent judgment and detail orientation
  •  Self-motivated and able to work with minimal oversight with time management skills
  •  Excellent writer and orator in Nepali and English

Additional information

Compensation: Daayitwa will provide compensation on a monthly rate basis. The rate will be mutually agreed upon, commensurate with the level of the required deliverables, the qualifications and experience of the candidate.

Application process: If you’re keen on this position, kindly complete the form below by 9th August 2026 2026. To access the page, please click on the provided link and right-click to go to the link https://forms.gle/JeGuizmwH7zuwZXRA

In the subject line, put “ Job Title followed by your first and last name” (e.g., “Multimedia Content Creator – Sabina Nepali ) and attach the following documents. All documents must be compiled in a single file, in the same order and saved in PDF format:

  •  Cover letter (one page max)
  •  CV
  • Academic transcripts/certificate for most recent qualification

Deadline: 9th August 2026. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. The vacancy may be closed prior to the deadline if a suitable candidate is found. Only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

Daayitwa is committed to promoting workforce diversity and actively encourages applications from individuals belonging to marginalized and discriminated groups, including women, Dalit, Janajati, Madhesi/Terai, and other minority communities. The organization values inclusive representation and strives to create a diverse and equitable working environment.

Position Overview:

The Sales & Marketing Manager is responsible for developing and executing sales and marketing strategies for Aloi that drive client acquisition, business growth, and brand visibility. The role combines identifying new business opportunities, establishing strategic partnerships, overseeing marketing initiatives, and ensuring the achievement of organizational sales targets, while working closely with product, operations and leadership teams.

Key Responsibilities:

Sales Strategy & Business Development

  • Develop and implement sales strategies aligned with the company’s business objectives.
  • Identify new market opportunities, customer segments, and potential partnerships.
  • Generate and qualify leads through various online and offline channels.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, financial institutions, cooperatives, enterprises, and strategic partners.
  • Lead client presentations, product demonstrations, and negotiations.
  • Prepare proposals, quotations, and commercial agreements.
  • Monitor sales performance and prepare regular sales forecasts and reports.
  • Ensure achievement of monthly, quarterly, and annual sales targets.

Marketing & Brand Management

  • Develop and execute integrated marketing campaigns to increase brand awareness and lead generation.
  • Plan and manage digital marketing activities, including social media, email marketing, website content, and paid advertising.
  • Coordinate the creation of marketing materials such as brochures, presentations, case studies, and promotional content.
  • Manage the company’s online and offline presence and ensure consistent brand messaging.
  • Analyze campaign performance and recommend improvements based on data and market insig

Required Skills and Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Management, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 3 years of professional experience in sales, marketing, business development, or a related field. Experience in banking, micro-finance or any financial institutions is preferred.
  • Experience managing strategic partnerships and corporate clients relationship.
  • Ability to conduct market research, competitor analysis, and customer segmentation to identify business opportunities.
  • Ability to develop brand positioning and ensure consistent brand messaging across all online and offline marketing channels.
  • Strong communication and negotiation skills.
  • Ability to understand complex financial products and explain them clearly to clients.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Proactive, goal-oriented, and able to work independently.
  • Familiarity with CRM software and sales tracking tools.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, technology-driven environment.

Company Benefits:

  • 5 working days (Sunday to Thursday)
  • Retirement Fund benefits in addition to the gross salary.
  • Paid leave benefits.
  • Flexible working hours.
  • Professional Training and Development opportunities.

Interested candidates are invited to submit their CV and cover letter to careers@aloi.global by 5th August 2026. Please include “Sales & Marketing Manager Application – [Your Full Name]” in the email subject line.

Kathmandu Forestry College (KAFCOL) Public Limited is a dynamic and expanding academic institution located in Chandragiri-8, Gairigaun, Kathmandu. Since its inception in 2005 the college has been offering B.Sc. Forestry program in affiliation with Tribhuvan University, Nepal. Additionally, since 2009,
it has been running a Diploma in Forestry program in collaboration with the Council for Technical Education and Vocational Training (CTEVT) of the Government of Nepal.

In 2012, KAFCOL partnered with the University of Salzburg, Austria, to jointly offer an MSc in the UNIGIS Program in Geographical Information Science and Systems (UNIGIS MSc). Furthermore, in 2015, the college launched a new M.Sc. Program in Natural Resources Management and Rural Development
(MSc in NRM-RD) in affiliation with Tribhuvan University.

KAFCOL is also actively engaged in research and outreach projects focusing on biodiversity, forestry, and natural resources management. The college was established through a joint effort by the Nepal Agroforestry Foundation, a national NGO dedicated to promoting agroforestry, and a group of forestry
and natural resource management professionals.
