Group of Helping Hands (SAHAS) Nepal is a non-profit making non-governmental-organization founded in 1996. Since then, SAHAS Nepal has been engaging in social mobilization, grassroots organisation/Community-Based Network Organisation (CBNO) formation and enhancing their capacity through partnership, and implementing diverse programme and projects in the sectors of sustainable agriculture and food security, climate change, and education in 21 districts of Nepal.

SAHAS Nepal will be implementing an education project in Solukhumbu titled “Community Mobilization for Inclusive and Quality Education in Solukhumbu District”. The aim of the project is to enhance quality and inclusive education in public schools in Solududhkunda Municipality and ThulungDudhkoshi Rural Municipality in Solukhumbu district with community mobilisation,school environment improvement, youth development, livelihood support and capacity building approaches.

SAHAS Nepal is looking the potential candidate for the following position.

Position: Monitoring and Evaluation Officer

Duty Station: Solududhkunda Municipality and Thulung Dudhkoshi Rural Municipality, Solukhumbu District

Required Number: 1

Academic qualification/experiences:

  • Bachelor’s degree in education, development studies, social science or relevant field with minimum 2 years of experience in education sector or development projects
  • Experience with data collection and analysis tools (e.g. Kobo Toolbox, Excel, SPSS)
  • Good understanding of Nepal’s education system and policies.

Major Responsibilities

  • Develop and implement a MEAL plan for the project to track performance and impact.
  • Prepare database of the project and monitor project’s progress into activities, outputs, outcomes and impact.
  • Design tools for data collection, including surveys (baseline, midline andendline surveys) and feedback mechanisms and generatereports.
  • Visit fields regularly to monitor project activities in schools and communities
  • Ensure accurate and timely data collection, analysis and reporting.
  • Support the development of Key Performance indicators (KPIs) to measure project success.
  • Document lessons learned and best practices of the project for learning, sharing and future programming in the form of case studies pictures and video documentation.
  • Prepare timely reports of the project as per funding partner’s requirements.
  • Organise capacity building on M & E tools and methodologies as per the need of the project staff.
  • Work closely with project team to ensure that impact, outcome and output level indicators are reported and monitored.

Salary and Benefits: As per the rules and regulations of SAHAS Nepal.

content.rendered:
Position: Resource Development and Program Quality Director
Location: Kusunti, KC Tower, Lalitpur, Nepal

With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Employee Contract Type:

International Assignment (WVI – Paid via GCLA) Fixed Term (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

Resource Development and Program Quality (RDPQ) Director is accountable for four major streams of work:

1) Lead the acquisitions team for all non-sponsorship funding streams, including but not limited to: grants from bilateral, multi-national, foundations, private and major donors; project-non-sponsorship, local corporate social investment (CSI), and other emerging impact investments including service contracts with development banks; in order to increase and diversify the resources of World Vision International Nepal to support country strategy goals to address the needs of the most vulnerable children and communities in Nepal;

2) Lead efforts to ensure all World Vision International Nepal’s Projects meet relevant donors’, government, and World Vision International’s technical quality and compliance requirements (including sponsorship and non-sponsorship funding); and

3) Streamlining World Vision International Nepal’s design, monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning systems contributing to innovative and improved evidence for quality improvement, policy influence, international funding acquisitions and country strategy implementation plan (CSIP)

4) Oversight of the Nepal Innovation Lab, ensuring it is bringing new thinking and innovation into Nepal and the wider region’s programs, in addition to ensuring it is adequately funded in order to operate effectively.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Leading efforts to acquire new international funding from existing and new donors. Tasks may include the following but not limited to:

  • Lead the WVI Nepal Resource Development Team, including the Grant Acquisition Manager, to build and achieve strong annual funding targets that are both ambitious and aligned with the international and national funding pipeline.
  • Proactively build multi-year funding strategy in coordination with National Director, with the goal of achieving sustainable funding for World Vision International Nepal through effective prepositioning and quality concept and proposal submission.
  • Implement WVI Nepal’s Acquisition Strategy aligned with Nepal Country Strategy and donor landscape, ensuring the broader World Vision International ecosystem including.
  • Support Offices and Regional Office are committed to supporting the delivery of the strategy
  • Ensure clear and solid internal ‘content’ review and coordination ‘process’, of all new concepts and proposals development in coordination with the Grants Acquisition Manager and cross-function team and World Vision Support Offices.
  • Ensure innovative ideas are incorporated in new concepts or projects proposals development, leveraging WVI Nepal’s Innovation Lab expertise and local and international experiences with the goal of maintaining secure funding source for the Nepal Innovation Lab.
  • Proactively lead and facilitate strategic consortium or partnership agreement with other peer local and INGOs, UN agencies and/or private contractors.
  • In coordination with the National Director, develop and oversee plan of action to position WVI Nepal in order to access local funding landscape – this may involve taking forward a suitable form of local registration.
  • Ensure all projects are aligned to the WVI Nepal country strategy and meet the relevant technical quality standards and compliance, leading team and facilitating Cross-Function collaboration with other departments, tasks may include the following but not limited to:
  • Work closely with Associate Director Program Quality to supervise and advise technical program managers/leads in designing and ensuring all WVI Nepal’s projects meet the quality standards of World Vision International, the relevant sector’s priorities of Government of Nepal, and donor’s standards outlined in project designs.
  • Ensure WVI Nepal’s technical teams remain aligned with current sector priorities, donor requirements, and development standards by actively engaging in relevant technical working groups, government forums, and peer networks; maintaining regular dialogue with sector ministries; promoting the application and sharing of key learnings across teams; and ensuring awareness of and compliance with applicable donor and organizational policies,
  • Support local capacity building and manage performance of all direct reports (GAM, MEAL, PDQ & Innovation Lab Managers), ensuring close collaboration with other WVI departments, including Operations.
  • Provide oversight to the Nepal Innovation Lab, ensuring it is effectively piloting new innovations and scaling up successful concepts in Nepal or across the partnership.
  • Collaborate with other SLT members in ensuring integration of PDQ issues.
  • Promote, engage and collaborate with WV Partnership’s PDQ and Strategy communities
  • Streamline WVI Nepal’s design, monitoring, evaluation and learning systems, contributing to improved evidence for quality improvement, policy influence and international funding acquisitions, tasks may include the following but not limited to:
  • Guide Senior MEAL Manager to ensure coherent measures and monitoring and reporting of all programs (sponsorship, PNS and grants), including alignment with CSIP, OIOS and MEAL global standards
  • Provide high level analytics to Senior Leadership Team on quality of WVI Nepal’s projects and provide technical and strategic recommendations for ongoing improvement.
  • Ensure World Vision’s local partnership approach is implemented effectively and efficiently while continuing to be adapted through best practice to the local context
  • Ensure consistency and quality of all project information from Partner NGOs level, Field Office, National Office and to all donors (internal World Vision Support Offices and external) in order to demonstrate projects impact and contributions of WVI Nepal’s to communities, the Government of Nepal, World Vision Global and donor’s priorities.
  • Ensure WVI Nepal’s relevant project information system comply and provide quality reporting to with World Vision International reporting systems, Power BI and other major systems and acts as an effective knowledge management system.
  • Provide directions, guidance, coaching and technical supports to PDQ team members and ensuring team accountability to deliver and measure the results
  • In collaboration with National Director, External Engagement and Strategy Director, Finance and Corporate Service Director, Field Operations Director and Senior MEAL Manager, support the successful implementation, review and reporting of country strategy and annual business plan, including but not limited to:
  • Co-lead with Field Operations Director in nurturing close communications and partnership with WVI Nepal’s Strategic Support Team/SST, or SOs representative for successful strategy Implementation in WVI Nepal
  • Guide Senior MEAL Manager to ensure coherent measures and monitoring of annual business plan aligned with CSIP and programs M&E
  • Support strategy and Annual Business review process in close collaboration with the National Director and External Engagement and Strategy Director
  • Ensuring World Vision’s local partnership approach is implemented effectively and efficiently while continuing to be adapted through best practice to the local context

KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE

Required Professional Experience

  • At least 7-10 years of working in the relevant leadership/managerial position in least developed/developing countries, preferably in Asia region.
  • Familiar with child-focused, multi-sectoral and integrated development programmes. Similar experiences leading and implementing multi-sector in World Vision is an advantage.
  • Proven successful experiences in coordinating and writing winning concept papers or proposals to key donors such as US Government, EU, FCDO, DFAT, GAC, MFAT, Global Fund, Nordic Governments and other donors.
  • Proven analytical skills and relevant experience in facilitating or leading programme design and evaluation, long term programmes plan and strategy development, and streamlining monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning system in an international organization.
  • Relevant experience on external engagement including with governments and donors for project initiation and maximizing the impact on child well-being.
  • Good understanding on the international needs and development trends and their relevance to Nepal’s development context.
  • Good knowledge of standards and requirement of bilateral and multi-laterals donors.
  • Project or organizational leadership experience managing medium to large team. Cross-cultural team or leadership experience is a plus.
  • Mature personality and able to manage multiple priorities.
  • Ability to manage pressures to meet tight project proposals deadlines and to maintain clarity of programmes and team focus.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English.

Required Education, training, license, registration and certification

  • Master’s degree in international development, development studies/management, project management, economics, agriculture, public health, public/social policy, social sciences or equivalent.

Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications

  • Relevant World Vision experience is a plus.
  • Work experiences in Nepal, or South Asia, or South East Asia is preferred

This is a non-accompanied international assignment. Family accompaniment is not provided for this position.

Applicant Types Accepted: Local and International Applicants (IA’s) Accepted

“World Vision is committed to achieving diversity, as the diversity of our teams is critical to our overall success. WV welcomes applications from qualified professionals all over Nepal. Women, people with disability, and members from other marginalized groups are strongly encouraged to apply.”

“Children and vulnerable adults who come into contact with WV as a result of our activities must be safeguarded to the maximum possible extent from deliberate or inadvertent actions and failings that place them at risk of abuse, sexual exploitation, injury, and any other harm. One of the ways that WVI Nepal shows this on-going commitment to safeguarding is to include rigorous background and reference checks in the selection process for all candidates, in accordance to its Child and Adult Safeguarding Policy. WVI Nepal has zero tolerance to child rights’ violations, by employees and/or affiliates.”

WVI Nepal reserves all rights to qualify/disqualify applications in any case.

  •  Monitor, and track various contracts to ensure timely payment and extensions.
  •  Provide support to monitor budget expenditure as per approved budget from UNDP Quantum system; analyse the Combined Delivery Report and provide advice as required.

  •  Undertake other financial and administrative tasks assigned by the Advancing Civic Engagement for Democratic Participation Project Manager, and UNDP Portfolio Manager.
  •  Ensure Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) considerations are incorporated in the project activities and project budget is made GESI Responsive.

Support knowledge building, knowledge sharing and capacity building relevant to the assigned project:

Published on 22 July 2026 Centre for Mental Health and Counselling–Nepal (CMC-Nepal) is a national-level non-governmental organization (NGO) dedicated to promoting mental health and psychosocial well-being. We are pleased to announce an exciting opportunity to join our team as a MEAL Officer in the Psychosocial Counselling and Community Integration for Transitional Justice (PCCITJ) project.

The PCCITJ project is funded jointly by the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC), CMC-Nepal, and Manas. Its goal is that “conflict victims improve their psychosocial well-being through equitable access to quality MHPSS service during the transitional justice process and later.” The project is being implemented in 22 rural municipalities and municipalities across Bagmati, Lumbini, Karnali, and Sudurpashchim Provinces of Nepal.

Job title: MEAL Officer

Number of positions: 1 (One)

Location: Deukhuri, Dang, Lumbini Province (with frequent field visit)

Position Overview:

The MEAL Officer is responsible for leading the Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) components of the PCCITJ project. This includes designing, coordinating, and implementing robust MEAL systems in accordance with project needs that support effective program implementation, learning, accountability, and reporting. The MEAL Officer supports data-driven decision-making for evidence-based programming. S/he maintains strong coordination with project and organizational staff, as well as relevant stakeholders at all levels. S/he works together with the MEAL Coordinator to strengthen the capacity of project staff on MEAL-related functions. The person also supports research initiatives, documentation, safeguarding integration, and financial performance tracking. A key aspect of the role is to promote learning, knowledge management, and innovation to adapt and improve project interventions. The MEAL Officer will be fully engaged (100%) in PCCITJ and will be responsible to the Program Manager.

Major duties and responsibilities

  • Lead end-to-end MEAL functions, including monitoring visits, indicator tracking, quality benchmarking, and evaluation processes.
  • Manage project data systems ensuring accuracy, security, confidentiality, and timely reporting aligned with donor and organizational requirements.
  • Establish and operationalize accountability and feedback mechanisms, integrating safeguarding and ensuring community-responsive actions.
  • Coordinate with government, TJ Commissions, NGOs/CBOs, and community structures to strengthen implementation, referrals, and advocacy.
  • Drive research, documentation, and knowledge generation including studies, case studies, learning briefs, and evidence-based reporting.
  • Build staff capacity on MEAL through training, mentoring, and promoting a culture of learning, adaptive management, and innovation.

Qualification and Experience

  • Master’s degree in Public Health, Statistics, Information Technology and Management Information Systems, Social Work, Social Sciences, Development Studies, or related fields.
  • Minimum of two years of progressive and relevant experience, preferably in health system strengthening, work with conflict victims, or community-based MHPSS projects.
  • Proficiency in MEAL frameworks, tools, and methodologies, including logical frameworks, indicator tracking, data quality assurance, and quality benchmark settings.
  • Strong knowledge of the Health Management Information System (HMIS), DHIS 2, and government monitoring mechanisms.
  • Demonstrated experience in data management, analysis, and visualization using MS Excel, SPSS, and other relevant software.

  • Support organizational reporting requirements and organizational events such as AGM, assessments, and reviews.
  • Develop at least one case story or success story each month, along with process documentation.
  • Conduct surveys and develop health profiles.
  • Ensure integrated programming and coordination across all outcomes and sectors.
  • Support proposal development and proposal-writing processes.

Required Skills and Competencies

  • Strong skills in logical framework (Logframe) development and results-based monitoring.
  • Excellent computer skills, including MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and other relevant applications.
  • Strong communication, analytical, documentation, and report-writing skills.
  • Basic proficiency in spoken and written English and Nepali.
  • Strong project management skills. on MNCH/Health & Nutrition
  • Knowledge of monitoring and evaluation, research methodologies, and documentation.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Ability to coordinate and collaborate effectively with government agencies, CSOs, and other stakeholders.
  • Experience in data analysis and reporting.
  • Knowledge of child rights, human rights, safeguarding, and SDG-related issues.
  • Excellent networking, advocacy, coordination, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet multiple deadlines.
  • Demonstrated experience in training design, curriculum development, and facilitation.
  • Experience in small-grant management, monitoring, and reporting.
  • Ability to work effectively in diverse and multicultural environments.
  • Enthusiasm for working with multidisciplinary teams and rural communities.
  • Proven track record of working with local, provincial, and federal government institutions.

Qualifications and Experience

  • Bachelor’s Degree in: BSc Nursing, PBN, (BPH with PCL Nursing/Health Assistant). Must be registered with the relevant professional council, such as NNC, NHPC, or NMC.
  • A minimum of three (3) years of relevant experience at the MNCH/Health and Nutrition Officer level with NGOs/INGOs or a minimum of two (2) years of experience in a coordinator-level position.

Helvetas is an organization specialized in development cooperation and humanitarian response, anchored in Switzerland. Our vision is a just world in which all people determine the course of their lives in dignity and security, using environmental resources in a sustainable manner.

For our Finance team based in Switzerland Head Office we are seeking a motivated and empathetic Senior Finance Officer PNP Projects, who will be based in Kathmandu, Nepal to join our organisation as per October 2026 or upon agreement. Helvetas Nepal invites applications from competent and committed Nepali Citizens for the following position: SENIOR FINANCE OFFICER 100%

YOUR MAIN TASKS

A. Financial Reporting & Compliance: Prepare accurate and timely donor budgets, financial reports and ensure full traceability of financial data. Lead financial closings and ensure audit readiness. Support PNP team on donor compliance and financial requirements.

B. Controlling & Monitoring: Develop and maintain Management Information System (MIS) for PNP projects portfolio. Monitor project financial performance, analyze deviations, and support corrective actions. Contribute to forecasts and budget revisions. Act as partner to PNP team, support and provide analysis and guidance.

C. Systems & Process Improvement: Ensure high-quality financial data and support optimization of finance systems and processes. Contribute to standardization of reports and tools. Develop and maintain practical finance guidelines, process flows and templates.

D. Audit & Coordination: Coordinate audits and follow up on findings. Collaborate across teams and act as finance focal point for internal and external stakeholders. Support capacity building and knowledge sharing across countries about PNP portfolio.

Required Education and Experience:

  • Minimum bachelor’s degree in business administration and/or finance, Master’s degree is an advantage for this position.
  • 8+ years of experience in finance in a Controlling / Management Accounting / analytical role incl.
  • Experience of 3-5 years with donor-funded projects in the international development / NGO context is required.
  • High proficiency with ERP, Finance systems and accounting software. Advanced Excel skills.
  • Good working knowledge of Power BI and/or other multidimensional data tools.
  • Fluency in written and spoken English. Strong analytical skills combined with a solution-oriented work approach.
  • A result-oriented mindset and willingness to take on responsibility for sub-processes. A structured mind-set and an autonomous working approach.

Duty station: Kathmandu, Nepal

Duration: Initially three years with a possibility of extension.

Salary and Benefits: As per rules and regulations of Helvetas Nepal.

UWS Nepal is a charity organisation dedicated to improving educational opportunities for underprivileged children. We started operations in 2015 as a non-profit, the same year our country witnessed a 7.8 magnitude earthquake. Post-earthquake UWS Nepal has constructed 636 earthquake-resistant classrooms across 321 communities, educating 20,690 students in our Sankhuwasabha, Gulmi, Bhojpur, Taplejung and Tanahun districts. We aim to provide quality education to all children, and to reach that goal; we work to improve educational opportunities for children living in marginalised communities and remote regions. Our education transformation philosophy is maintained by developing and introducing child-friendly pedagogies that allow for more significant innovation in the classroom and greater engagement between the in-class lessons and real life, parents-teacher relationship, and harmonised relationship between local government and local communities in a shared mission to ensure a future for children in the communities where we work. Our vision is Zero Education Poverty.

Details / requirements:

Posiiton: Senior Global MEAL Associate

Location: Kathmandu, Nepal or Antananarivo/Toliara, Madagascar

Help us turn data into insight, and insight into impact.

This is an exciting time to join UWS.

As we roll out our ambitious 2030 Programme Strategy, we’re strengthening how we measure and demonstrate impact across Cambodia, Madagascar, Myanmar and Nepal. Our MEAL team ensures high-quality data drives learning, decision-making and programme improvement.

We’re looking for a talented and driven Senior Global MEAL Associate to join our global team and help advance our monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning systems.

About the role

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who loves working with data and wants to use their skills to create meaningful change.

Working with colleagues across four countries, you’ll strengthen data systems, improve data quality, analyse performance and develop clear dashboards, visualisations and reports that help turn evidence into action.

Data collection platforms, analysis, data visualisation and reporting are at the core of this role. We’re looking for someone who can turn complex data into clear, accessible insights that support better decisions.

We’re looking for someone with:

  • Strong skills in data analysis, reporting and visualisation.
  • Confidence using tools such as Excel, Power BI and data collection platforms.
  • The ability to turn complex data into clear, practical insights.
  • A collaborative, organised and detail-oriented approach.
  • A commitment to evidence-led programmes that create meaningful change.

Why join UWS?

You’ll join a supportive global team working towards Zero Education Poverty, helping shape how UWS measures and demonstrates impact across our programmes.

Most importantly, your work will directly contribute to improving programmes and expanding educational opportunities for children in some of the world’s most marginalised communities.

How to apply

Please submit:

Your CV
A cover letter (maximum two pages) outlining your suitability for the role

We also encourage candidates to share an example of previous work showing their skills in data analysis, reporting or data visualisation, such as a dashboard, report extract, slide or anonymised sample.
